metadata.schemeName: Jute Diversification Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to set up production centres to promote eco-friendly jute products and generate sustained employment. It provides skill training, machine subsidies, and financial incentives to collaborating agencies, targeting artisans, women self-help groups, and entrepreneurs.

page_content:
# Jute Diversification Scheme **Ministry:** Ministry Of Textiles | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Artisan, Entrepreneur, Training, Employment, Subsidy, Equipment, Incentive | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme "Jute Diversification Scheme" was launched by the National Jute Board, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India. The scheme aims to spread jute diversification programs, provide training, and create sustained employment by setting up Jute Resource-cum-Production Centres across the country. The scheme provides basic, advanced, and design training in jute diversified products manufacturing, financial incentives for collaborating agencies, and subsidies for procuring machinery. The applicant must be a registered agency or entrepreneur with at least three years of experience in product identification, bulk production, skill training, and marketing of jute diversified products. The scheme is implemented by the National Jute Board. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through the official website, followed by a hard copy submission.
## Benefits ##### ***Financial Assistance for Activities*** - The scheme provides an estimated cost of ₹12,40,000/- for organizing 5 cycles of basic, advance, and design training for 24 beneficiaries per cycle. - Incentive for Collaborating Agencies: The agency receives ₹2,48,000/- (calculated as 20% of the activity cost) for organizing the activities and maintaining the infrastructure. ##### ***Infrastructure Support*** The scheme provides ₹12,000/- for the installation of a biometric machine, internet connectivity, and maintenance. ##### ***Machinery Subsidy*** The scheme offers ₹9,00,000/- per year per centre to procure 72 machines (at 50% subsidy or a maximum ceiling of ₹12,500/- per machine, whichever is less) for successful beneficiaries engaged in production. ##### ***Disbursal*** - 50% of the activities cost is released as an advance along with the approval of the action plan. - The remaining 50% of the activities cost, the cost of the biometric machine, and the incentive are released upon successful completion of the activities and submission of final claims and reports. - The machine subsidy is released in two installments, where 50% is released within one month of installation, and the remaining 50% is released after six months upon inspection certifying that the beneficiaries are engaged in manufacturing and sales. - The payments of such incentives are paid strictly through Direct Bank Transfer. ##### ***Conditions*** - The collaborating agency must ensure the engagement of at least 50% of the trainees in jute diversification activities post-training. - In the case of self-employment, the beneficiary must achieve sales of at least ₹5,000/- per month or ₹15,000/- per quarter. - The agency must maintain a separate bank account for all advances and limit cash transactions to a maximum of ₹5,000/- per activity. - The installation of an Aadhaar linked biometric attendance machine and a webcam is mandatory at the training site.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a bonafide Indian agency or an Indian citizen. - The applicant must be a reputed registered jute entrepreneur, manufacturer, exporter, merchant trader, non-governmental organization, cooperative society, federation, public sector undertaking, or organization. - The applicant must be engaged in the product identification, bulk production, skill trainings, and marketing of jute diversified products for at least the last three years. - The applicant should possess recognized experience in the training, promotion, and development of Women Self Help Groups in the field of production and marketing of jute diversified products, handlooms, or handicrafts. - The applicant must have their own office of at least 250 sq.ft. equipped with a telephone or mobile connection, a computer or laptop, and email facilities. - The applicant must have at least 500 sq.ft. of space available for setting up the Jute Resource-Cum-Production Centre. - The applicant must obtain a minimum of 50 marks in the evaluation criteria to be eligible for consideration for selection.
##### ***Preference*** Preference is given to recognized agencies with at least three years of experience in training, promotion, and development of Women Self Help Groups in the handloom, handicrafts, and textiles sector. ##### ***Earmarking/Reservation*** At least 70% of the training beneficiaries must be individual women or women belonging to Women Self Help Groups. ##### ***Relaxation*** If an entrepreneur collaborates with the purpose of converting the centre into a full-fledged manufacturing unit by employing at least 50% of its trainees, the condition of training over 70% women will not be applicable. ##### ***Post-Selection Conditions*** - The applicant must sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Jute Board. - The applicant must submit an annual action plan supported by a list of confirmed bonafide trainees. - The applicant must submit a bank guarantee equivalent to 50% of the activities cost of the approved cycles. - The applicant must set up the centre by procuring and installing new branded machineries within one month from the date of the in-principle approval.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online ##### **Step 1:****** ***Accessing the Portal*** The applicant must access the [official website](https://www.jute.com) of the National Jute Board to begin the application procedure. The application must be initiated through the designated online portal. ##### **Step 2:****** ***Filling the Online Proposal*** The applicant must complete the online application by filling in all the relevant details, including agency profile, infrastructure facilities, past experience in jute diversified products, and proposed action plans. All requested information must be accurately entered into the online system to generate an acknowledgement. ##### **Step 3:****** ***Submitting the Hard Copies*** After successfully submitting the online proposal, the applicant must print the online acknowledgement. The printed acknowledgement, accompanied by a covering letter on the official letterhead of the company, must be prepared for offline submission. ##### **Step 4:****** ***Physical Document Dispatch*** The applicant must compile all the prescribed supporting documents and attach them to the printed acknowledgement. This complete application package must be submitted physically to the Head Office or the respective Regional Office of the National Jute Board, depending on the jurisdiction of the proposed centre. ##### **Step 5:****** ***Evaluation and Selection*** The submitted proposals will be scrutinized and evaluated by a Sub-Committee based on predefined criteria such as agency experience, proximity of location, and infrastructure. Agencies scoring a minimum of 50 marks will be shortlisted and recommended to the Monitoring Committee for final approval and selection.
##### ***Grievance Redressal / Help & Support*** Email: jute@njbindia.in. Fax: (033) - 2217 2456. Address: National Jute Board, 3A & 3B, Park Plaza, 71, Park Street, Kolkata 700 016.

page_content:
# PM POSHAN - Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme For Holistic Nourishment **Ministry:** Ministry of Education | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Health & Wellness, Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** School, Children, Health, Govt Scheme, Nutrition India | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description PM POSHAN is a centrally sponsored scheme by the Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education. Under this scheme, one hot cooked meal will be provided to the children studying in Government and Government – aided schools. The Scheme is implemented across the country covering all the eligible children without any discrimination of gender and social class.
The main objectives of the PM POSHAN Abhiyaan are to address two of the pressing problems for the majority of children in India, viz. hunger and education by improving the nutritional status of eligible children in Government and Government-aided schools as well as encouraging poor children, belonging to disadvantaged sections, to attend school more regularly and help them concentrate on classroom activities.
POSHAN Abhiyaan is one of the many schemes under the umbrella scheme "Integrated Child Development Services Scheme (ICDS)". ICDS also includes Anganwadi Services Scheme, Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana, and Scheme for Adolescent Girls. ## Benefits **Nutrition norm per child per day:** 1. Primary: Calorie – 450; Protein - 12 gms 1. Upper Primary: Calorie – 700; Protein - 20 gms
**Food norms per child per day:** 1. Primary: Food grains - 100 gms; Pulses - 20 gms; Vegetables - 50 gms; Oil & fat - 5 gms, Salt & condiments - As per need. 1. Upper Primary: Food grains - 150 gms; Pulses - 30 gms; Vegetables - 75 gms; Oil & fat – 7.5 gms, Salt & condiments - As per need.
Under the Scheme, there is the provision of hot cooked meals to children of pre-schools or Bal Vatika (before class I) in primary schools also in addition to the 11.80 crore children of classes I to VIII studying in 11.20 lakh schools. ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must be a citizen of India. 1. The applicant must be studying in a Primary or Upper Primary class (Class 1st to Class 8th) in a Government or a Government-aided school. ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline There is no application process for this scheme. PM POSHAN is equally applicable to all children who are studying in Government and Government – aided schools.

metadata.schemeName: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The “Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme (BIG)” is a flagship scheme of BIRAC which recognizes and invests in innovative ideas in the biotech sector. BIG scheme supports individual entrepreneurs/ start-ups from ideation to Proof of Concept.

page_content:
# Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme

**Ministry:** Ministry Of Science And Technology | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Biotechnology, Ignition Grant, BIRAC, BIG, Entrepreneur, Start-up | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual

## Description
The “Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme (BIG)” is a flagship scheme of the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), (a not-for-profit Section 8, Schedule B, Public Sector Enterprise, set up by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India), which recognizes and invests in innovative ideas in the biotech sector. The ideas should have clear potential to translate into commercial products/technologies. BIG supports individual entrepreneurs/ start-ups from ideation to Proof of Concept (PoC).
> **Purpose of the BIG scheme:**


  - Supports ideation to Proof of Concept
  - Nurtures entrepreneurship to enable translation of ideas into commercially viable products/ technologies to address unmet need
  - Enables Biotech Startup Ecosystem in the country to become globally competitive

> **Types of projects supported:**

BIG scheme supports innovation under Healthcare, Lifesciences, Diagnostics, Medical Devices, Drugs, Vaccines, Drug Formulations and delivery systems, Industrial Biotechnology, Agriculture, Secondary agriculture, Waste Management, Sanitation, Clean Energy, and related areas.
**The project proposals can be submitted in any of the following seven categories:**

  - Devices & Diagnostics
  - Drugs including drug delivery
  - Industrial Biotechnology including Secondary Agriculture
  - Agriculture
  - Biosimilars & Stem Cells
  - Vaccines
  - Bioinformatics & facilities

BIRAC encourages proposals involving integration of Biotech with applied sciences that may include Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, Sensors, Big Data Analytics, Cloud Computing, Machine Learning, Automation, Robotics, and related disciplines to potentially facilitate transforming healthcare, life sciences, agriculture, secondary agriculture, and other bio-based industry/ markets.
> **Types of projects not supported:**


  - Basic/exploratory research projects
  - Projects having a low element of novelty
  - Projects involving systematic clinical trials, field trials or late-stage validation/certification of the technology.

**Note:** BIG grant is not a research fellowship and cannot be used to support PhD or any other academic research.
> **Project Duration:**

The funding is provided for a period of up to 18 months. The project is implemented in a milestone-based manner.

## Benefits
Support provided to grantees under the scheme:
1. Under the BIG scheme, BIRAC provides a grant-in-aid of up to INR 50 lakhs (approx. USD 75,000) for a period of 18 months.
2. BIG Partners and BIRAC provide continuous mentoring support to the grantees, including but not limited to the following:
• Technical Mentoring (Connect with Technical Experts)
• IP Support
• Legal Support
• Networking and Outreach
• Trainings
• Regulatory Advice
• Business Mentoring
• Connect with Investors
• Any other assistance on a case basis

## Eligibility Criteria
> **Eligibility criteria for an Individual:**

1.	The individual applicant should be an Indian citizen.
2.	The primary applicant should be the Project Leader.
3.	The applicant has to be incubated in an incubator (Incubator could be located anywhere in the country and may/may not be supported by BIRAC). At the time of application, the applicant is expected to have identified a preferred incubator. LoI/MoU with the incubator is required for final approval.
4.	If the applicant is formally employed (or registered as a student) with an academic or research organization, then
•	the applicant has to produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the competent authority of the organization indicating that the organization has policies in place to allow the applicant while in service/ on sabbatical/on Extraordinary Leave:
•	accept funding support (if successful) as an individual,
•	manage the funds through a separate no-lien account in individual capacity
•	undertake the BIG project in an incubator
•	to create an enterprise.
•	Alternatively, the applicant needs to provide an undertaking that he/she plans to terminate his/her association with the current employer and take up the project full-time in the event of grant approval. A resignation/ relieving/ retirement letter will be needed as a supporting document before final approval and release of the grant.
5.	If the applicant is formally employed with a for-profit company/LLP,
•	the applicant needs to provide an undertaking that he/she plans to terminate his/her association with the current employer and take up the project full-time in the event of grant approval (A resignation/ relieving/retirement letter will be needed as supporting document before final approval and release of the grant.), or,
•	Alternatively, the application should be submitted under the Company/LLP category.
6.	An individual who is a promoter shareholder of a Biotech company or one of the partners in a Biotech LLP will not be allowed to apply as an individual, irrespective of the percentage of shareholding of the applicant in the company. (In such a case, the application can be submitted through the company/LLP route, in case the company/LLP meets the required eligibility criteria as detailed below).
> **Eligibility criteria for Company/ LLP:**


   1. The Company/LLP should be registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1956/2013.
   1. The incorporation date of the Company/LLP should not be earlier than 5 years from the date of closing of a particular BIG call.
   1. A company is considered as 'owned’ by resident Indian citizen(s) if minimum 51% of the capital is beneficially owned by resident Indian citizen(s) and/or Indian companies, which are ultimately owned and controlled by resident Indian citizens.
   1. Company/LLP’s application should be represented by a Project Leader.
   1. The Company/LLP must have its own in-house R&D facility that is functional and adequate to execute the project. If the Company/LLP does not have a functional and adequate laboratory of its own then it should be incubated at an incubator (This shall be verified and confirmed by BIG Partner ),
   1. If an applicant company, in which any promoter holding more than or equal to 20% of the shares, is a co-promoter of another ineligible company or a partner in another ineligible LLP, then the applicant will not be eligible. The only exception to this shall be a situation wherein the latter ineligible company/LLP is operating in a non-biotech domain. In case the applicant is an LLP: An applicant LLP, in which any of the partners is also a partner in another ineligible LLP or is a co-promoter in another ineligible company, then the applicant will not be eligible. The only exception to this shall be a situation wherein the latter ineligible LLP/company is operating in a non-biotech domain.

**Note 01:** Every proposal must clearly identify a Project Leader who will take responsibility for the technical and managerial aspects of the project execution.
**Note 02:** The Project Leader must be technically qualified to undertake the project. The Project Leader must have completed basic undergraduate training in any discipline.
**Note 03:** In the event that the proposal is shortlisted for presentation in front of the Selection Committee(s), the Project Leader will be required to present the case for support. In the event that a proposal is shortlisted for funding support, the Project Leader will be required to sign the project agreement.
**Note 04:** The project Leader must be a shareholder in the applicant company.
**Note 05:** The proposed objectives and deliverables should not have received funding support from any other agency.
**Note 06:** BIG support can be provided only once to any individual/startup.
**Note 07:** Biotech Start-ups and Individual Entrepreneurs with innovative ideas having potential for commercialization are eligible to apply.
**Note 08:** Scientists, Faculty, Research Scholars, and Graduates in any discipline incubating/ intend to incubate at a Bio Incubator.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Online
> **Application process:**

**Step 01:** BIRAC issues a national call inviting applications under BIG at least twice a year (1st of January & 1st of July). The Call for Proposals is advertised through one or more means that may include the BIRAC website, newspapers, journals, and magazines. The Call for Proposals is typically open for a period of up to one and a half months.
**Step 02:** Application for BIG needs to be submitted online ONLY through the BIRAC website [www.birac.nic.in](https://birac.nic.in/login.php).
**Step 03:** For proposal submission, the applicant can register on the BIRAC website under “BIG User”. 
**Step 04:** The eligible applicants can fill up and submit their applications by visiting the official website.
**Note 01:** The BIG Scheme is implemented across the country through BIRAC’s BIG Partners. The Call will mention the names of BIG Partners for the particular call. Names of the BIG Partners and their responsibilities are mentioned in Annexure 2.
**Note 02:** Applicants are advised to provide sufficient details in their applications to allow for an informed and fair evaluation/review.
**Note 03:** Requests for changes in a proposal once submitted will not be entertained.
**Note 04:** Providing incorrect information intentionally is viewed adversely and may lead to disqualification.
> **Selection process:**

BIG selection is a multi-tier process involving the following steps:
**Step 01:** Eligibility Check: BIG Partners screen the applications for eligibility requirements as laid out in the scheme document and appropriateness under the BIG scheme.
**Step 02:** Examination by Preliminary Selection Committee (PSC): The PSC examines all eligible proposals on the following contours:
•	Scheme fit
•	Availability of adequate technical details which are minimally required for online review
•	Plagiarism
**Step 03:** Online review by subject matter experts: Proposals recommended by PSC are reviewed online by 3 or more subject matter experts.
**Step 04:** Presentation before Thematic Technical Expert Panel (TEP): Based on expert reviews, shortlisted applications are called for a Face-to-face presentation before the Technical Expert Panel (TEP). The TEPs are conducted in a thematic manner where all proposals of a particular theme are evaluated together by a common committee. All proposals are scored by individual TEP Experts and the Geometric Mean of Individual Scores is used to arrive at the final score for a particular proposal.
•	Proposals with score ≥60 are considered at the next step (ESC)
•	Proposals with score <60 are not considered further
**Step 05:** Scoring Cut-off decision by the Expert Selection Committee (ESC): ESC takes the final decision with regard to the cut-off score for final selection. Proposals above the decided cut-off will be considered for further due diligence. ESC may choose to have either the same or differential scoring cut off across the themes.
**Step 06:** ESC-recommended applications are then subjected to final financial and technical due diligence by the BIG Partner. This may require a visit by BIG partner representative(s) to the applicant’s site and involves the following steps:
•	Reconfirming eligibility by verification of original documents
•	Legal, technical, and financial due diligence
• Confirming applicant’s claimed resources: Space, equipment, manpower, advisors, incubation services, samples, etc.
•	Confirming compliance strategy with regard to safety, ethics, waste disposal, etc.
•	Confirming for any special guidance by ESC
•	Justification of budget (usually by verifying quotations); meeting budget caps and other requirements
•	Finalization of milestones, budget, and payment schedule; defining clear measurable milestones.
> **Indicative evaluation criteria:** BIG Proposals are reviewed on the following parameters during online review and TEP Stage:

1.	Unmet Need (max 20)
2.	Value Proposition/Differentiation (max 20)
3.	Technical Viability (max 30)
4.	Team Strength/Passion (max 15)
5.	Business Perspective (max 15)
•	Potential
•	Clarity/Team’s view
•	Commercialization Potential (Yes/No)
[Registration guidelines for BIG Scheme(Company/Individual)](https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/1547451412_big_registration_guidelines_14_01_2019.pdf)

metadata.schemeName: Marketing Development Assistance Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The Marketing Development Assistance (MDA) Scheme under the Overseas Promotion & Publicity (OPP) Scheme aims to support the promotion and marketing of Indian tourism in overseas markets.

page_content:
# Marketing Development Assistance Scheme **Ministry:** Ministry Of Tourism | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Travel & Tourism, Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Tourism, Financial Assistance, Promotion, Operators, International | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The Ministry of Tourism launched the Marketing Development Assistance (MDA) Scheme under the Overseas Promotion & Publicity (OPP) Scheme. The scheme aims to provide financial support to tourism service providers approved by the Ministry of Tourism, Govt. of India or the respective State Government / Union Territory (UT) Administration for undertaking promotion and marketing of India in the overseas markets.
> **Objectives****:** - To motivate stakeholders to promote tourism to the country from the overseas markets. - To enhance the visibility of the brand Incredible India in the overseas markets. - To augment foreign tourist arrivals to the country.
## Benefits **For Tourism Service Providers** Financial support for study tours, and participation in travel shows/exhibitions/road shows in overseas markets (organized by the Ministry of Tourism) will be provided up to a maximum of ₹3,50,000/- per case/tour. **Sr. No.** **Particulars** **Extent of Support** 1Economy class airfare for travel between India to another country and from there to a group of countries by air/rail.90%2Cost of built-up/furnished stall, electricity and water charges, participation fee, etc., at travel fair/exhibitions held overseas.90%3Lodging expenses on overseas tour Max. 5 nights with an upper ceiling of room rate at ₹10,000/- per night.
**For Tourism Departments of State Governments / UT Administrations** Financial support for participation in overseas travel shows and exhibitions will be provided as follows: **Sr. No.** **Particulars** **Extent of Support**1. Cost of built-up/furnished stall, electricity and water charges, participation fee, etc., at travel fair/exhibitions held overseas.Overall ceiling of ₹3,50,000/-. 2. Since, the representatives of State Govts and UTs are provided TA/DA by the States/UTs, the provisions of financial assistance towards international air fare and lodging are not applicable to them.
**For Tourism Service Providers /Tourism Departments of State Governments / UT Administrations** Financial support for online promotion of tourism destinations and products in overseas markets, including digital content creation, will cover 50% of the total cost, up to ₹1,00,000/- per financial year, subject to actuals. ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The tourism service providers should be travel agents, inbound tour operators, tourist transport operators, classified hotels, classified bed & breakfast units, classified home stays, classified motels, guest houses & tented accommodation units, standalone restaurants, convention centers, and online aggregators, sales tours, participation in travel fairs/exhibitions and road shows (organized by Ministry of Tourism), online promotion of tourism destinations and products, tour packages in the overseas markets, including content creation/production of digital promotional brochures/leaflets etc. 1. The tourism service providers should be approved by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, or the concerned State / Union Territory Tourism Department. 1. The approved tourism service providers should show a minimum fee of ₹1.00 crore – ₹2.00 crore in any of the preceding two years i.e. 2018-19 or 2019-20, the number of tours may be limited to a maximum of two in one financial year. 1. The approved tourism service providers should show a minimum fee of ₹2.00 crore and above in one of the preceding two years i.e. 2018-19 or 2019-20, the number of tours may be limited to a maximum of three in one financial year. 1. Tourism departments of State Governments / UT Administrations are also eligible to avail benefits under the Scheme. However, the above eligibility conditions do not apply to them.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Prior Approval:** **Step 01:** The TSP/SG/UT shall obtain Prior Approval from the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, before undertaking a tour overseas. **Step 02:** The applicants download the prior approval application form [Annexure-I](https://tourism.gov.in/sites/default/files/2022-03/Revised%20MDA%20Guidelines%2010032022.pdf). **Step 03:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required). **Step 04:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form at least 21 days before the tour to the Assistant Director General (Overseas Marketing) via email at mda-tourism@gov.in.
> **Reimbursement Claims:** After undertaking the tourism promotional activity/tour abroad for which Prior Approval had been accorded by the Ministry of Tourism the Tourism Service Provider / State Govt./ UT Administration will apply to reimbursement/claim. **Step 01:** The applicants download the claim application form [Annexure-II, III & IV](https://tourism.gov.in/sites/default/files/2022-03/Revised%20MDA%20Guidelines%2010032022.pdf). **Step 02:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required). **Step 03:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form within 45 days of completion of the activity to the Assistant Director General (Overseas Marketing), Ministry of Tourism via email at mda-tourism@gov.in.
**NOTE:** Submission of claims in physical form will not be accepted.

metadata.schemeName: Innovation In Science Pursuit For Inspired Research (INSPIRE) - Fellowship
metadata.briefDescription: INSPIRE Fellowship is one of the components of INSPIRE scheme implemented by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India to strengthen the Science and Technology base of the country. This Component focuses on attracting students to pursue doctoral degree.

page_content:
# Innovation In Science Pursuit For Inspired Research (INSPIRE) - Fellowship **Ministry:** Ministry Of Science And Technology | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Fellowship, Science, University, Doctoral | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description INSPIRE Fellowship is one of the components of INSPIRE scheme implemented by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India to strengthen the Science and Technology base of the country. This Component focuses on attracting students to pursue doctoral degrees in basic and applied sciences including engineering, medicine, agriculture, veterinary, pharmacy, etc. after either master’s degree in science/engineering or a bachelor/ master’s degree in Medicine. ## Benefits > **Duration** The fellowship shall be tenable for a maximum period of five years from INSPIRE Fellowship “Effective Date” or completion of the Ph.D. program (i.e. up to the date of successful Ph.D. viva-voce), whichever is earlier.
> **HRA** HRA to the Fellows shall also be applicable as per GoI norms depending upon the location of the Host Institute.
> **Contingency Expenditure** Expenditure of contingency grant would be governed as per host institution norms. The limit of the contingency grant is ₹20,000/annum. The unspent balance of the contingency grant at the end of a year shall be adjusted to the next year with a maximum ceiling of ₹ 20,000.
> **Internship** INSPIRE Fellow shall be allowed for availing of a short-term Research Internship at any national or international Laboratory/ University/ Institute up to a maximum period of 18 months either in one or multiple slots during 5 years tenure of Fellowship.
> **Upgradation of Fellowship from JRF to SRF** The up-gradation of Fellowship from Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) to Senior Research Fellowship (SRF) would normally be considered after the completion of two (2) years of INSPIRE Fellowship. However, it can be considered after completion of one year as JRF if INSPIRE Fellow has an acceptance of at least one research paper (as a 1st Author) in any international peer-reviewed journal from the Ph.D. work carried out at the respective Host Institute.
> **Mode and Cycle of Payment** The fellowship grant shall be transferred through PFMS to the student’s host institute’s ZBSA Bank Account in the Bank of Maharashtra following CNA (Central Nodal Agency) Model. Host the institute shall transfer monthly fellowship to students’ bank accounts following the host institute norms. ## Eligibility Criteria 1. 1st Rank Holders in any recognized University and academic Institutions (Excluding Autonomous Colleges) in India in Post-Graduate (PG) level examination in Basic/Applied Sciences including Engineering, Pharmacy, Agricultural Sciences, and Veterinary Sciences. 1. 1st Rank Holders at the Graduate/Post-graduate Level Examination in Medicine only conducted by a University/ Institution in India. 1. 1st Rank should be obtained in university in basic/applied science subject course/program having a batch size of a minimum of 07 students with a minimum aggregate of 70% marks (or CGPA equivalent) for the entire course/ program.
**OR**
1. INSPIRE Scholars who have secured a minimum of 70% marks (or CGPA equivalent) in aggregate at M.Sc. integrated M.S. / M.Sc.
**Note 1:** Merely fulfilling the eligibility criteria for the INSPIRE Fellowship will not guarantee the final offer of fellowship. **Note 2:** Subject Expert Committee (SEC) will finally recommend the applications for the award of INSPIRE Fellowship considering the academic merit, research proposal, supervisor’s research credentials and host institution, etc. parameters on a competitive basis. **Note 3:** This Fellowship shall be available only for pursuing a full-time Ph.D. program in any recognized University / Institution/ R&D Laboratory in the country.
> **Post-Selection Eligibility Criteria for Continuation of the Fellowship** 1. Keep DST updated regarding the Research progress made during fellowship tenure. 1. INSPIRE Fellow shall not take any paid or unpaid assignment other than related to his/her approved research program. However, if required, the fellow may assist the host institute in its academic activities as per Ph.D. program guidelines governed by the Host Institution, provided such assignments shall not hamper the progress of the research work of the fellow. 1. Once the INSPIRE Fellow joins the Fellowship, he/she shall complete the research work within the 5 years tenure of the fellowship to achieve the approved objectives of the research problem. 1. The INSPIRE Fellow must acknowledge the support provided by DST in all the publication(s)/patent(s) and Ph.D. Thesis. 1. Soft copy of the Ph.D. thesis published research papers and patent details if any shall be submitted in a USB storage device to the INSPIRE Programme Division of DST by speed post. 1. DST needs to be informed about any disciplinary action taken by the University against INSPIRE Fellow. ## Exclusions 1. Students who are 1st Rank Holders in College including Autonomous College Examination, and 1. Students who have obtained degree(s) through Distance Education Mode, and 1. Students who are 1st Rank Holder in any specialization at M.Sc. 2nd year/last year. 1. Students who are availing multiple (more than one) fellowships concurrently from different sources.
> **Termination or Discontinuation of INSPIRE Fellowship** 1. Non-acceptance of Final Offer within 30 days from the date of issue of Final Offer. 1. Upon successful completion of Ph.D. viva-voce or 5 years of INSPIRE Fellowship tenure, whichever is earlier; 1. Resignation from the Fellowship before awarding a Ph.D. degree based on the Research Supervisor’s recommendation and upon acceptance of resignation by DST as per the terms and conditions detailed in point 7 above. 1. Change of host institution without prior approval of DST. 1. In case, INSPIRE Fellow is found ineligible at any stage including submission of incorrect information / document(s) / application, any unintentional computer error or printer’s devil, etc. 1. In case of termination of fellowship on the unethical ground(s) INSPIRE Fellow is liable to refund the completely released INSPIRE Fellowship grant along with interest. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Official Portal/Link:** https://www.online-inspire.gov.in/ > **Call for INSPIRE Fellowship Applications** Call for INSPIRE Fellowship applications is announced during 3 rd/4th quarter of each financial year. Applications are sought from the eligible students through the given below INSPIRE Web-portal: https://www.online-inspire.gov.in
One can apply for the INSPIRE Fellowship, online mode, only against the call. To apply online, please visit the link https://www.online-inspire.gov.in and follow the guidelines as given:
**Step 1:** Log in to the portal by entering the username (registered Email ID) and password. **Step 2:** A screen will appear where you have to click the ‘Fellowship’ link. **Step 3:** After clicking on the ‘Fellowship’ link, please click the button ‘Apply for Fellowship’. **Step 4:** Fill in the mandatory fields of the following section by clicking the 'EDIT' button: Personal Particulars, Contact Details, Educational Qualification (from class 12th standard onwards), Eligibility Criteria, Enrolment in Ph.D., Current Employment details. **Step 5:** Check the Declaration Button. Enter Place, Date, and Verification Code (CAPTCHA). **Step 6:** Click 'Submit'. Once you click the SUBMIT Button, a page will appear mentioning that your application has been submitted successfully. A reference number will also be mentioned which shall be used for any communication.
**Note 1:** Please SAVE your filled details before proceeding to the next section. **Note 2:** Fields marked * are mandatory.
**IMPORTANT:** Please note that you cannot Edit/Modify your application once you click SUBMIT Button. Please ensure that all the particulars you have provided are correct. You can click the 'PRINT PREVIEW' button to view the details entered.
> **Check Application Status** 1. One can view the status of the application by entering the Application Reference Number in the portal. 1. All applicants selected for the INSPIRE Fellowship shall be informed by an Email notification sent to the registered Email ID.
**Online Selection Process** 1. Two-tier selection process i.e. screening of eligible applications by an Internal Committee, followed by final selection through an Expert Committee. However, the selection process will be expected to complete within 6 months from the last date of submission of the application/requisite documents. 1. The result (provisional/final offer/Rejection) of the selection process will be communicated to individually selected candidates through an online web portal (www.online-inspire.gov.in) only. The result shall be uploaded on the respective applicant’s INSPIRE web-portal account only.

# Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: \Small Cardamom Replanting/New Planting: Karnataka (Ha.) and other States **Ministry:** Ministry Of Commerce And Industry | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment, Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Replanting, Plant, Agriculture, Planting | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Under the “Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom” implemented by the Spices Board India during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26), assistance is provided for Small Cardamom Replanting/New Planting in Karnataka and other states to motivate growers to improve production and productivity through systematic replanting of diseased, old, and senile plantations, as well as to promote area expansion, in accordance with the modalities and scheme guidelines approved by the Competent Authority.
## Benefits 1. 33.33% of cost of cultivation of subject to a maximum of ₹75,000/- per Ha for General Category and 75% of cost of cultivation ₹1,68,000/- per Ha for SC/ST payable in two annual installments of ₹37,500/- and 84,000/- each year respectively. 1. Individual registered cardamom growers having a land holding size of 0.10 Ha to 8 Ha. 1. Minimum area to be replanted under the programme is 0.10 Ha in a continuous block and the maximum area is limited to 2 Ha per beneficiary per year and a maximum of 8 Ha. in block year of 5 years from 2021-2026.The plant population is minimum 3000 Nos. per ha for closer planting [pure crop] and 1500 Nos in intercropped plantations. 1. Replanting cycle is considered as 8 years and a second time benefit for the same area replanted by a beneficiary will be available only on completion of 8 years except on exclusive circumstances like natural calamities, devastating pest and disease attacks as jointly certified by a committee constituted by Board.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicants from Karnataka and other states having potential areas suitable for Small Cardamom cultivation are eligible to apply under the scheme. 1. The applicants undertaking replanting/new planting as a pure crop using suckers will be given preference, subject to final inspection and recommendation by the designated officials.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Registration** Step 1: The applicant should visit the [ServicesPlus](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/) website. Step 3: Select the relevant service/scheme name. Step 4: Fill in the required details in the application form. Step 5: Submit the application.

metadata.schemeName: Biotechnology Research Innovation And Entrepreneurship Development (Bio-RIDE)
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to foster innovation, promote bio-entrepreneurship, and strengthen India's position as a global leader in biomanufacturing and biotechnology. It provides seed funding, extramural grants, and infrastructure support to startups, enterprises, industries, and academia.

page_content:
# Biotechnology Research Innovation And Entrepreneurship Development (Bio-RIDE) **Ministry:** Ministry Of Science And Technology | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Science, IT & Communications, Education & Learning | **Tags:** Institution, Research, Grant, Incubation, Mentorship, Innovation, Entrepreneurship | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme "Biotechnology Research Innovation And Entrepreneurship Development (Bio-RIDE)" was launched by the Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology. The scheme aims to propel the nation toward sustainable green growth and a robust bioeconomy. The scheme provides comprehensive support including seed funding, incubation support, extramural research grants, and substantial financial assistance to establish shared infrastructure like bio-artificial intelligence hubs, biofoundries, and biomanufacturing hubs. The applicant must be a legally registered entity in India possessing demonstrated prior experience in the applied areas of bio-services or high-performance biomanufacturing. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Biotechnology and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council, and the applications for this scheme are accepted primarily through periodic national calls on their official digital portals.
## Benefits - The scheme has a total proposed financial outlay of ₹91,97,00,00,000/- for the period spanning from 2021-22 to 2025-26. - Startups receive seed funding, incubation support, and dedicated mentorship to nurture a thriving ecosystem for bio-entrepreneurs. - Researchers, institutions, and universities receive extramural funding and direct grants for cutting-edge research and development in modern biology. - Financial assistance of up to ₹50,00,00,000/- is provided for the setting up of Bio-Artificial Intelligence Hubs. - Financial assistance of up to ₹65,00,00,000/- is provided for the setting up of Biofoundries. - Financial assistance of up to ₹75,00,00,000/- is provided for the setting up of Biomanufacturing Hubs. - Coordinating hubs are eligible to propose an annual budget of up to ₹50,00,000/- to comprehensively cover the operational costs of collaborating projects. - Academic institutions receive funding through grant-in-aid mechanisms for mission mode projects as per the extramural research guidelines of the Department of Biotechnology. - Startups, small and medium enterprises, and industries seeking funding beyond ₹50,00,000/- receive financial assistance through co-funding combined with royalty sharing or equity financing. - Private universities, non-governmental organizations, trusts, and foundations receive capital support but are required to share 25% of the total capital investment cost. - Incubators or companies established by the Central Government or private universities receive funding with a mandatory co-funding requirement of a minimum of 30% of the total project cost. - Incubators or companies established by the State Government receive funding with a mandatory co-funding requirement of a minimum of 50% of the total project cost.
##### ***Conditions*** - Startups, small and medium enterprises, and industry applicants must contribute a minimum of 30% of the total project cost in cash, strictly excluding land and construction costs. - Joint industry-academia projects require the involved industry partner to share a minimum of 30% of the cost attributed to the industry component. - Beneficiaries opting for the royalty-sharing model must pay a 5% royalty on the net sales of the developed product until the paid royalty equals the disbursed financial assistance. - Beneficiaries opting for equity financing must agree to the government taking an equity stake through convertible notes that get compulsorily converted at the valuation of the first investment round of ₹10,00,00,000/- or more within five years, or mandatorily at the end of the fifth year at a 20% discount of the latest valuation. - The applicant must successfully implement a clearly defined sustainability business plan to ensure continuous operations after the government support period is over. - In the event of project foreclosure, the beneficiary must completely refund the disbursed amount within 30 days from the date of foreclosure. - In the event of project termination due to non-compliance, the beneficiary must completely refund the disbursed amount along with a 12% interest within 30 days from the date of termination.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a legal entity, either for-profit or not-for-profit. - The applicant must be officially registered in India with the respective taxation and other administrative authorities. - The applicant must have tangible prior experience in the applied functional area of bio-services or biomanufacturing. - The applicant must not be blacklisted by any Central Government. - The applicant must not be blacklisted by any State Government. - The applicant must not be blacklisted by any Public Sector Undertaking of the Government of India. - The applicant must ensure that major promoters or the legal entity are not involved in any major litigation that may impact the delivery of assigned projects. - The applicant must strictly adhere to the data protection, confidentiality, and conflict of interest policies laid down by the Department of Biotechnology and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council. - The applicant, if applying as a startup, small and medium enterprise, or industry, must have a minimum of 51% of its stake owned and controlled by resident Indian citizens. ##### ***Desirable Criteria*** - The applicant should preferably demonstrate proven expertise, operational experience, and access to pre-existing infrastructure. - The applicant should ideally have already secured the necessary regulatory clearances for their innovation or be close to obtaining them.
## Exclusions

## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Step 1:** The applicant must continuously monitor the official portals of the Department of Biotechnology and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council for periodic national calls for proposals. The applicant must thoroughly review the released guidelines and identify the relevant thematic sector for their project. **Step 2:** The applicant must thoroughly prepare and optionally submit an Expression of Interest if it is specifically requested by the authorities prior to the full proposal submission stage. This initial submission helps the reviewing committee fundamentally gauge the scope and feasibility of the intended project. **Step 3:** The applicant must systematically draft and submit the complete project proposal through the designated official online platform before the final deadline. This exhaustive application must clearly detail the bio-services scope, technical milestones, pre-existing infrastructure, and precise funding requirements. Post-Application Process **Step 4:** The submitted project proposal is initially evaluated by a Preliminary Screening Committee to verify strict compliance with the defined eligibility criteria. Any proposals that fail to meet the foundational legal, financial, and technical prerequisites are systematically filtered out at this stage. **Step 5:** The applicant must professionally present the comprehensive proposal before the Selection Committee for Biofoundries and Biomanufacturing Hubs. This expert committee will meticulously evaluate the core technical aspects, infrastructural readiness, and overall innovation viability of the submission. **Step 6:** The applicant's proposal is subsequently reviewed by the Financial Evaluation Committee to determine the exact funding mechanism logically applicable to the project. This critical evaluation includes accurately assessing the modalities for co-funding, equity financing, and royalty-sharing based on the applicant's exact entity type. **Step 7:** The applicant will receive the formal selection confirmation and the corresponding financial disbursement strictly based on the binding recommendations of the Apex Committee. The successfully selected beneficiary must then sign the necessary grant agreements to formally initiate the biomanufacturing project. **Step 8:** The applicant will undergo continuous performance monitoring facilitated by the Project Monitoring Committee to ensure milestone adherence. Third-party evaluations will additionally be carried out periodically to stringently review the ongoing progress and infrastructural utilization.

# Free Travel Facility for the Teachers Awarded at the National and State Level **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Transport & Infrastructure | **Tags:** Free Travel Facility, National Awarded Teacher, Free Transport | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Launched on 4th February, 2020, the scheme “Free Travel Facility for the Teachers Awarded at the National and State Level” by the Rajasthan State Transport Corporation under the Transport Department, Government of Rajasthan, aims to provide free travel facilities in Rajasthan State Transport Corporation buses to teachers who are residents of Rajasthan and have received national or state level awards in recognition of their excellence in the field of education.

metadata.schemeName: Post-Matric Scholarship for Students belonging to National Minorities
metadata.briefDescription: This scholarship provides financial assistance to students belonging to minority communities studying at the post-matric or post-secondary level to help them pursue higher education. It is available for students studying in India who have secured a minimum of 50% marks in their previous examination.

page_content:
# Post-Matric Scholarship for Students belonging to National Minorities **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Ladakh | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Post Matric, Scholarship, Students, Minority Communities | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Post-Matric Scholarship for Students belonging to National Minorities" has been implemented by the Ministry of Minority Affairs through the Social Welfare Department, Government of Ladakh. This scholarship has been designed to provide financial assistance to students from minority communities pursuing post-matriculation or post-secondary education, enabling them to continue higher studies. It has been made available to students studying in India who have secured a minimum of 50% marks in their previous examination, with parents’/guardians’ annual income not exceeding ₹2.0 lakhs. The scholarship has been awarded for courses from Class XI to Ph.D. that are not covered under the MCM (Merit Cum Means) scheme.
## Benefits **Financial Assistance / Benefits:** **Admission and Tuition Fee:** **Classes XI and XII:** - Hostellers: Actual, up to ₹7,000 per annum - Day Scholars: Actual, up to ₹7,000 per annum **Technical and Vocational Courses (XI and XII level, includes raw materials, etc.):** - Hostellers: Actual, up to ₹10,000 per annum - Day Scholars: Actual, up to ₹10,000 per annum **Undergraduate and Postgraduate Courses:** - Hostellers: Actual, up to ₹3,000 per annum - Day Scholars: Actual, up to ₹3,000 per annum **Maintenance Allowance (for 10 months in an academic year, includes study material, etc.):** **Classes XI and XII (including technical and vocational courses):** - Hostellers: ₹380 per month - Day Scholars: ₹230 per month **Courses other than technical and professional at Undergraduate and Postgraduate level:** - Hostellers: ₹570 per month - Day Scholars: ₹300 per month **M.Phil and Ph.D. (for researchers without any fellowship):** - Hostellers: ₹1,200 per month - Day Scholars: ₹550 per month
**Note:** Hostellers include students who are not staying in hostel of the school/institute concerned but are staying as paying guest or in rented accommodation in towns/cities which are not the places where their parents reside.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be belonging to a minority community. 1. The applicant should be studying in India at the post-matriculation or post-secondary level. 1. The applicant should be have secured a minimum of 50% marks in the previous examination. 1. The applicant should be from a family where the parents’/guardians’ annual income does not exceed ₹2.0 lakhs. 1. The applicant should be pursuing courses from Class XI to Ph.D. that are not covered under the MCM (Merit Cum Means) scheme.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline Step 1:The applicant should obtain the application form free of cost from the Head of the Institute, District Social Welfare Officer (DSWO), or download it from the Ministry of Minority Affairs website. The completed form, with all required documents and proofs, should be submitted to the Head of the Institute.
Step 2: The Head of the Institute should examine the applications, verify the necessary certificates, and forward them to the Chief Education Officer (for up to 12th standard), DSWO (for graduation courses beyond 12th), or Director, Social Welfare Department (for courses outside the state) as applicable.
Step 3: The DSWO/Head of the Institute should consolidate the verified applications in the prescribed format and forward the list to the Director, Social Welfare Department for onward submission to the Administrative Department to sanction and arrange funds from the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India.

metadata.briefDescription: "Medical Expenses-Treatment for Major Ailments Including Surgery'' scheme by the BOCW Welfare Board, Labour Dept.,West Bengal, is a welfare scheme that provides medical expenses for the treatment of beneficiary or his/ her dependents suffering from Cancer, Heart disease, Kidney disease, T.B. etc.

page_content:
# Medical Expenses-Treatment for Major Ailments Including Surgery **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** West Bengal | **Categories:** Health & Wellness, Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Labour, Building Worker, Construction Worker, Treatment, Ailments, Surgery, Medical Expenses | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Medical Expenses-Treatment for Major Ailments Including Surgery'' scheme by the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, West Bengal, is a welfare scheme for the registered workers of the board. Under this scheme, the Board shall provide financial assistance as medical expenses for the treatment of beneficiary or his/ her dependents suffering from Cancer, Heart disease, Kidney disease, T.B., Eye disease, Leprosy and Nerve disease. For the operation of diseases in case of Heart, Kidney etc. the Board may sanction a higher amount. ## Benefits - **Quantum of Assistance:** Upto a maximum amount of ₹20,000/- Per Annum. **Note:** For the operation of diseases like Heart, Kidney etc. the Board may sanction a maximum amount of ₹60,000/-. ## Eligibility Criteria > **For Registration as a Building/ Construction Worker:** - The applicant should be a resident of West Bengal. - The applicant should be a Building/ Construction Worker. - The applicant should be between 18 and 60 years. - The applicant should have engaged in building and construction work for at least 90 days in a given year. > **For the Application of the Welfare Scheme:** - The applicant should be a registered member Under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board of West Bengal. - The member or his/ her dependents should suffer from Cancer/ Heart disease/ Kidney disease/ T.B./ Eye disease/ Leprosy/ Nerve disease. ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline > **Registration Process as a Building/ Construction Worker:** **Step 1:** To register as a beneficiary under the BOCW Welfare Board, an applicant worker should request Form-27 from the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers and should attach all the mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). **Step 2:** Application shall be submitted to the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers. > **Application Process of the Welfare Scheme:** **Step 1:** A registered worker should request Form-XI for the application from the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers and should attach all the mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). **Step 2:** Application shall be submitted to the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers for this benefit. > **Helpdesk:** Labour Department Department of Labour, Government of West Bengal, 12th Floor, N.S Building, Block-A, 1, Kiran Shankar Roy Road, Kolkata-700001 Helpline of Labour Department, Govt. of West Bengal (Shramik Sathi): 1800-103-0009 > **Note:** - Upon successful verification, the construction worker is registered and an identity card and passbook are issued to him/ her. ₹20/- as the registration fee and ₹30/- as yearly subscription is taken. The amounts taken are noted in the passbook and a receipt is issued. - After one year, the beneficiary's subscription is renewed upon payment of a renewal fee of ₹30/- and submission of an application in Form-27A. - If not renewed the registration of the beneficiary is cancelled after the expiry of one year. Fresh application for renewal to be submitted to the ALC for consideration.

Under this scheme, the Board shall provide financial assistance to a beneficiary in case of hospitalization for 5 or more days and become disabled due to an accident. Also in case of death of such pension holder, his/her spouse/nominee will be entitled to a monthly family pension.

## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline > **Registration Process as a Building/ Construction Worker:** **Step 1:** To register as a beneficiary under the BOCW Welfare Board, an applicant worker should request Form-27 from the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers and should attach all the mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). **Step 2:** Application shall be submitted to the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers. > **Application Process of the Welfare Scheme:** **Step 1:** A registered worker should request Form-XXXIV for the application from the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers and should attach all the mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). **Step 2:** Application shall be submitted to the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers for this benefit. > **Helpdesk:** Labour Department Department of Labour, Government of West Bengal, 12th Floor, N.S Building, Block-A, 1, Kiran Shankar Roy Road, Kolkata-700001 Helpline of Labour Department, Govt. of West Bengal (Shramik Sathi): 1800-103-0009 > **Note:** - Upon successful verification, the construction worker is registered and an identity card and passbook are issued to him/ her. ₹20/- as the registration fee and ₹30/- as yearly subscription is taken. The amounts taken are noted in the passbook and a receipt is issued. - After one year, the beneficiary's subscription is renewed upon payment of a renewal fee of ₹30/- and submission of an application in Form-27A. - If not renewed the registration of the beneficiary is cancelled after the expiry of one year. Fresh application for renewal to be submitted to the ALC for consideration.

metadata.schemeName: Pension Benefit
metadata.briefDescription: The "Pension Benefit'' scheme by the BOCW Welfare Board, Labour Department,West Bengal, is a welfare scheme that provides a monthly pension after completion of 60 years to the eligible registered member.

page_content:
# Pension Benefit **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** West Bengal | **Categories:** Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Labour, Building Worker, Construction Worker, Pension, Nominee | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Pension Benefit'' scheme by the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, West Bengal, is a welfare scheme for the registered workers of the board. Under this scheme, the Board shall provide financial assistance in the form of pension to a registered member on completion of 60 years of age who has served the board for at least 5 years. Also, in case of death of the beneficiary, the spouse/nominee of the beneficiary is entitled to receive family pension of half of the amount of the pension which the beneficiary used to receive prior to his death. ## Benefits - **Pension:** ₹750/- to ₹1120/- Per Month. - **Family Pension:** Half of the amount of the pension which the beneficiary used to receive prior to his death (in case of death of the beneficiary).
## Eligibility Criteria > **For Registration as a Building/ Construction Worker:** - The applicant should be a resident of West Bengal. - The applicant should be a Building/ Construction Worker. - The applicant should be between 18 and 60 years. - The applicant should have engaged in building and construction work for at least 90 days in a given year. > **For the Application of the Welfare Scheme:** - The applicant should be a registered member Under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board of West Bengal. - The member should have served the board at least for 5 years. ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline > **Registration Process as a Building/ Construction Worker:** **Step 1:** To register as a beneficiary under the BOCW Welfare Board, an applicant worker should request Form-27 from the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers and should attach all the mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). **Step 2:** Application shall be submitted to the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers. > **Application Process of the Welfare Scheme:** **Step 1:** A registered worker should request Form-XXXVII for the application from the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers and should attach all the mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). **Step 2:** Application shall be submitted to the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers for this benefit. > **Helpdesk:** Labour Department Department of Labour, Government of West Bengal, 12th Floor, N.S Building, Block-A, 1, Kiran Shankar Roy Road, Kolkata-700001 Helpline of Labour Department, Govt. of West Bengal (Shramik Sathi): 1800-103-0009 > **Note:** - Upon successful verification, the construction worker is registered and an identity card and passbook are issued to him/ her. ₹20/- as the registration fee and ₹30/- as yearly subscription is taken. The amounts taken are noted in the passbook and a receipt is issued. - After one year, the beneficiary's subscription is renewed upon payment of a renewal fee of ₹30/- and submission of an application in Form-27A. - If not renewed the registration of the beneficiary is cancelled after the expiry of one year. Fresh application for renewal to be submitted to the ALC for consideration.

metadata.schemeName: Mukhyamantri Nishulk Coaching Yojana-OBC
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to provide free coaching and residential facilities to Other Backward Class(OBC) students of Rajasthan for various competitive examinations through reputed coaching institutes.

page_content:
# Mukhyamantri Nishulk Coaching Yojana-OBC **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Social welfare & Empowerment, Education & Learning | **Tags:** Free Coaching, Other Backward Class, Hostel Facility, OBC | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme “Mukhyamantri Nishulk Coaching Yojana-OBC” launched by the Social Justice and Empowerment Department, Government of Rajasthan, aims to support Other Backward Class(OBC) students through free coaching, hostel accommodation for various entrance and professional exams.
## Benefits - **Residential Facility:** Selected students will be provided with hostel accommodation under the departmental hostels. - **Coaching Facility:** Free coaching will be arranged in reputed local coaching institutes. > **Notes:** - Students availing benefits under this scheme will not be eligible to receive benefits under any similar central or state government scheme. - If a student’s attendance is below 80%, their name will be removed from coaching, and the payment for that month will not be made to the coaching institution. In case of unavoidable circumstances, the department will consider the student’s application. - No coaching institute shall collect any type of fee from the selected students; payment will be made directly by the department. - Applicants availing the benefit of the scheme will not be eligible for the benefit of the "Anuprati Scheme" run by the department.
## Eligibility Criteria - Applicants must be natives of Rajasthan. - Applicants must belong to the Other Backward Class(OBC) community. - SC applicants must have secured 60% marks in Class 10th. - SC applicants seeking admission to IITs and medical colleges must have secured 70% marks in Mathematics and Science in Class 10. - Undergraduate students must have secured 60% marks in the second and third year of graduation. If the results are not declared within the previous year, the results will be considered. - Applicants must be studying regularly in Class 11th and 12th for admission to national-level technical/medical/law courses. - Applicants must reside in the Social Justice and Empowerment Department's hostels in Jaipur and Kota. - Applicants must be pursuing regular undergraduate/postgraduate studies at a government or recognized private college for CAT/MAT coaching for admission to national-level management institutes and IIMs. - The annual income of the family (from all sources) should not exceed ₹2,50,000/-.
> **Notes:** - Coaching facility will be available to students for a maximum period of two years for the entrance examinations of engineering and medical courses and for only one year for the entrance examinations of law and management courses. - Coaching facility for postgraduate courses will be provided to the students till the final year of graduation or till the next year of passing the graduation examination. - Students admitted to the coaching institute can complete the course only within the period of the contract with the coaching institute. If the contract with any institute is for a period of 2 years, then admission can be taken in the 2-year course in the first year of the contract but admission cannot be taken in the 2-year course in the second year.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Registration Process:** **Step 1:** Visit the official portal of Rajasthan Single Sign On: [https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/) **Step 2:** On the homepage, click on the "[Register here](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/register)" tab. **Step 3:** Select ‘Jan Aadhaar’ option for registration under the ‘Citizen’ tab. **Step 4:** Complete the registration process by entering your Jan Aadhaar Number. **Step 5:** After successful registration, you will receive a User ID (SSO ID) and Password. These credentials will allow you to check your application status and apply for scheme in the future. > **Application Process:** **Step 1:** To apply under the scheme, revisit the official portal of Rajasthan Single Sign On: [https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/) **Step 2:** On the homepage, click on the "[Login to RajSSO](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/signin)" tab. **Step 3:** Enter your username (SSO ID), password, and Captcha, then click ‘Login’. **Step 4:** Once logged in, update your profile. **Step 5:** Click on SJMS SMS icon, then click on "HSMS (Hostel & RREIS)" icon **Step 6:** Fill in the required information, and upload all necessary documents on the online portal. **Step 7:** After entering the information and uploading the documents, make sure to submit/save your application form.

page_content:
# West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Assistance to Individual Handloom Weaver **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** West Bengal | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Handloom, Handloom Weaver, Financial Benefit | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description “Assistance to Individual Handloom Weaver" is a sub-scheme under "West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024”, launched by the Micro, Small & Medium Enterprise and Textiles Department, Government of West Bengal on 7th March, 2024, and it shall remain in force for a period of five years. The objective of this sub-scheme is to provide one-time financial assistance to the individual Handloom weavers who are not under the ambit of any Primary Weavers’ Cooperative Societies.

metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote higher education and mobility among meritorious girl students by providing a scooter or financial assistance.

page_content:
# Kali Bai Bheel Medhavi Chhatra Scooty Yojana (12th Pass) **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Education, Scooty, Bhil Community, Financial Assistance, Women Empowerment | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme “Kali Bai Bheel Medhavi Chhatra Scooty Yojana (12th Pass)” launched by the Higher Education Department, Government of Rajasthan, aims to support meritorious girl students by providing scooters or ₹40,000 to eligible girl students pursuing higher education after Class 12th.
## Benefits - **Scooter:** Eligible meritorious girl students receive a scooter under the scheme. > **Additional Benefits with Scooter:** - **Transportation and Registration Charges:** Includes registration, transfer in the student’s name, and delivery expenses.- **1-Year General Insurance:** 1-year insurance coverage for the scooter.- **5-Year Third-Party Insurance:** 5-year third-party insurance coverage.- **2 Litres of Petrol:** Provided once at the time of distribution.- **1 Helmet:** Given at the time of scooter delivery.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must have passed Class 12th with a minimum of 65% marks from the Rajasthan Board of Secondary Education or 75% marks from the Central Board of Secondary Education. - The applicant must be studying in any school or college located in Rajasthan. - The applicant must be a regular student in Class 12th in a government or private school, including residential schools run by the State Government. - Marks obtained in supplementary examinations will not be counted in the prescribed percentage. - The applicant must be pursuing a regular graduate degree from any college in Rajasthan (such as B.A. B.Ed., B.Sc. B.Ed., B.Com. B.Ed., B.E., B.Tech., B.Arch., MBBS, IIT, BBA, BBM, BCA, BDS, BHMS, BAMS, LAW, etc.). - The applicant must not have a gap of one year between passing Class 12th and admission to a graduate degree course. - The applicant may receive benefits from this scheme even if receiving financial assistance from any other scheme. - However, if the student has received a scooter based on Class 10th results from the TAD Department or School Education Department, she will receive ₹40,000/- under this scheme if eligible. - The annual income of the student’s parents must not exceed ₹2,50,000/-. - Under the TAD Department, all eligible students from families exempt from income tax are eligible for benefits.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online - via CSC - Contact with nearest E-mitra center to apply for this service.

# Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement: QGBG (Quality Gap Bridging Group) - Spice Producer’s Groups in Identified Clusters **Ministry:** Ministry Of Commerce And Industry | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment, Banking,Financial Services and Insurance, Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Agriculture, Farming, Farmer, Spices Board | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement – QGBG (Quality Gap Bridging Group) – Spice Producer’s Groups in Identified Clusters is implemented by the Spices Board, India under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The objective of the scheme is to strengthen the capacity of Spice Producer Groups (SPGs) to produce spices that meet quality, safety, and traceability standards by providing support to identified groups. The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
## Benefits **Assistance subjected to a maximum of** ₹ **25 Lakhs per Spice Producer's Groups for the following activities-** **1. Post-harvest machine /equipment bank:** Setting up of post-harvest machine/equipment bank availing the assistance under the Post-harvest improvement programme of the Board during next five years at a maximum of 90 % of the cost, limited to the cost ceiling of each programme/ programmes fixed for Spice Producer's Groups in this working procedure. Assistance for Spice Producer's Groups will be for only two machine/equipment under each component of the PHI programme for use among the members of the Spice Producer's Groups. The custodian of the machines/equipments availed under the Board’s programme will be the designated office bearer of the Spice Producer's Groups (₹ 15 Lakh / Spice Producer’s Groups) 2. IT support for joining online platform on traceability and improving quantum of sale by the Spice Producer's Groups (hardware +other required accessories and subscriptions) (₹ 1.28 lakhs/ Spice Producer’s Groups) 3. Establishment of plot for GAP ( ₹ 1.50 lakhs/ Spice Producer's Groups )- Area 0.4ha. Assistance proposal based and on standard cost of cultivation, at maximum of ₹ 0.50 lakh/plot/year for 3 consecutive years. 4. Support for technical manpower for maintenance of online platforms, GAP plot and office of Spice Producer's Groups ( ₹ 0.20 lakh/person/month for 3 consecutive years) The above assistance will be provided to Spices Producers Group based on MoU with Spices Board. Group need to be a legal entity such as registered FPO, FPC, SHG, SPS and other such entities which can enter into a legally binding agreement. Those entities which are restricted from receiving assistance other than promoting/sponsoring agencies are not eligible under the component. Assistance will be released based on terms and conditions by NITI Aayog.
## Eligibility Criteria 1.All spice growing States and regions in India preferably in the ODOP (One District One Product) and clusters of Spices under AEP of MoC and operational area of collaborative national and international projects of Spices Board 2.On receipt of application with documents, the Officer concerned will visit the Reg. Office of the group and evaluate the status, facility and arrangements available with the group for taking up the activity components successfully. Eligible application will be recommended to Divisional Officer/Regional Officer as the case may be for further scrutiny and issue of permission letter to the group to sign MoU with the Board. Recommending Officer will arrange signing of MoU and collection of documents proving purchase and physically verify the installation of the equipment/device and recommend Eligible case for sanction of assistance. 3.Other assistance on IT support, establishment of GAP plot and support for technical manpower under the component will be extended based on the terms and conditions stipulated in the MoU. Number of members in a group will be a deciding factor for selection of the group and quantum of assistance. The subcomponents (1 to 4) will be implemented together in exemplary groups with good track record and singly or clubbing 2 components as decided by the Board.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Registration** Step 1: The applicant should visit the [ServicesPlus](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/) website. Step 2: Click on the “[Register” ](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/citizenRegistration.html)option on the homepage. Step 3: Fill out the registration form by entering Full Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, Password, selecting State, and Captcha. Step 4: Review all details carefully and submit the registration form. Step 5: An OTP will be sent to your registered mobile number or email; enter the OTP and click “Verify.” Step 6: Registration will be completed successfully, and a confirmation message will be displayed or sent via email. **Login** Step 1: The applicant should visit the ServicesPlus website and click on [“Login.”](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/loginWindow.do) Step 2: Enter your Email ID, Password, and Captcha. Step 3: Select the relevant service/scheme name. Step 4: Fill in the required details in the application form. Step 5: Submit the application.

# Concession Travel for Licensed Coolies of RSRTC **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Transport & Infrastructure | **Tags:** Travel Concession, Fare Concession, Coolie | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Launched on 19th May, 2008, the scheme “Concession Travel for Licensed Coolies of RSRTC” by the Rajasthan State Transport Corporation under the Transport Department, Government of Rajasthan, aims to support RSRTC licensed coolies through providing a 50% concession in passenger fare on municipal bus services to eligible beneficiaries.
