metadata.schemeName: West Bengal Student Credit Card Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The Higher Education Department, Government of West Bengal has introduced the Student Credit Card Scheme for the students of West Bengal to enable them to pursue higher education without having any financial constraints.

page_content:
# West Bengal Student Credit Card Scheme **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** West Bengal | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Education Loan, Higher Study | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description This scheme is designed to support the students to pursue secondary, higher secondary, madrasah, undergraduate and post graduate studies including professional degree and other equivalent courses in any School, Madrasah, College, University and other affiliated institutes within and outside India. Students studying in various coaching institutions for appearing in different competitive examinations like Engineering, Medical, Law, IAS, IPS, WBCS etc, can also avail the loan under this scheme.
## Benefits **Points** 1. The Scheme provides a maximum loan of ₹10,00,000/- at a 4% simple annual interest rate after interest subvention. 1. The interest rate for loans up to ₹10,00,000/- is set at the prevailing 3-year MCLR of State Bank of India plus 1%, fixed at the time of sanction. 1. Students can access the loan at any point during their course of study. 1. Both the student and the parent/legal guardian must co-submit the loan application. 1. An agreement between the student, parents/legal guardians, and the bank will formalize the loan terms. **Margin money:** 1. Up to ₹4,00,000/-: Nil 1. Above ₹4,00,000/-: 5% 1. Scholarships/assistance ships included 1. Paid pro-rata as disbursements are made **Security**: 1. No unnecessary restrictions or collateral security 1. No security/collateral other than co-obligation of parents/legal guardians 1. State government to enter separate agreement with banks **Insurance:** 1. Life cover for student up to loan amount 1. Premium paid by student and debited from loan account **Time limits:** 1. The Higher Education Department and the School Education Department will communicate on loan sanctioning and disbursement process timeline after receiving approval from the competent authority. ## Eligibility Criteria 1. Indian citizen & resident of West Bengal for 10 years (self-declaration). 1. Applicant should not be aged more than 40 years at application time. 1. Applicant should enrolled in higher education programs within or outside the country in schools, madrasahs, colleges, universities, IITs, IIMs, IISc, IIESTs, ISIs, NLUs, AIIMSs, NITs, XLRI, BITS, SPA, NID, IIFTs, ICFAI Business School, etc. or studying in coaching institutes for various competitive exams such as Engineering, Medical, Law, IAS, IPS, WBCS, SSC, etc.
**Note:** Students upload progress reports after each semester/year. ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Step 1:** Applicant have to visit the official [website ](https://wbscc.wb.gov.in)and click on "STUDENT CREDIT CARD" **Step 2:** Now Click on “STUDENT REGISTRATION” option and select the one option from the following - [For institutions in India](https://wbscc.wb.gov.in/Applicant_Registration).- [For institutions outside India](https://wbscc.wb.gov.in/Scc_Foreign/Applicant_Registration). **Step 3:** Provide the require details for online registration process and click on “Submit” button to generate user id and password. **Step 4:** After completion of the registration process a unique id will be generated. **Step 5:** Now with the credentials need to log in through clicking on “Student Login” button from the home page **Step 6:** Here the candidate need to furnish their all details which can be accessed through the “Applicant Dashboard.” **Step 7:** Upload the required documents and click on "Submit". > **User Manual:** [Click here](https://wbscc.wb.gov.in/assets/StudentManual.pdf).

# Free Travel Facility for Appearing in Interviews for Competitive Examinations Conducted by UPSC/RPSC/RSMSSN **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Transport & Infrastructure | **Tags:** Free Travel Facility, Competitive Examination Interviews, Free Transportation | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Launched in 2018, the scheme “Free Travel Facility for Appearing in Interviews for Competitive Examinations Conducted by UPSC/RPSC/RSMSSN” by the Rajasthan State Transport Corporation under the Transport Department, Government of Rajasthan, aims to support interview candidates by providing free travel in ordinary express services from their residence to the interview location.

metadata.schemeName: Research Associates (RA)
metadata.briefDescription: The Research Associates (RAs) of the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) in India are individuals who engage in research work under the DBT-Research Associateship Program in Biotechnology and its was started in 1999.

page_content:
# Research Associates (RA)

**Ministry:** Ministry Of Science And Technology | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Education & Learning, Skills & Employment | **Tags:** Education, Employment, Bio-Technology | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual

## Description
The objective of DBT-Research Associateship (DBT-RA) Programme is to train and nurture young researchers, scientists and generate a critical mass of trained manpower in modern areas of biology and biotechnology and build a robust postdoctoral base for the growth of Biotechnology sectors in the country.

## Benefits
> Stipend: RAs are awarded a fellowship of ₹55,000 per month, plus house rent allowance (HRA) and other benefits. The fellowship is tenable for two years, with the possibility of renewal for another two years based on satisfactory performance.

## Eligibility Criteria
1. Applicant  must have Ph.D./ M.D./ M.S. degree in a relevant field.
1. Applicant  must have good academic record.
1. Age limit is 40 years for male candidates and 45 years for female candidates.
1. Applicants who are employed can apply, but must relinquish their employment to accept the fellowship.
1. The DBT-RA fellowship can be availed only once in a career.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Online
1. Application for DBT-RA programme shall be by ONLINE mode only.
1. To apply, interested applicants may kindly visit DBT-RA Online Portal [https://ra.dbtindia.gov.in/](https://ra.dbtindia.gov.in/)1. Applicants must register on the DBT-RA Online portal, fill in complete information in the online application form and submit it before the closing date of application.
1. Online application form to be filled by applicant comprises information pertaining to Personal Information, Academic Qualifications, Research Contribution, Referee Details, Proposed Research Work, Proposed Mentor Details and Proposed Host Institution.
1. Documents to be submitted along with Online Application Form include –

  - Self-attested pdf copy of DOB certificate
  - Self-attested pdf copies of degree certificates
  - A Consent letter from the mentor. (Format for the Consent letter is available at the DBT-RA portal.)

1. Names and contact details of the Referees are to be provided by the applicant while filling out the application form.
1. During submission of online application form, email with link to submit letter of recommendation shall be sent by the applicant to the email addresses of all the referees who have been mentioned in the application form.

page_content:
# National Career Service Centers For SC/STs (Erstwhile Coaching-cum-Guidance Centre for SC/STs) **Ministry:** Ministry Of Labour and Employment | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Skills & Employment | **Tags:** Student, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Coaching, Training, Counselling, Stipend | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme "National Career Service Centers For SC/STs" was launched by the Directorate General of Employment (DGE), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India. The scheme aims to enhance the employability of educated Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) jobseekers through counselling, coaching, and training. The scheme provides vocational guidance, confidence-building programmes, personality development sessions, practice in typing and shorthand, special coaching for competitive exams, and computer training courses. The applicant must be an educated, unemployed SC/ST jobseeker registered with an Employment Exchange to avail of these benefits. The scheme is implemented by the National Career Service Centers (NCSCs) located in various states.
## Benefits - The scheme offers Vocational Guidance and Career Counselling Services to educated SC/ST jobseekers. - The scheme provides Practice in Typing and Shorthand to ensure registrants maintain their speed while waiting on the Live Register of Employment Exchanges. - The scheme offers a Special Coaching Scheme to prepare candidates for competitive examinations and selection tests for Group “C” or equivalent posts (e.g., General English, General Awareness, Computer Training). - The scheme provides Computer Training Courses through outsourcing, including ‘O’ Level Software/Hardware training, Office Automation, and Cyber Secured Web Development. - The scheme provides a monthly stipend of ₹1,000/- per candidate. - The scheme provides free books and stationery worth ₹1,000/- per candidate for the entire course. _*The stipend is paid through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), subject to the candidate maintaining 80% attendance in a particular month._
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Caste (SC) or the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category. - The applicant must be an unemployed jobseeker. - The applicant must be registered with an Employment Exchange. - The applicant must have passed 10+2 (Minimum educational qualification for coaching or courses). - The family annual income of the applicant should not be more than ₹3,00,000/- per annum.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline ##### ***Step 1: Locate the Nearest Center*** The applicant must identify the nearest National Career Service Center (NCSC) for SC/STs from the [list of 25 centers](https://dge.gov.in/ncsc_for_sc_sts) located across India (e.g., Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, etc.). ##### ***Step 2: Obtain the Application Form*** The applicant must collect the application form physically from the respective NCSC office or request it through the official email ID of the center (e.g., ncscbengaluru[at]gmail[dot]com for Bengaluru). ##### ***Step 3: Submit the Application*** The applicant must fill out the application form completely and attach self-attested copies of all required documents. The applicant must submit the duly filled form along with the documents to the Sub-Regional Employment Officer at the respective National Career Service Center address or submit it via email if the option is provided by the specific center.

metadata.schemeName: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme addresses eradicating bonded labour in India. It introduces varying rehabilitation assistance amounts based on beneficiary categories, such as adults, children, women, and extreme cases, with provisions for annuity schemes and Direct Benefit Transfer.

page_content:
# Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer **Ministry:** Ministry Of Labour and Employment | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Rehabilitation, Labour, DBT, Trafficking, Social Justice | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer-2021, effective from January 27, 2022, is a crucial initiative led by the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India that addresses eradicating bonded labour in India. It introduces varying rehabilitation assistance amounts based on beneficiary categories, such as adults, children, women, and extreme cases, with provisions for annuity schemes and Direct Benefit Transfer. The scheme also facilitates surveys, awareness programs, and evaluatory studies to combat bonded labour, with financial support. It emphasizes skill development, socio-economic assistance, and monitoring mechanisms, all aimed at offering comprehensive support to eradicate the bonded labour system in the country. ## Benefits > **For Adult Male Beneficiaries** - The rehabilitation assistance shall be ₹1,00,000 (One Lakh Rupees) per adult male beneficiary. - Beneficiaries have the option to deposit the assistance in an annuity scheme or receive it as a cash grant. - The District Administration will assess the cash requirement of the beneficiary and, with their consent, place the money in an annuity scheme. > **Special Category Beneficiaries (Children, Women)** - Rehabilitation assistance for special category beneficiaries, such as children, including orphans, or those rescued from forced labour, and women, shall be ₹2,00,000/-. - At least ₹1,25,000/- shall be deposited in an annuity scheme in each beneficiary's name. - The remaining amount shall be transferred to the beneficiary's account via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). > **Extreme Cases of Bonded or Forced Labor** - In cases of extreme deprivation, such as transgender individuals, women, and children rescued from sexual exploitation, or trafficking, the rehabilitation assistance shall be ₹3,00,000/-. - At least ₹2,00,000/- shall be deposited in an annuity scheme in each beneficiary's name. - ₹1,00,000/- shall be transferred to the beneficiary's account via DBT. > **Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund:** - Each state shall create a Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund at the district level with a permanent corpus of at least ₹10,00,000 (Ten Lakhs Rupees) at the disposal of the District Magistrate. - Penalties recovered from convicted perpetrators of bonded labour may be deposited in this corpus. > **Immediate Financial Assistance** - The District Administration shall provide immediate financial assistance up to ₹30,000/- to rescued individuals from the District Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund. - The District Magistrate may disburse higher amounts if required but limited to the maximum entitlement prescribed under this scheme. > **State Government Responsibilities** - Providing a safe and secure environment for capacity building of child-bonded labourers. - Addressing the special needs of female freed bonded labourers, including financial support for marriage. - Offering special care for disabled individuals, in line with the national policy for disabled people. - Providing employable skill development training for adult bonded labourers who do not fall into the above categories.
## Eligibility Criteria - The beneficiary should be a rescued bonded labour.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Step 1: Submission of Proposal** - The District Magistrate/Administration forwards the proposal for financial support to the relevant State Ministry/Department dealing with the Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Scheme (BLR). - The State/UT Government submits each proposal for immediate cash assistance and rehabilitation assistance. > **Step 2: Release of Funds** - The eligible reimbursements are disbursed directly by the M/oLE to the State/UT Government. - The State/UT Government transfers the allocated funds to the concerned District Magistrate/Collector to support the implementation of BLR. > **Step 3: Disbursement of Benefits** - The District Administration will assess the cash requirement of the beneficiary and exercise its best judgment if the amount should be put under an annuity scheme or transferred to the beneficiary account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

metadata.schemeName: Additional Infrastructure for Up-gradation of Existing EMRS
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to enhance the capacity of existing Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) from 480 students (240 boys and 240 girls) by providing additional academic and residential infrastructure facilities for tribal students.

page_content:
# Additional Infrastructure for Up-gradation of Existing EMRS **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** EMRS Upgradation, Tribal Students, Residential Schools, Infrastructure Development, Academic Facilities | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Launched in 2016, the scheme "Additional Infrastructure for Up-gradation of Existing EMRS" by the Tribal Area Development Department, Government of Rajasthan, aims to enhance student capacity and improve facilities by providing additional classrooms, hostels, dining halls, staff quarters, and allied infrastructure to tribal students studying in existing EMRS.
## Benefits - **Infrastructure Up-gradation:** - Construction of a school building for 480 students (Classes 6 to 12); - Construction of a hostel for 240 boys; - Construction of a hostel for 240 girls; - Construction of a dining hall; - Development of sports facilities; - Construction of a modern guest room for parents; - Construction of a warden quarter, staff quarters, and watchman room; and - construction of a boundary wall.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The following category of citizens is eligible under the scheme for capacity enhancement of Eklavya Model Residential Schools: - Students belonging to the tribal majority areas. 2. The following reserved category of citizens is eligible under the scheme: - Scheduled Tribe (ST) students.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline > The applicant should submit the proposal in written application to: - **For the districts of the Tribal Sub-Plan:** Commissioner, Tribal Area Development Department/ Deputy Commissioner, Tribal Area Development Department. - **For the districts of the Non-Sub-Plan area:** Office of the Chief Executive Officer, Zila Parishad.

metadata.schemeName: Compensation to  Victims of Atrocities Belonging to SCs/STs
metadata.briefDescription: The objective of this scheme is to provide financial relief to SC/ST persons affected by caste discrimination in cases registered with the police under Section 3 of the Scheduled Castes and Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, as amended in 2018.

page_content:
# Compensation to Victims of Atrocities Belonging to SCs/STs **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Himachal Pradesh | **Categories:** Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Victims, Atrocities, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The Scheme "Compensation to Victims of Atrocities belonging to SCs/STs" has been launched by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Himachal Pradesh. The scheme provides financial relief to persons belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes who are victims of caste-based discrimination and whose cases are registered with the police under Section 3 of the Scheduled Castes and Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, as amended in 2018.
## Benefits To provide relief amount to victims belonging to Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes ranging from ₹85,000/- to ₹8,25,000/-.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must belong to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe. 1. The applicant must be a victim of caste-based atrocity or discrimination. 1. A case must be registered with the police under Section 3 of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline Step 1: Immediately after the incident, the victim must register a First Information Report (FIR) at the nearest police station. Step 2: The police forward the FIR to the district administration for necessary action. Step 3: After verification, the district administration sanctions and releases the relief amount.

metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to encourage tribal students to participate in sports and prepare them for national and international competitions by providing free hostel accommodation, food, training, and study support.

page_content:
# Operating Sports Hostel **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Housing & Shelter | **Tags:** Tribal Students, Sports Hostel, Sports Coaching | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Launched in 1996, the scheme "Operating Sports Hostel" by the Tribal Area Development Department, Government of Rajasthan, aims to promote sports among tribal students and prepare them for higher-level competitions by providing hostel accommodation, sports training, food, study materials, and other facilities to tribal students studying in classes 6th to 12th.
## Benefits - **Free Hostel Accommodation:** Selected students are provided free residential hostel facilities in sports hostels. - **Food and Nutrition:** Students receive free meals, breakfast, and a special nutritional diet as per the approved pattern. - **Sports Training:** Professional sports training is provided by trained coaches and experts. Training is conducted using modern sports equipment. - **Educational Support:** Students are allowed to continue regular schooling in nearby schools while staying in the sports hostel. - **Study Materials and Uniform:** School uniforms and other essential study materials are provided free of cost.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a tribal student. - The applicant must be residing in the state of Rajasthan. - The applicant must be currently studying in any class from 6th to 12th. - The applicant should be free from any physical disability or any type of disease. - The applicant’s father or guardian must not be an income tax payer. - The applicant must not have failed in their previous academic class. - The applicant must successfully pass the prescribed Battery Test for selection.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online - via CSC - **Where to Apply:** Applicants can apply by visiting the nearest [E-Mitra kiosk](https://reportsemitraapp.rajasthan.gov.in/WebSrc/Reports/rpt_search_new_emitra_ksk.jsp). - **Application Fee:** The application form for the "Operating Sports Hostel" is free of cost. - **Selection Process:** Admissions are granted based on the performance in the Battery Test and the decision of the Selection Committee.

metadata.schemeName: Establishment of Marketing Infrastructure
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote the creation and development of marketing infrastructure for horticulture commodities by providing subsidy for establishing retail outlets and collection, sorting, grading, and packing units to farmers.

page_content:
# Establishment of Marketing Infrastructure **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Marketing Infrastructure, Horticulture, Retail Market Outlet, Subsidy, Credit Linked Back Ended Assistance, Farmer | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Establishment of Marketing Infrastructure" scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Horticulture Department, Government of Rajasthan, with 60% Central Government funding and 40% State Government funding, and aims to develop marketing infrastructure for horticulture commodities through financial assistance to eligible beneficiaries. The scheme is project-based and viable projects are submitted for approval under the National Horticulture Mission after approval by the State Mission Executive Committee. It encourages investment from private and cooperative sectors in horticulture marketing infrastructure. The scheme also strengthens existing wholesale markets and rural haats while promoting grading, standardization, and quality certification of horticultural produce. It further seeks to create awareness among farmers, consumers, entrepreneurs, and market functionaries regarding market-related agricultural activities, including contract farming.
## Benefits > **Retail Market/Outlet (Controlled Environment):** - Subsidy of 35% is provided for establishing a retail market/outlet. - The maximum project cost considered is ₹15,00,000/- per unit. - Assistance is provided as credit-linked back-ended subsidy. - The beneficiary must submit a Detailed Project Proposal along with a Bank Loan Sanction Letter and prescribed affidavit, wherever applicable. > **Collection, Sorting, Grading and Packing Unit:** - Assistance of 40% is provided for establishing a collection, sorting, grading, and packing unit. - The maximum project cost considered is ₹15,00,000/- per unit. - Assistance is provided as credit-linked back-ended subsidy.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a farmer.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online - via CSC - **Mode of Application:** Online - **Mode of Online Application:** E-Mitra - Applicants can apply by visiting their nearest [E-Mitra center](https://reportsemitraapp.rajasthan.gov.in/WebSrc/Reports/rpt_search_new_emitra_ksk.jsp) or online through their own E-Mitra account. > **Note:** - Applying for a vermicompost unit is free. - The cost of setting up a retail market/outlet (controlled environment) has been fixed at ₹15,00,000/- per unit, on which 35% subsidy is payable as a credit-linked, back-ended loan. For this, the application, along with a detailed project proposal, along with bank loan sanction letter (affidavit of the applicable programme/component), has to be submitted to the District Horticulture Development Society, Jaipur.

metadata.schemeName: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance at a concessional rate of interest for setting up higher-cost income-generating activities, such as small business units, taxis, Mahindra Jeeps, Tata Sumos, shuttering work, piggery farms, etc.

page_content:
# National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation Scheme **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Himachal Pradesh | **Categories:** Banking,Financial Services and Insurance, Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Loans, Bank, Safai Karamcharis, Transport, Corporation | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Under the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) Scheme of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, the Government of Himachal Pradesh provides financial assistance at concessional rates of interest to set up higher-cost income-generating activities, such as small business units, taxis, Mahindra Jeeps, Tata Sumos, shuttering work, piggery farms, etc. Loans are also provided to Safai Karamcharis for the purchase of transport vehicles, such as Maruti Vans and Mahindra Jeeps, up to ₹5,00,000/- at an interest rate of 6%, and above ₹5,00,000/- at an interest rate of 8%, through the said corporation.
## Benefits - Concessional rate of interest at 6% for loans up to ₹5,00,000/- and 8% for loans above ₹5,00,000/-. - Maximum loan limit of ₹5,00,000/- under the concessional interest category. - Flexible repayment period of up to 5 years, making repayment easier for beneficiaries. - Low promoter’s contribution, limited to up to 5% of the total project cost. - Margin money support of 10% of the project cost provided by the HPSCST Development Corporation. - Major portion of project cost (85%) covered through an NSKFDC term loan, reducing the financial burden on beneficiaries.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be an unemployed member of a Safai Karamchari family of Himachal Pradesh. 1. The applicant should be between 18 and 55 years of age (20 to 53 years in the case of vehicle loans). 1. The applicant should be not a defaulter of any bank or financial institution. 1. The applicant should possess the required aptitude and/or valid license for the proposed activity. 1. The applicant should submit the application in the prescribed form along with a caste certificate and a Himachali certificate issued by the Executive Magistrate.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline Step 1: Obtain and fill the prescribed application form and attach all required documents. Step 2: Submit the completed application to the concerned District Manager or Corporation office for verification. Step 3: After approval, the application is forwarded to the HP SC/ST Development Corporation for further processing.

The scheme supports both individual artisans and those who apply through a group, society, or association, helping them meet their day-to-day business needs.

page_content:
# Hast Shilp Vikas Yojna **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Himachal Pradesh | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship, Sports & Culture, Skills & Employment | **Tags:** Handicrafts, Development, Loan, Skills | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The Hast Shilp Vikas Yojana is a scheme implemented under the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of Himachal Pradesh, through the Himachal Pradesh Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation. Under this scheme, the Corporation provides working capital assistance to artisans. Artisans may avail of this assistance either individually or by forming a group, society, or association. The assistance is interest-free for a period of two years. However, a society, association, or group may charge interest at the rate of 2% from the artisan to meet its administrative expenses.
## Benefits **Financial Support:** Provides a loan of ₹15,000 per artisan to support their craft and livelihood. **Low-Cost Financing:** Interest-free for 2 years, with only a minimal 2% administrative charge if routed through a society/group. **Flexible Repayment:** Loan repayment period of 2 years, making it easier for artisans to manage finances.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe family. 1. The applicant should be a bonafide resident of Himachal Pradesh. 1. The applicant should belong to a below poverty line (BPL) family. 1. The applicant should not be a defaulter of any financial institution or bank. 1. The applicant’s annual family income should not exceed ₹35,000/- per annum in both rural and urban areas.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline Step 1: Obtain and fill the prescribed [application form](https://himachalservices.nic.in/hpscstdc/PDFs/HastShilpi.pdf) and attach all required documents. Step 2: Submit the completed application to the concerned District Manager or Corporation office for verification. Step 3: After approval, the application is forwarded to the HP SC/ST Development Corporation for further processing.

page_content:
# Application for Subsidy on Winning International Award **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Artists, Film, Actor, Award | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The application for "Winning International Award" service has been introduced under the Chhattisgarh Film Policy, 2021 by the Culture and Archaeology Department, Government of Chhattisgarh to recognize and encourage film projects that achieve excellence and receive awards at internationally recognized film festivals or platforms. The service enables eligible applicants to apply online for subsidy by submitting details of the award along with the prescribed supporting documents for verification. It aims to promote high-quality filmmaking, encourage global recognition of films associated with Chhattisgarh, and provide financial incentives to filmmakers whose achievements enhance the state's reputation in the international film industry.
## Benefits - Financial assistance of up to ₹5.00 crore. - Assistance is provided for one award category only and can be availed only once in a year.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant can claim assistance only once in a financial year and for only one award category. The award is available for films that achieve outstanding excellence in categories such as: - Best Film - Best Director - Best Actor - Best Actress - Films promoting National Integration - Films conveying Social Messages - Other recognized award categories as determined by the Government.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Application Process** **Step 1: Portal Access and Login** The applicant (or the authorized operator) must visit the [Sewa Setu Portal](https://sewasetu.cgstate.gov.in/home?lang=en), and login using either their Citizen credentials or through the Lok Sewa Kendra (LSK) login system to proceed with the application. **Step 2: Application Submission** The user must navigate to the application form of the scheme that they wish to apply for. In the form, enter all the required details accurately. In the form, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload all the mandatory documents in the specified format and size. Ensure that all documents are clear, legible, and in the accepted file format before uploading. Once all required documents are successfully uploaded and the entered information is verified by the applicant, they must finally submit the application. **Step 3: Application Reference Number Generation** The portal generates an Application Reference Number (ARN). The applicant should save the ARN for all future correspondence and status tracking regarding their submitted application. > **Post-Application Process** **Step 1: Preliminary Verification by Film Facilitation Cell** The application is received online by the Film Facilitation Cell, where the submitted application details and supporting documents are examined for completeness and correctness. If any discrepancies are found, the application is returned to the applicant for necessary corrections. **Step 2: Approval process by Film Facilitation Cell** Based on the verification: If the application is found satisfactory, it is forwarded to the Deputy Director for further examination. If any discrepancies or deficiencies are identified, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application is found ineligible, it may be rejected with recorded remarks. **Step 3: Examination by Deputy Director** The Deputy Director reviews the application, committee recommendations, and all supporting documents to assess eligibility and compliance with the applicable guidelines. **Step 4: Approval process by Deputy Director** Based on the examination, the Deputy Director may forward the application with recommendation to the Director for approval. If any required document is incomplete, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application is found ineligible, it is rejected with suitable remarks. **Step 5: Review by Director** The Director scrutinizes the application, recommendations, and supporting documents to ensure that all requirements have been fulfilled and that the case is suitable for approval. **Step 6: Final Decision by Director** Based on the review: If approved, the Director applies the Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) through the system. If additional information or documents are required, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application does not meet the prescribed criteria, it is rejected with remarks. **Step 7: Generation of Digitally Signed Sanction Order** Upon approval, a Digitally Signed Sanction Order is generated through the system using the Director's Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). **Step 8: Issuance of Sanction Order** The approved Digitally Signed Sanction Order is issued and made available to the applicant through the system. **Step 9: Disbursement of Subsidy through DBT** After issuance of the Sanction Order, the approved subsidy amount is processed through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism and transferred to the beneficiary's registered bank account. **Step 10: Application Closure** After successful issuance of the Sanction Order and completion of all processing formalities, the application status is updated as Completed and the case is formally closed.

metadata.schemeName: Bee-Keeping
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote bee-keeping by providing subsidy on the purchase of bee colonies and bee-keeping boxes to farmers and bee-keepers, thereby encouraging honey production and improving income.

page_content:
# Bee-Keeping **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Bee Keeping, Apiculture, Horticulture Department, Bee Colony Subsidy, Farmer, Honey Production, Beekeeping Box | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Bee-Keeping" scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Horticulture Department, Government of Rajasthan, with 60% funding from the Central Government and 40% funding from the State Government, and aims to promote bee-keeping through subsidy assistance for purchasing bee colonies and bee-keeping boxes for farmers and bee-keepers. The scheme provides a subsidy on eligible costs for bee colonies and boxes, subject to prescribed limits. A maximum of 50 bee colonies and 50 bee-keeping boxes can be subsidized for each beneficiary. Preference is given to small and marginal farmers, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, women farmers, and trained beekeepers. Subsidy is released after verification through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
## Benefits > **Subsidy on Bee Colony:** - Subsidy of 40% of the cost of one bee colony or ₹800/- per colony, whichever is lower. - The reference cost of one 8-frame bee colony is ₹2,000/-. > **Subsidy on Bee-Keeping Box:** - Subsidy of 40% of the cost of one bee-keeping box or ₹800/- per box, whichever is lower. - The reference cost of one bee-keeping box is ₹2,000/-. > **Maximum Assistance:** - Subsidy is available for a maximum of 50 bee colonies per beneficiary. - Subsidy is available for a maximum of 50 bee-keeping boxes per beneficiary.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a farmer.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online - via CSC - **Mode of Application:** Online - **Mode of Online Application:** E-Mitra - Applicants can apply by visiting their nearest [E-Mitra](https://reportsemitraapp.rajasthan.gov.in/WebSrc/Reports/rpt_search_new_emitra_ksk.jsp) center or online through their own E-Mitra account. > **Note:** Applying for "Bee-Keeping" is free.

metadata.schemeName: National Horticulture Mission-Protected Cultivation
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote protected cultivation of horticultural crops by providing subsidy for the establishment of Green Houses, Shade Net Houses, Plastic Mulching, Low Tunnels, Anti Bird Nets, and cultivation of high-value vegetables and flowers under protected structures.

page_content:
# National Horticulture Mission-Protected Cultivation **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Protected Cultivation, National Horticulture Mission, Green House, Poly House, Shade Net House, Plastic Mulching, Flower Cultivation | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "National Horticulture Mission-Protected Cultivation" is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Horticulture Department with 60% Central Government funding and 40% State Government funding. The scheme aims to promote protected cultivation by providing subsidies for Green Houses, Shade Net Houses, Plastic Mulching, Low Tunnels, Anti Bird Nets, and planting materials for high-value vegetables and flowers. It supports farmers in controlling climatic factors such as temperature, humidity, and sunlight for improved horticultural production. The assistance is provided according to prescribed unit costs and scheme guidelines through online application and verification. The scheme is meant for individual farmers and eligible beneficiaries undertaking protected cultivation activities.
## Benefits > **Greenhouse & Shade Net House Provisions:** - **Financial Subsidy:** Generous financial assistance to set up standard-compliant protected cultivation structures.- **Generous Area Coverage:** Subsidy allocation covering a substantial area of up to 4,000 square meters per beneficiary.- **Flexible Funding Options:** Complete freedom to self-fund or access facilitated bank loans through an official Letter of Intent (LOI).- **Payment Security:** Secure payment release to empanelled construction firms only after the materials arrive and the farmer provides written approval.- **On-Site Technical Support:** Continuous, free on-field technical assistance and troubleshooting by local Agriculture Supervisors and Officers. > 2. **Plastic Mulching Incentives:** - **Standard Cost Rebate:** A 50% cost subsidy up to ₹16,000/- per hectare for general category farmers to boost weed control and water conservation.- **Enhanced Smallholder Support:** An upgraded 75% subsidy up to ₹24,000/- per hectare specifically for Small and Marginal farmers.- **Top-Up Funding:** Additional financial top-ups provided directly through the Mukhyamantri Krishak Saathi Yojana.- **Broad Land Coverage:** Financial assistance extending up to a maximum of 2 hectares per individual beneficiary. > **3. Plastic Low Tunnel Incentives:** - **Frost Protection Subsidy:** A 50% financial subsidy on an estimated cost of ₹60/- per square meter to protect crops from extreme winter weather.- **Premium Budget Upgrades:** An increased subsidy of 75% and an expanded area allowance of up to 4,000 square meters for Small/Marginal farmers.- **Automated Payouts:** Direct, hassle-free financial transfers executed straight into the farmer's bank account via automated DBT channels. > **4. Anti-Bird Net Incentives** - **Crop Protection Funding:** A 50% subsidy based on a unit cost of ₹35/- per square meter to prevent bird damage and safeguard crop yield.- **Large Area Allocation:** Financial coverage stretching up to a maximum limit of 5,000 square meters per beneficiary. > **5. High-Value Crops & Planting Material Provisions:** - **Cultivation Cost Rebate:** A 50% financial subsidy on the procurement of high-value vegetable seeds and premium flower saplings (Roses, Gerberas, Carnations, and Lilium).- **High-Ceiling Cost Coverage:** Financial assistance caps modeled on premium market rates (up to ₹140/sqm for vegetables and up to ₹610/sqm for premium flowers) for up to 4,000 square meters.- **Certified Quality Assurance:** Access to high-quality, genetically pure, and climate-resilient saplings from verified government nurseries and agricultural universities.- **Free Package of Practices (PoP):** Mandatory step-by-step crop management guides and technical booklets provided directly by the supplying agency.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a farmer.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online - via CSC **Step 1:** Visit the [official website](https://rajkisan.rajasthan.gov.in/rajkisanweb/login/2#searchmenu). **Step 2:** Click on "Login using SSO ID" or "Login using Jan Aadhaar ID". **Step 3:** Complete the online application form for the scheme. **Step 4:** Upload the required supporting documents. **Step 5:** Submit the application online. **Step 6:** The competent committee will verify the site suitability and documents. **Step 7:** After approval, the beneficiary may undertake construction according to prescribed standards. **Step 8:** Physical verification will be conducted after completion of the work. **Step 9:** Eligible subsidy will be released through DBT as per the prescribed installment pattern. > **Contact Us:** - [District Office](https://agriculture.rajasthan.gov.in/dam/#/sm/jankalyan-category-and-entry-type/372028/7/3/14). - [Regional Office](https://agriculture.rajasthan.gov.in/dam/#/sm/jankalyan-category-and-entry-type/372027/7/3/13).

metadata.schemeName: National Horticulture Mission - Mechanization in Horticulture
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to reduce the cost of horticulture crop production and increase productivity by providing subsidy on horticulture machinery and power-operated equipment to eligible farmers and farmer groups.

page_content:
# National Horticulture Mission - Mechanization in Horticulture **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** National Horticulture Mission, Mechanization, Horticulture, Tractor Subsidy, Power Tiller Subsidy, Rotavator, Plastic Mulch Laying Machine | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The National Horticulture Mission-Mechanization in Horticulture is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Horticulture Department, Government of Rajasthan with 60% Central Government and 40% State Government funding. The scheme aims to reduce the cost of horticulture crop production and increase productivity through financial assistance for purchasing horticulture machinery and power-operated equipment. The scheme benefits farmers, producer organizations, farmer groups, self-help groups, and women farmer groups engaged in horticulture cultivation. Subsidy is provided on eligible machinery as per the prescribed rates and conditions under the scheme. Applications are submitted online through E-Mitra and subsidy is released after verification through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
## Benefits > **Tractor (Up to 20 PTO HP) with Rotavator/Equipment:** - General Farmers: 25% of the cost, up to ₹75,000/- per equipment. - Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Small and Marginal Farmers, and Women Farmers: 35% of the cost, up to ₹1,00,000/- per equipment. - Maximum admissible equipment cost: ₹3,00,000/-. > **Power Tiller (Below 8 BHP):** - General Farmers: Up to ₹40,000/- per equipment. - Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Small and Marginal Farmers, and Women Farmers: Up to ₹50,000/- per equipment. - Maximum admissible equipment cost: ₹1,00,000/-. > **Power Tiller (8 BHP and Above):** - General Farmers: Up to ₹60,000/- per equipment. - Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Small and Marginal Farmers, and Women Farmers: Up to ₹75,000/- per equipment. - Maximum admissible equipment cost: ₹1,50,000/-. > **Land Development, Tillage and Seed Bed Preparation Equipment (Up to 20 BHP):** - General Farmers: Up to ₹12,000/- per equipment. - Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Small and Marginal Farmers, and Women Farmers: Up to ₹15,000/- per equipment. - Maximum admissible equipment cost: ₹30,000/-. > **Sowing, Planting and Digging Equipment:** - General Farmers: Up to ₹12,000/- per equipment. - Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Small and Marginal Farmers, and Women Farmers: Up to ₹15,000/- per equipment. - Maximum admissible equipment cost: ₹30,000/-. > **Plastic Mulch Laying Machine:** - General Farmers: Up to ₹28,000/- per equipment. - Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Small and Marginal Farmers, and Women Farmers: Up to ₹35,000/- per equipment. - Maximum admissible equipment cost: ₹70,000/-. > **Automatic Horticulture Machinery:** - General Farmers: Up to ₹1,00,000/- per equipment. - Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Small and Marginal Farmers, and Women Farmers: Up to ₹1,25,000/- per equipment. - Maximum admissible equipment cost: ₹2,50,000/-. > **Tractor Mounted/Operated Sprayer (Above 35 BHP)/Electrostatic Sprayer:** - General Farmers: 40% of the cost, up to ₹50,000/- per equipment. - Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Small and Marginal Farmers, and Women Farmers: 50% of the cost, up to ₹63,000/- per equipment. - Maximum admissible equipment cost: ₹1,26,000/-.
## Eligibility Criteria > The following categories of citizens are eligible for Mechanization in horticulture under National Horticulture Mission: - Farmers.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online - via CSC - **Mode of Application:** Online - **Mode of Online Application:** E-Mitra - Applicants can apply by visiting their nearest [E-Mitra](https://reportsemitraapp.rajasthan.gov.in/WebSrc/Reports/rpt_search_new_emitra_ksk.jsp) center or online through their own E-Mitra account. > **Note:** Applying for "National Horticulture Mission - Mechanization in Horticulture" is free.

metadata.schemeName: National Horticulture Mission - Production of Planting Material
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote the production of quality planting material by providing financial assistance for the establishment of high-tech nurseries, small nurseries, and tissue culture units to eligible beneficiaries under the National Horticulture Mission.

page_content:
# National Horticulture Mission - Production of Planting Material **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** National Horticulture Mission, Planting Material, High Tech Nursery, Tissue Culture Unit, Horticulture Department, Fruit Plants, Greenhouse | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "National Horticulture Mission-Production of Planting Material" is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Horticulture Department, with 60% funding from the Central Government and 40% funding from the State Government, aiming to enhance the production capacity and quality of planting material through financial assistance for establishing nurseries and tissue culture units for eligible beneficiaries. The scheme supports the establishment of high-tech nurseries, small nurseries, and tissue culture units with credit-linked back-ended subsidies as per prescribed norms. It promotes the production of high-quality fruit planting material through vegetative propagation and the development of necessary nursery infrastructure. The scheme also requires compliance with accreditation and technical standards for maintaining quality planting material production.
## Benefits > **High-Tech Nursery Subsidy:** Financial assistance of 40% of the project cost, subject to a maximum of ₹10,00,000/- per hectare. Maximum subsidy of ₹40,00,000/- for up to 4 hectares. Assistance is provided as a credit-linked back-ended subsidy. > **High-Tech Nursery Cost Norm:** Standard project cost is ₹25,00,000/- per hectare. A beneficiary can establish a nursery on a maximum area of 4 hectares. > **Small Nursery Subsidy:** - Financial assistance of 50% of the project cost. - Maximum subsidy of ₹7,50,000/- for 1 hectare. - Assistance is provided as a credit-linked back-ended subsidy. > **Small Nursery Cost Norm:** - Standard project cost is ₹15,00,000/- per hectare. - Assistance is available for a maximum of 1 hectare. > **Strengthening of Tissue Culture Units:** - Standard cost is ₹20,00,000/- per unit. - Public sector receives 100% of the project cost. - Private sector receives 50% of the project cost as a credit-linked back-ended subsidy. > **Establishment of New Tissue Culture Units:** - Standard project cost is ₹2,50,00,000/- per unit. - Public sector receives 100% of the project cost. - Private sector receives 40% of the project cost as a credit-linked back-ended subsidy. > **Production Requirement:** - High-tech nurseries must produce 50,000 quality fruit plants per hectare per year through vegetative propagation. - Small nurseries must produce 25,000 quality fruit plants per hectare per year through vegetative propagation. - Tissue culture units must produce a minimum of 25,00,000 plants per year for commercial use.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a farmer/ farmer group/ a government institution.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online - via CSC - **Mode of Application:** Online - **Mode of Online Application:** E-Mitra - Applicants can apply by visiting their nearest [E-Mitra](https://reportsemitraapp.rajasthan.gov.in/WebSrc/Reports/rpt_search_new_emitra_ksk.jsp) center or online through their own E-Mitra account. > **Note:** Applying for "National Horticulture Mission-Production of Planting Material" is free.

page_content:
# Promotion of Integrated Pest/Nutrient Management **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Integrated Pest Management, Integrated Nutrient Management, Farmer, Subsidy, Bio-Pesticides | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Promotion of Integrated Pest/Nutrient Management" is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Horticulture Department, Government of Rajasthan, with 60% Central Government funding and 40% State Government funding, and aims to promote Integrated Pest Management and Integrated Nutrient Management through subsidy support to farmers. The scheme provides financial assistance for adopting approved IPM/INM practices in horticulture crops. Subsidy is available for eligible bio-pesticides and pest management inputs under the recommended modules. The programme is implemented according to prescribed IPM recommendations and region-specific scientific recommendations wherever applicable. The subsidy is released through RTGS or, in specified cases, to the supplying agency.
## Benefits > **Subsidy:** - Subsidy of 30% of the cost, subject to a maximum of ₹1,200/- per hectare. - Subsidy is available for a maximum area of 4 hectares per beneficiary. - A farmer is eligible for assistance under Integrated Pest Management and Integrated Nutrient Management; however, the subsidy shall not exceed ₹1,200/- per hectare. > **Eligible Inputs** **Subsidy is available for approved IPM inputs such as:** - Bacillus thuringiensis - Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus (NPV) - Trichocards - Trichoderma - Neem-based pesticides - Pheromone traps - Light traps - Other approved bio-pesticides under the IPM module
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a farmer.
## Exclusions

metadata.schemeName: State Art Exhibition-Artist Category
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme "State Art Exhibition (Artist Category)" is a State Promotional scheme by the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. This scheme is organized as a promotional initiative to encourage and showcase the talents of local artists in the field of Fine Arts in Goa.

page_content:
# State Art Exhibition-Artist Category **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Goa | **Categories:** Sports & Culture, Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Art Exhibition, Financial Support, Graphic Design, Artists | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme “State Art Exhibition (Artist Category)” is a State Promotional Scheme implemented by the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. The scheme is organised as a promotional initiative to encourage and showcase the talents of local artists in the field of Fine Arts in Goa. The exhibition provides a platform for visual artists to present their artworks and gain public recognition.
**The exhibition will be conducted in three sections, namely:** 1. Painting & Graphic Print 1. Applied Art 1. Sculpture
For participation, the entry form along with the rules and regulations (Prospectus) will be made available at Kala Academy. The dates for receiving entries will be announced through local daily newspapers. A non-refundable admission fee of ₹100/- per section will be charged. An artist may participate in more than one section; however, a separate entry fee is required for each section. For selection and judging, Kala Academy will appoint a panel of three judges to evaluate and select the artworks.
## Benefits - Three Best Awards of ₹20,000/- each will be awarded in each section of the exhibition.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant should be a local artist of Goa working in the field of Fine Arts. - The applicant should submit original artwork created by the applicant and not previously awarded.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The interested applicant should visit the Kala Academy, Goa, and request a hard copy of the prescribed format of the application form from the [**Office of Tiatr Academy of Goa**](https://www.goa.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/3RD-ALL-GOA.pdf#:~:text=Detailed%20Rules%20and%20Regulations%20of%20the%20competition%2C,is%20June%206%2C%202025%20during%20office%20hours.), Block A, 2nd Floor, Campal Trade Centre, Campal, Panaji, Goa. **Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required). **Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents, within the prescribed period (if any), to the academy staff.

page_content:
# Literary Award **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Goa | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Award, Programme, Academy, Culture | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Literary Award", organised by the Kala Academy under the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa, aims to encourage Goan Konkani and Marathi writers for their creative literary contributions. Entries are invited through press notes released in local dailies, and submitted books are placed before the Advisory Committee for their recommendation and selection.
## Benefits The award includes ₹10,000/- along with a memento and certificate, presented at a special function.

page_content:
# Mizoram Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (MBOCWWB): Benefits for Members' Children **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Mizoram | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Construction Workers, Educational Assistance, Congratulatory Grant, Educational Assistance | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme “Benefits for Members' Children” under the "Mizoram Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board Benefits for Workers" is implemented by the Mizoram Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Government of Mizoram, aims to provide welfare benefits to eligible construction workers and their children. The Board has been constituted under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996, and a Welfare Fund has been established. Eligible construction workers between 18 and 60 years of age who have worked for not less than 90 days in a year may apply for membership. Registered members with at least 1 year of continuous registration may receive annual educational assistance for up to 2 children. The educational assistance is transferred directly to the beneficiaries' accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
## Benefits > **Educational Assistance for Members' Children:** - **KG-I to Class VIII:** ₹4,000/- per child annually. - **Class IX to Class XII:** ₹5,000/- per child annually. - **Undergraduate Students:** ₹6,000/- per child annually. - **Industrial Training Institute/Polytechnic Diploma Course Students:** ₹6,000/- per child annually. - **Professional & Technical Degree Course Students:** ₹20,000/- per child annually. - **Research Scholars/Post-Graduate Level Students:** ₹20,000/- per child annually. - **Number of Children:** Educational assistance is available for up to 2 children of a member who has held continuous registration for at least 1 year. > **Congratulatory Grant:** - **Top 10 in Board Examinations:** ₹50,000/- each for up to 2 children securing a position within the Top 10 in HSLC, HSSLC, and CBSE examinations. - **Distinction:** ₹20,000/- each for up to 2 children securing Distinction in HSLC, HSSLC, and CBSE examinations.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be an Indian citizen. - The applicant must be between 18 and 60 years of age. - The applicant must have been engaged as a construction worker for at least 90 days in a year. - The applicant must be engaged as a contractor or employee in one of the covered categories of construction work. > **Contractors or employees engaged in the following categories of work:** 1. Carpenter 2. Mason 3. Cement Mason 4. Painter 5. Helper (Construction Works) 6. Electrician 7. Wireman 8. Fitter 9. Welder 10. Plumber 11. Iron and Aluminium Worker 12. Blacksmith 13. Lumberjack 14. Sand Extraction Worker 15. Stone Quarry Worker 16. Stone Breaker 17. Road and Earthwork Labourer 18. JCB/Dozer Operator 19. Construction Machine Operator 20. Construction Driver 21. Brick Factory Worker > **Membership Fee:** - A one-time Registration Fee of ₹25/- shall be payable at the time of enrolment. - A monthly subscription of ₹10/- is payable to maintain active membership. Alternatively, an advance payment of ₹120/- may be made to cover one year's subscription. - Members wishing to pay the Membership/Renewal Fee in advance may do so for a period of up to three (3) years. - Membership must be renewed within one (1) year from the date of expiry, in accordance with [Section 17 of the BOCW (RE&CS) Act, 1996](https://lesde.mizoram.gov.in/uploads/attachments/2024/05/bbadc4155d1796a962f3883e14e4cc9c/pages-145-bocw-recs-act-1996.pdf).
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** Eligible registered members of the Welfare Board may apply for the respective welfare schemes by submitting the prescribed scheme-specific application form, duly filled in and accompanied by the requisite supporting documents, through the prescribed offline mode. **Step 2:** The application forms and supporting documents shall be as specified by the Welfare Board for the respective scheme/benefit. - **Application Form for Registration under the Board**: [Click here](https://bocw.mizoram.gov.in/uploads/attachments/2023/06/70c9592db154bfccb04514f40e9b5ea8/pages-103-registration-form.pdf).- **Application Form for Educational Assistance**: [Click here](https://bocw.mizoram.gov.in/uploads/attachments/2025/04/68aec1e763c73dc3fde14e8cde2379a0/pages-103-cea-7th-amendment.pdf). > **Contact Us:** [Click here](https://bocw.mizoram.gov.in/page/whom-to-contact).

metadata.schemeName: Promotion of Intensive Aquaculture through Introduction of Bio-floc Technology
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote sustainable intensification of the freshwater fish and brackish water shrimp farming for boosting productivity and generating high income in a limited area & subsidy assistance is provided to farmers, hatchery operators, private entrepreneurs, and unemployed youth.

page_content:
# Promotion of Intensive Aquaculture through Introduction of Bio-floc Technology **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Odisha | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Bio-floc Technology, DBT, Intensive Aquaculture, Fish & Shrimp Farming, Back-ended Subsidy | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme "Promotion of Intensive Aquaculture through Introduction of Bio-floc Technology" was launched by the Fisheries & Animal Resources Development Department, Government of Odisha. It aims to promote sustainable intensification of the freshwater fish and brackish water shrimp farming for boosting productivity and generating high income in a limited area. Through this scheme, subsidy assistance at 40% of the unit cost for the General Category and at 60% of the Unit Cost for the SC / ST / Women Category is provided to farmers interested in taking up grow-out tanks, nursery and seed tanks; fish and shrimp hatchery operators; private entrepreneurs; and unemployed youth. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Fisheries through District Fisheries Officers and the field functionaries under the supervision of the Zonal Deputy Director of Fisheries. The total outlay under the said programme is Rs.2525.00 lakh. During the current year, 5000 nos. of Bio-floc tanks will be developed under this programme with subsidy support under the state plan. Subsidy amount shall be released to Aadhaar linked Bank Account of the beneficiary in two phases. The beneficiary shall construct the Bio-floc unit as per the minimum design and specification shown in the tables in the guideline pdf. > **Objectives** 1. To promote high-yielding intensive fish farming in a small area using Bio-floc technology. 1. To encourage farmers, entrepreneurs, and unemployed youth into income generation through the small-scale Bio-floc farming system.
## Benefits > **Subsidy Assistance** 1. Subsidy assistance is provided at 40% of the unit cost for the General Category and at 60% of the Unit Cost for the Scheduled Caste (SC) / Scheduled Tribe (ST) / Women Category. 1. Financial assistance is provided in the form of a back-ended subsidy. 1. The assistance under the special package is available for a minimum of 2 tanks and a maximum of 6 tanks. 1. If a beneficiary has availed a subsidy earlier for the installation of a Bio-floc unit under different schemes of the Government of India and State Government for less than 6 tanks, he/she shall also be eligible to avail further subsidy under this scheme. However, in such cases, the subsidy shall be limited to a maximum of 6 tanks, including the installation of tanks earlier. 1. The total outlay under the said programme is ₹2525.00 lakh. > **Model-Wise Unit Cost and Subsidy:** - Under the PVC / Tarpaulin model, the unit cost for Two Tanks is ₹1.50/- lakh with a subsidy of ₹60,000/- for the General Category and ₹90,000/- for the SC / ST / Women Category. For Four Tanks, the unit cost is ₹3.00/- lakh with a subsidy of ₹1,20,000/- for the General Category and ₹1,80,000/- for SC / ST / Women Category. For Six Tanks, the unit cost is ₹4.00/- lakh with a subsidy of ₹1,60,000/- for the General Category and ₹2,40,000/- for SC / ST / Women Category. - Under the Brick Masonry model, the unit cost for Two Tanks is ₹2.00/- lakh with a subsidy of ₹80,000/- for the General Category and ₹1,20,000/- for the SC / ST / Women Category. For Four Tanks, the unit cost is ₹4.00/- lakh with a subsidy of ₹1,60,000/- for the General Category and ₹2,40,000/- for SC / ST / Women Category. For Six Tanks, the unit cost is ₹6.00/- lakh with a subsidy of ₹2,40,000/- for the General Category and ₹3,60,000/- for SC / ST / Women Category. > **Component-Wise Assistance (Two Tanks – 30 Cubic Meter Capacity)** - **PVC / Tarpaulin Model** 1. For two tanks of 30 cubic meter capacity, the Bio-floc Tank (PVC / Tarpaulin / Polyliner with frames, solid base, drain pipe, and fish net covering) has a unit cost of ₹40,000/- with a subsidy of ₹16,000/- at 40% and ₹24,000/- at 60%. 1. The Green House Shed with Entry Door, including installation costs (GI Frames covered with shade net; Floor area 50 square meters; Height 3 meters; Specification & Drawing in Annexure-I) has a unit cost of ₹60,000/- with a subsidy of ₹24,000/- at 40% and ₹36,000/- at 60%. 1. The Electric Water Pump (0.5 Horse Power) has a unit cost of ₹4,000/- with a subsidy of ₹1,600/- at 40% and ₹2,400/- at 60%. 1. The Ring Blower / High-Pressure Air Pump has a unit cost of ₹20,000/- with a subsidy of ₹8,000/- at 40% and ₹12,000/- at 60%. 1. The Electronic Weighing Balance has a unit cost of ₹1,000/- with a subsidy of ₹400/- at 40% and ₹600/- at 60%. 1. The Uninterrupted Power Supply Unit with Inverter (1100 Volt Ampere) and Battery (150 Ampere Hour) or Portable Genset (1 Kilowatt) has a unit cost of ₹25,000/- with a subsidy of ₹10,000/- at 40% and ₹15,000/- at 60%. 1. The grand total unit cost for this model is ₹1,50,000/- with a subsidy of ₹60,000/- at 40% and ₹90,000/- at 60%. - **Brick Masonry Model (30 Cubic Meter Capacity)** 1. For two tanks of 30 cubic meter capacity, the Bio-floc Tank (Brick Masonry Tanks with frames, solid base, drain pipe, and fish net covering) has a unit cost of ₹90,000/- with a subsidy of ₹36,000/- at 40% and ₹54,000/- at 60%. 1. The Green House Shed with Entry Door, including installation costs, has a unit cost of ₹60,000/- with a subsidy of ₹24,000/- at 40% and ₹36,000/- at 60%. 1. The Electric Water Pump (0.5 Horse Power) has a unit cost of ₹4,000/- with a subsidy of ₹1,600/- at 40% and ₹2,400/- at 60%. 1. The Ring Blower / High-Pressure Air Pump has a unit cost of ₹20,000/- with a subsidy of ₹8,000/- at 40% and ₹12,000/- at 60%. 1. The Electronic Weighing Balance has a unit cost of ₹1,000/- with a subsidy of ₹400/- at 40% and ₹600/- at 60%. 1. The Uninterrupted Power Supply Unit with Inverter (1100 Volt Ampere) and Battery (150 Ampere Hour) or Portable Genset (1 Kilowatt) has a unit cost of ₹25,000/- with a subsidy of ₹10,000/- at 40% and ₹15,000/- at 60%. 1. The grand total unit cost for this model is ₹2,00,000/- with a subsidy of ₹80,000/- at 40% and ₹1,20,000/- at 60%. > **Disbursement of Funds:** 1. Subsidy amount shall be released to Aadhaar linked Bank Account of the beneficiary through Direct Benefit Transfer. 1. Subsidy shall be released in two phases. - 40% of the subsidy shall be released after the installation of the Bio-floc unit. - Rest 60% back-ended subsidy shall be released after completion of the project. > **Note - Conditions Linked to Benefits:** 1. The beneficiary shall construct the Bio-floc unit as per the minimum design and specification shown in the tables in the guidelines. 1. Only items mentioned in the unit cost, namely tarpaulin / PVC Tanks, Blower, Water Pump, Genset, and Shed, are eligible under subsidy upon submission of actual GST bills for those items.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must be a resident/domicile of the state of Odisha. 1. The applicant shall be a farmer interested in taking up grow-out tanks, nursery, and seed tanks. 1. The applicant shall be a fish and shrimp hatchery operator. 1. The applicant shall be a private entrepreneur. 1. The applicant shall be an unemployed educated youth. 1. The eligible brackish water shrimp farms/nurseries and seed tanks/hatchery beneficiaries must have a license from the Coastal Aquaculture Authority. 1. The assistance under the special package shall be available to the above categories of beneficiaries with a minimum of 2 tanks and a maximum of 6 tanks. 1. If a beneficiary has availed a subsidy earlier for the installation of a Bio-floc unit under different schemes of the Government of India and State Government, for less than 6 nos. of tanks, he/she shall also be eligible to avail further subsidy under this scheme. However, in such cases, the subsidy shall be limited to a maximum of 6 tanks, which will include the installation of tanks earlier. > **Preference / Priority / Reservation** - Priority will be given to unemployed educated youth since Bio-floc farming involves advanced technology, and the beneficiary has to undergo specialized training on Bio-floc systems before operation of the unit.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The scheme shall be advertised through the Departmental website, newspapers, and wall posters in the District and Block Fisheries Offices across the State. The Director of Fisheries shall undertake wide publicity of the scheme. **Step 2:** Interested farmers (Grow-Out Tanks, Nursery and Seed Tanks); fish and shrimp hatchery operators; private entrepreneurs; unemployed youth shall apply in the prescribed format as specified in [Annexure-I](https://fard.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-03/6.%20Subsidy%20for%20Intensive%20Shrimp%20%26%20Fish%20Farming%20through%20Bio-Floc%20Technology_0.pdf) and submit the filled-in application form along with the required documents to the respective District Fisheries Officer through hardcopy or through email. The applications can also be submitted online to the Directorate of Fisheries, Odisha, Cuttack, through email - director.odifish.inland@gmail.com. Identification of beneficiaries shall be made with Aadhaar linking at the time of submission of the application. **Step 3:** The applications received by the Directorate of Fisheries, Cuttack, through e-mail shall be forwarded to the respective District Fisheries Officers for necessary action. The District Fisheries Officer, on receipt of the applications, shall forward them to the concerned Assistant Fisheries Officer for necessary site inspection. The initial geo-tagged photographs of the site/fish farm, along with the beneficiary and field verification report, shall be prepared by the Assistant Fisheries Officer and submitted to the District Fisheries Officer as per the format enclosed at Annexure-II. The Assistant Fisheries Officer shall ensure that the project proposed by the beneficiary is completely new. **Step 4:** Each beneficiary shall select two persons, including him/her, for undergoing training on Bio-floc technology, and the list of trainees shall be submitted to the District Fisheries Officer. The District Fisheries Officer shall submit the list of such trainees to the Directorate of Fisheries before issue ofthe Go-Ahead to the beneficiary. The Directorate of Fisheries shall organize the training on Bio-floc technology for the beneficiaries nominated by the District Fisheries Officers at the Zonal Level. **Step 5:** The District Fisheries Officer shall issue a Go-Ahead letter to the selected beneficiaries to take up the Bio-floc farm unit installation based on the feasibility report of the Assistant Fisheries Officer. **Step 6:** The beneficiary shall install the Bio-floc farm unit as per the approved design and complete the stocking of fish/shrimp seed. The beneficiary shall inform the concerned Assistant Fisheries Officer upon completion of the unit. **Step 7:** A District Level Inspection Team comprising the District Fisheries Officer, Assistant Fisheries Officer / SFTA / JFTA I/C of the Block and Panchayat Extension Officer shall undertake joint field inspection of the site. Geo-tagged post-installation photographs of the Bio-floc units, along with the beneficiary, shall be taken upon completion of installation and stocking. The beneficiaries shall submit the GST bills/receipts towards the installation of the Bio-floc unit. Only items mentioned in the unit cost are eligible under the subsidy upon submission of actual GST bills for those items. **Step 8:** The District Fisheries Officer shall release the subsidy to the beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer to the Aadhaar-linked Bank Account only on the eligible items in the Bio-floc units after proper verification of the GST bills/receipts. > **Note (Annexures):** 1. [Annexure-I contains the prescribed Application Form format to be used by the applicant, given in the guidelines pdf.](https://fard.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-03/6.%20Subsidy%20for%20Intensive%20Shrimp%20%26%20Fish%20Farming%20through%20Bio-Floc%20Technology_0.pdf) 1. Annexure-II contains the format for the field verification report and geo-tagged photographs to be submitted by the Assistant Fisheries Officer. 1. Specification & Drawing for Green House Shed are provided in Annexure-I.
