metadata.schemeName: Nagaland Government Ex-Gratia Scheme for Students Studying Outside Nagaland
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to provide Ex-Gratia in the event of the death of students studying outside Nagaland. Through this scheme, financial assistance is provided to the nominee of the deceased student.

page_content:
# Nagaland Government Ex-Gratia Scheme for Students Studying Outside Nagaland **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Nagaland | **Categories:** Health & Wellness, Education & Learning | **Tags:** Ex-Gratia, Scheduled Tribes, Students Studying Outside Nagaland, Death Coverage | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme "Nagaland Government Ex-Gratia Scheme for Students Studying Outside Nagaland (NGESSO)" was launched by the Department of Higher Education, Government of Nagaland. It aims to provide Ex-Gratia in the event of the death of students studying outside Nagaland. Through this scheme, an amount of ₹5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakh) only is provided to the nominee of the deceased student. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Higher Education, Nagaland. The scheme covers death cases only. The Nominee can claim the Ex-Gratia amount within a period of 2 (two) months after the death of the student by furnishing the prescribed documents. Students studying outside Nagaland are required to register their names through forms issued by the Office of the Directorate of Higher Education. All registered students must renew their registration manually every academic year (annually).
## Benefits > **Ex-Gratia Amount** An amount of ₹**5,00,000**/- only is provided under the scheme. The scheme covers death cases only. The Nominee can claim the Ex-Gratia amount within a period of 2 (two) months after the death of the student by furnishing the prescribed documents. > **Mode of Disbursement** For claiming the Ex-Gratia amount, the Nominee shall submit his/her Bank Account Number, Name, and Address of the Bank, IFSC of the bank, supported by a photocopy of the front page of the Bank Pass Book. > **Frequency of Disbursement** The Ex-Gratia amount of ₹5,00,000/- is payable in death cases only. > **Expected Time of Disbursement** The Nominee can claim the Ex-Gratia amount within a period of 2 (two) months after the death of the student. > **Validity Period** Students studying outside Nagaland will be allowed to register their names by applying through the forms issued by the Office of the Directorate of Higher Education, Nagaland: Kohima, and Registration forms are to be submitted within the stipulated time period. It shall be mandatory for all the registered students to renew their registration manually every academic year (annually).
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must belong to any recognised Scheduled Tribes / Indigenous inhabitants of Nagaland State only. 1. The applicant must be admitted to a regular course with a minimum duration of 1 year in any recognised institution outside the State of Nagaland, but within India only. 1. The applicant must be pursuing studies from the primary level to Post Doctoral Courses. 1. The applicant must be pursuing studies in a Secular / Technical / Professional / Diploma / Theology / course, etc. 1. The applicant must have registered their names and details under the Office of the Directorate of Higher Education, Government of Nagaland. 1. The applicant must have nominated the name and details of their nominee for claims under the Ex-Gratia Scheme during registration. 1. The applicant’s death must have occurred outside Nagaland.
## Exclusions 1. Students residing in Nagaland and pursuing correspondence/distance education courses outside the State are not eligible.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Step 1:** Students studying outside Nagaland shall download the Registration Form ([**Annexure-A**](https://highereducation.nagaland.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/FRESH25.pdf)) from: [https://highereducation.nagaland.gov.in/nagaland-government-ex-gratia-scheme-for-students-studying-outside-nagaland-ngesso/](https://highereducation.nagaland.gov.in/nagaland-government-ex-gratia-scheme-for-students-studying-outside-nagaland-ngesso/) or obtain the form issued by the Office of the Directorate of Higher Education, Nagaland. **Step 2:** The student must fill out the Registration Form [(**Annexure-A**, 2025–26)](https://highereducation.nagaland.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/FRESH25.pdf) and attach: 1 recent passport-size photo of the Student, 1 recent passport-size photo of the Nominee, a photocopy of the Student’s Identity Card, a photocopy ofthe Admission Receipt, a photocopy of the Scheduled Tribe & Indigenous Certificate, a specimen signature of the Nominee, and a photocopy of the Front Page of the Bank Pass Book of the Nominee. **Step 3:** The filled Registration Form with necessary documents shall be sent/submitted to: NGESSO Section, Directorate of Higher Education, Below Nagaland Secretariat Complex, Nagaland: Kohima – 797001 on/before 31st January and within the stipulated time period. **Step 4:** After successful verification of forms and documents, the Department shall assign a Registration number to each applicant and upload the list on the Department’s website. **Step 5:** Registered students shall renew their registration manually every Academic year (Annually) by submitting the [**Renewal Form** (2025–26)](https://highereducation.nagaland.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/RENEWAL25.pdf) to the same address on/before 31st January 2026, along with a photocopy of the student’s Identity Card and photocopy of the Admission Receipt; in case of a change of nominee, 1 recent passport-size photo of the Nominee, Specimen signature of the Nominee, and photocopy of the Front Page of Bank Pass Book of the Nominee shall be enclosed. **Step 6:** In case of death of the registered student outside Nagaland, the Nominee shall submit an application to the Director, Directorate of Higher Education, Government of Nagaland, Kohima within 2 (two) months mentioning the name of the deceased student, date of death, cause of death and place of death, along with: Certificate issued by the nearest Police Station, Certificate issued by the Principal/Head of Department, Registration ID Number of the deceased student, Bank Account Number/Name and Address of the Bank/IFSC supported by photo copy of the front page of the Bank Pass Book, and sign an undertaking prepared by the Directorate of Higher Education.

metadata.schemeName: Hostels for ST Boys and ST Girls
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to attract implementing agencies for undertaking the hostel construction programme for ST Girls to reduce drop out rate. Through this scheme, central assistance for the construction/extension of hostels is provided to ST boys and girls (including Primitive Tribal Groups).

page_content:
# Hostels for ST Boys and ST Girls **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Nagaland | **Categories:** Housing & Shelter, Education & Learning | **Tags:** Tribal Hostel Infrastructure, Centrally Sponsored Scheme, ST Education, ST Students Welfare | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme "Hostels for ST Boys and ST Girls" by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme which aims to attract the implementing agencies for undertaking hostel construction programme for ST Girls studying in middle schools, higher secondary schools, colleges and universities towards the broader vision of containment and reduction of their drop out rate. Through this scheme, central assistance limited only to the cost of construction/extension of hostels is provided to ST boys and girls (including Primitive Tribal Groups). The scheme is implemented through the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations and the Central/other Universities. The hostels are constructed at places where the educational institutions concerned are situated, keeping in view the concentration of ST population in a particular area or place and are sanctioned as far as possible as a part of the established educational institutions or in close vicinity of such institutions. The hostels can be constructed for middle, secondary, college, and university level of education and also for Vocational Training Centres in tribal areas where State Governments/Union Territory Administrations take initiative to run these centres efficiently. The construction includes boundary walls, two rooms set for the hostel warden, a kitchen, a toilet, a common room, and one room set for Chowkidar as an integral part of the scheme and the cost of construction will be worked out based on the State/Union Territory Public Works Department/Central Public Works Department schedule of rates prescribed for such type of construction. The hostels shall be completed within 2 years from the date of release of the central assistance and extension of existing hostels shall be completed within 12 months, while the implementing agencies shall supervise construction and submit quarterly physical and financial progress reports to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, New Delhi. > **Objectives** 1. The primary objective of the modification is to attract the implementing agencies for undertaking hostel construction programme for ST Girls studying in middle schools, higher secondary schools, colleges and universities towards the broader vision of containment and reduction of their drop out rate.
## Benefits > **Central Assistance** 1. Central assistance is limited only to the cost of construction/extension of the hostels for ST Girls and Boys (including Primitive Tribal Groups). > **Funding Pattern** 1. **Hostels For ST Girls** - 100% central assistance to State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. - 100% central assistance to Central/other Universities. 1. **Hostels For ST Boys** - 50:50 matching basis for State Governments. - 100% central assistance for Naxal-affected states (specified districts identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs). - 100% financial assistance to Union Territory Administrations. - 90% financial assistance to Central Universities. - 45% central share, 45% State share, and 10% to be borne by the Universities concerned for other Universities. - If the State Governments concerned do not contribute their share of 45% to the Universities, the share of the former will also have to be borne by the Universities concerned, thereby raising their contribution to 55%. 1. **Hostels For Vocational Training Centres** - Hostels for Vocational Training Centres for ST Girls and Boys will be funded on the same criteria as other hostels for schools/colleges. > **Mode of Disbursement** 1. The grants-in-aid shall be released after ensuring the physical release of the requisite matching share by the State Government/Union Territory Administration/University concerned. > **Validity Period** 1. Hostels shall be completed within 2 years from the date of release of the central assistance. 1. Extension of existing hostels shall be completed within 12 months.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must be a State Government. 1. The applicant must be a Union Territory Administration. 1. The applicant must be a Central University. 1. The applicant must be an other University. 1. The applicant must construct the hostel at a place where the educational institutions concerned are situated. 1. The applicant must keep in view the concentration of the ST population in a particular area or place. 1. The applicant must sanction the hostel as far as possible as a part of the established educational institutions or in the close vicinity of such institutions. 1. The applicant must construct hostels for Vocational Training Centres only in those tribal areas where State Governments/Union Territory Administrations take the initiative to run these centres efficiently. 1. The applicant must construct hostels for middle, secondary, college, and university levels of education, and also for Vocational Training Centres. 1. The applicant must ensure that the number of inmates for whom accommodation can be provided in a hostel should not exceed 100, but may exceed if there is a requirement for additional seats. 1. The applicant must bear the expenditure on maintenance of the hostels from their own funds. 1. The applicant must make available unencumbered land free of cost for the construction of the hostel. 1. The applicant must submit a certificate to the effect that a matching provision, wherever necessary, exists in the State Budget for the Scheme. 1. The applicant must construct boundary walls, two rooms set for the hostel warden, a kitchen, a toilet, a common room, and one room set for the Chowkidar as an integral part of the hostel scheme. 1. The applicant must construct a few rooms/blocks barrier-free and include facilities like ramps, etc. in the design of the construction for the convenience of the ST students with disabilities. 1. The applicant shall work out the cost of construction of hostels based on the State/Union Territory Public Works Department/Central Public Works Department schedule of rates prescribed for such type of construction. 1. The applicant shall ensure completion of hostels within 2 years from the date of release of the central assistance. 1. The applicant shall ensure the completion of the extension of existing hostels within 12 months. > **Preference / Priority / Relaxation** 1. Preference will be given to State Governments that commit annual maintenance expenditure, as per reasonable norms. 1. The applicant State Government located in naxal-affected states (specified districts identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs from time to time) will be eligible for 100% central assistance for Hostels for ST Boys. 1. The applicant State Government may have its required matching share provided by any Member of Parliament/Member of Legislative Assembly from his/her Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme/Members of Legislative Assembly Local Area Development Scheme fund, in case it is unable to provide the required matching share from its budget.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The State Government/Union Territory Administration/Central University/other University identifies the requirement for the construction/extension of a hostel and makes available unencumbered land free of cost for the construction of the hostel. **Step 2:** The Plan of the Hostel is prepared and duly approved by the competent authority in the State Government/Union Territory Administration/University. **Step 3:** The application for the grant is prepared, supported by the Utilization Certificate as well as details of physical and financial progress in respect of hostels sanctioned earlier by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. **Step 4:** The application includes details of the location of the proposed hostel and the number of seats in each hostel and is accompanied by a certificate to the effect that matching provision, wherever necessary, exists in the State Budget for the Scheme. **Step 5:** The quarterly progress reports are submitted to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. **Step 6:** The grants-in-aid are released after ensuring the physical release of the requisite matching share by the State Government/Union Territory Administration/University concerned. **Step 7:** The implementing agency supervises the construction of hostels regularly and submits quarterly progress reports, both physical and financial, to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, New Delhi till the completion of the hostels. **Step 8:** The hostel construction is completed within 2 years from the date of release of the central assistance, and the extension of existing hostels is completed within 12 months.

metadata.schemeName: Sangeet Natak Mahotsav
metadata.briefDescription: The "Sangeet Natak Mahotsav" is a programme organized by the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Govt. of Goa, with the objective of reviving and promoting the rich tradition of Sangeet Natak (musical plays) in the state. Participation is invited through press notes released in local newspaper.

page_content:
# Sangeet Natak Mahotsav **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Goa | **Categories:** Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Mahotsav, Musical, Financial Support, Kala Academy | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Sangeet Natak Mahotsav" is a programme organized by the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa, with the objective of reviving and promoting the rich tradition of Sangeet Natak (musical plays) in the state. Participation is invited through press notes released in local newspapers. Eligible participants include all Goan institutions registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, and those that have regularly renewed their registration as per the Act. The selection of participating groups is carried out by a panel of judges appointed by the Kala Academy, based on auditions and rehearsals. ## Benefits **Assistance available:** Selected participating institutions are paid a lumpsum of ₹30,000/- plus 80% of the total sale proceeds from ticket sale of the concerned play. Besides auditorium made available free of charge with available and permissible infrastructural facilities ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a Goa institution registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. 1. The applicant should have valid and up-to-date registration, renewed from time to time as per the provisions of the Act. ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1**: Collect the prescribed application form from Kala Academy, available free of charge. Fill in all required details as per the guidelines. **Step 2:** Attach a photocopy of the institution’s valid registration/renewal certificate. Submit the entry form along with a refundable security deposit of ₹1,000/- to ensure staging of the selected play (duration must be between 2½ to 3 hours). **Step 3:** Submit the completed application and documents within the stipulated deadline to the Member Secretary, Kala Academy Goa.

metadata.schemeName: Border Area Development Programme (BADP)
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote the development of border areas by supporting development works in villages located along the international border in Rajasthan.

page_content:
# Border Area Development Programme (BADP) **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Transport & Infrastructure | **Tags:** Border Area Development, BADP, Border Development, Border Villages, Rural Development, Infrastructure Development, Rural Development | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Border Area Development Programme (BADP)" is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Department, Government of Rajasthan, which aims to promote the development of border areas through providing development works to people living in border regions. The scheme was launched in 1993-94. It is funded in the ratio of 60% by the Central Government and 40% by the State Government. The programme is implemented in the border districts of Barmer, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, and Sri Ganganagar through the respective district councils and implementing agencies. Development works are undertaken after approval of the annual action plan by the competent district, state, and central authorities.
## Benefits - **Development of Border Areas:** Development works are undertaken in villages located within 0 to 10 km of the international border. - **Coverage:** The programme is implemented in 16 development blocks across the border districts of Barmer, Jaisalmer, Bikaner, and Sri Ganganagar in Rajasthan. - **Funding Support:** Development works are funded under a 60:40 cost-sharing ratio, with 60% contribution from the Central Government and 40% contribution from the State Government (effective from 2016-17).
## Eligibility Criteria - Under this scheme, development works of border areas are carried out.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** Development works are identified and proposed under the annual action plan. **Step 2:** The District-Level Committee, headed by the District Collector, approves the proposed development works. **Step 3:** The approved proposals are submitted to the State-Level Screening Committee headed by the Chief Secretary. **Step 4:** The State-Level Screening Committee forwards the approved action plan to the Border Management Department, Government of India. **Step 5:** After approval by the Government of India, the scheme is implemented through the border district councils and designated implementing agencies.

metadata.schemeName: Carol Singing Festival
metadata.briefDescription: The "Carol Singing Festival" is a programme organized by the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa, with the aim of promoting singing talent and preserving the rich tradition of Christmas carols.

page_content:
# Carol Singing Festival **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Goa | **Categories:** Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Festival, Singing, Talent, Academy | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The ‘Carol Singing Festival’ is a programme organised by the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa, to promote singing talent and preserve the rich repertoire of Christmas carols. Participation entries are invited through a press note published in local dailies. The entry form, along with the rules and regulations, is available at Kala Academy.
## Benefits In addition to round-trip transport, Kala Academy provides ₹2,000/- as participation fees.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. Any Goa Carol singing group is eligible to participate. ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** Visit the Kala Academy office to collect the entry form, which is available free of charge along with the rules and regulations of the festival. **Step 2:** Complete the entry form with accurate group details and ensure all required information is provided as per the guidelines. **Step 3:** Submit the filled form within the stipulated deadline to the Member Secretary, Kala Academy Goa.

metadata.schemeName: Khell Tiatr Festival
metadata.briefDescription: The Khell Tiatr Festival is a cultural initiative of the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa, aimed at preserving and promoting the rich Goa tradition of Khell Tiatr. Participation is invited through press notes published in local newspapers.

page_content:
# Khell Tiatr Festival **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Goa | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Festival, Academy, Committee, Financial Support | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The Khell Tiatr Festival is a cultural initiative of the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa, aimed at preserving and promoting the rich Goan tradition of Khell Tiatr. Participation is invited through press notes published in local newspapers. Eligible participants include traditional Goan Khell Tiatr performing groups actively engaged in the propagation and promotion of this art form. The selection of 5 to 7 Khell Tiatrs is carried out by a designated Sub-Committee of the Tiatr Advisory Committee or by the authorities of the Kala Academy.
## Benefits **Assistance Available:** Selected participating institutions are provided with a lump sum amount of ₹7,000/-, along with 80% of the total proceeds from ticket sales of their respective play. Additionally, the auditorium is made available free of charge, along with the available and permissible infrastructural facilities required for the performance.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a traditional Goa Khell Tiatr performing group with a track record of staging Khell Tiatrs. 1. The applicant should be actively involved in the propagation and promotion of the Khell Tiatr art form in Goa.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1 :** Write the application on plain paper, clearly stating your interest in participating in the Khell Tiatr Festival. Include your contact details such as telephone number and communication address. **Step 2 :** Enclose a copy of the script of the Khell Tiatr, details of the cast and crew (credits), and any other relevant information supporting the authenticity and traditional value of the play. **Step 3 :** Make sure the Khell Tiatr is written by a Goan playwright and retains the traditional essence of the art form. The play should be between 2 to 3 hours in duration to qualify. **Step 4 :** Submit the complete application along with documents to the Member Secretary, Kala Academy Goa within the stipulated deadline.

# Supply of School Uniform , Shoes Socks to all Students for Std IX to XII **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Education, Free Stationery, Free Shoes Socks | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description Provision of complete uniform(Shirt, Pants, Skirt, Tie, Belt) socks, shoes to all students in classes IX to XII of Government schools. It ensures that every child, regardless of their socio-economic background, has the basic physical tools required for a productive learning environment. Standardized uniform scheme to promote discipline and equality among male and female students, removing social distinctions based on attire.


## Benefits
1. Fosters a sense of identity, equality and discipline among students. 2. Significantly reduces school absenteeism and improves performance by eliminating the financial barrier of purchasing clothes. 3. Providing shoes and socks promotes better foot health and hygiene for students commuting to school. 4. Promotes regular school attendance by supporting foundational needs
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a student. 2. The applicant should be studying in class 9th to 12th. 3. The applicant should be studying in a government school in UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline 1. No separate application is required. 1. Eligible students enrolled in government schools are automatically covered under the scheme.

metadata.schemeName: Scheme for Promotion of Affordable Rental Smart Housing (SPARSH 2.0): Rent Subsidy
beneficiaryState: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to reduce the rental burden on workers and economically weaker section families residing in affordable rental housing complexes.

page_content:
# Scheme for Promotion of Affordable Rental Smart Housing (SPARSH 2.0): Rent Subsidy **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu | **Categories:** Housing & Shelter | **Tags:** Rental Housing, Economically Weaker Section, Labour, Affordable Housing, Industrial Workers | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme “Scheme for Promotion of Affordable Rental Smart Housing (SPARSH 2.0)” implemented through verticals "Subsidising the stay of urban poor and labourers in SPARSH 2.0 housing complexes to give such complexes a competitive advantage over other chawls etc. and bring down the rental charges for the Urban poor" by the Labour & Employment Department, UT Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu aims to reduce the rental burden on workers and economically weaker section families residing in affordable rental housing complexes. Through this scheme, monthly rent subsidy is provided to eligible beneficiaries residing in registered SPARSH 2.0 housing complexes. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Labour & Employment through designated nodal officers. Subsidy benefits are transferred directly to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts of beneficiaries. The subsidy is primarily transferred to female family members wherever applicable. The scheme also allows direct transfer to individual dormitory beneficiaries. The registration process also ensures annual monitoring and compliance verification. SPARSH 2.0 is applicable across Daman, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Diu for the period from 2022 to 2027. > **Objectives:** - To address the vision of “Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyan” by creating a sustainable ecosystem of affordable rental housing solutions for workers in industries, construction sites, and other weaker sections. - To achieve the objective of “Housing for All” by promoting affordable rental housing for workers and labourers. - To create a conducive environment by incentivising public and private entities to invest in affordable rental housing stock. - To increase the productivity of industries by improving the health and well-being of workers. - To reduce the financial burden on workers due to treatment costs and wage loss. - To increase the happiness and quality of life of workers. - To harmonise the Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHC) Scheme guidelines with the SPARSH Scheme.
## Benefits Subsidising the stay of urban poor and labourers in housing complexes registered or constructed under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme, either by a private player under vertical 1 or 2 or by any PSUs, Autonomous bodies, etc., under vertical 3 1. All EWS families staying in the housing complexes registered or constructed under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme shall be entitled to a rent subsidy of Rs. 500 per month per person subject to a maximum of 5 persons in a family. 1. For any housing complex registered under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme, such subsidy shall be allowed for a period of not more than 20 years from the date of Registration, or till 40 years from the date of construction, whichever is earlier. 1. Subsidy shall be transferred to any lady member of the family in her account through Aadhar-linked bank transfer in case of families, or to each individual person in case of a dormitory. Subsidy shall be transferred to the Aadhar-linked bank account of the Karta or senior most earning male member of the family if no female member is either available or stays in the Housing Complex.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should belong to Dadra And Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. 1. The applicant should be the owner or authorised representative of the housing complex. 1. The housing complex should fulfil SPARSH 2.0 infrastructure norms. 1. The housing complex should possess valid construction permission and/or an occupancy certificate. 1. The applicant should agree to reserve at least 66% dwelling units for Economically Weaker Section beneficiaries. 1. The applicant should agree to maintain the housing complex and waste management systems.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The owner or authorised representative of the housing complex should obtain Form A prescribed under the scheme. **Step 2:** The applicant should fill out Form A and attach all required supporting documents. **Step 3:** The completed application should be submitted to the concerned officer designated by the Secretary of Labour for the respective district. **Step 4:** The nodal officer shall verify the application within 30 days. Technical verification may also be conducted through the associate town planner or other competent authority. **Step 5:** After successful verification, the nodal officer shall issue the Registration Certificate in Form B. **Step 6:** The nodal officer shall execute an agreement with the owner as prescribed under the scheme. **Step 7:** The registration shall be verified annually. Registration may be cancelled if the scheme conditions are violated.

page_content:
# Scheme for Promotion of Affordable Rental Smart Housing (SPARSH 2.0): Construction and Redevelopment Incentives **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu | **Categories:** Housing & Shelter | **Tags:** Rental Housing, Infrastructure, Floor Space Index, Regulatory Relaxations, Housing Project | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme “Scheme for Promotion of Affordable Rental Smart Housing (SPARSH 2.0)” implemented through verticals "Incentivising the development or redevelopment of housing complexes and residential spaces for urban poor as SPARSH 2.0 housing complexes by relaxing construction norms for such complexes" by the Labour & Employment Department, UT Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu aims to encourage development and redevelopment of affordable rental housing infrastructure. Through this scheme, additional Floor Space Index benefits, additional ground coverage, commercial utilisation relaxations, and regulatory relaxations are provided to eligible housing complex developers and owners. It also mandates the reservation of dwelling units for beneficiaries of the Economically Weaker Section. Housing complexes registered under the scheme become eligible for further scheme incentives and benefits. The registration process also ensures annual monitoring and compliance verification. SPARSH 2.0 is applicable across Daman, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Diu for the period from 2022 to 2027. > **Objectives:** - To address the vision of “Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyan” by creating a sustainable ecosystem of affordable rental housing solutions for workers in industries, construction sites, and other weaker sections. - To achieve the objective of “Housing for All” by promoting affordable rental housing for workers and laborers. - To create a conducive environment by incentivising public and private entities to invest in affordable rental housing stock. - To increase the productivity of industries by improving the health and well-being of workers. - To reduce the financial burden on workers due to treatment costs and wage loss. - To increase the happiness and quality of life of workers. - To harmonise the Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHC) Scheme guidelines with the SPARSH Scheme.
## Benefits For any housing complex to apply under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme, the proposed construction should either be registered under the ARHC scheme or, in the alternative, should fulfil all conditions as mentioned in the first vertical except condition (g) and shall also have other valid permissions as may be required in law. Concerned authorities, whether the Planning and Development Authority or Municipalities, entrusted with the responsibility of giving construction permission or an occupancy certificate, shall provide the following benefits/relaxation to the construction permission. 1. Each such housing complex under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme shall be entitled to an additional 50% of the applicable FSI. 1. Each such housing complex under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme shall be entitled to an additional 20% of the ground coverage. 1. Each such housing complex under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme shall be entitled to such relaxations in setbacks or abutting road size as the concerned Authority may determine by rules/bye-laws made in this behalf. 1. With the exception of Green Zone and notwithstanding any other zone, road-width, or area, 20% of the permissible ground coverage shall be allowed to be used for commercial/business purposes. 1. The concerned Authority shall regularise the existing housing complexes if they fall within the relaxed guidelines as prescribed under this Scheme. Concerned Revenue Departments shall prioritise any application for NA for the construction of such housing complexes.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should belong to Dadra And Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. 1. The applicant should be the owner or authorised representative of the housing complex. 1. The housing complex should fulfil SPARSH 2.0 infrastructure norms. 1. The housing complex should possess a valid construction permission and/or occupancy certificate. 1. The applicant should agree to reserve at least 66% dwelling units for Economically Weaker Section beneficiaries. 1. The applicant should agree to maintain the housing complex and waste management systems.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The owner or authorised representative of the housing complex should obtain Form A prescribed under the scheme. **Step 2:** The applicant should fill out Form A and attach all required supporting documents. **Step 3:** The completed application should be submitted to the concerned officer designated by the Secretary, Labour, for the respective district. **Step 4:** The nodal officer shall verify the application within 30 days. Technical verification may also be conducted through the Associate Town Planner or other competent authority. **Step 5:** After successful verification, the nodal officer shall issue the Registration Certificate in Form B. **Step 6:** The nodal officer shall execute an agreement with the owner as prescribed under the scheme. **Step 7:** The registration shall be verified annually. Registration may be cancelled if the scheme conditions are violated.

page_content:
# Virasat Loan Scheme of NMDFC **Ministry:** Ministry Of Minority Affairs | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Banking,Financial Services and Insurance | **Tags:** Virasat Loan Scheme Of NMDFC | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description This scheme is part of the Term Loan scheme and is implemented with the objective to meet Working Capital and Fixed Capital for purchase of equipment/tools/machineries/raw material. Maximum loan of upto Rs.10.00 lacs can be availed under Credit Line-1 & 2. Simple interest of 5% p.a. is charged under Credit Line-1 and at 6% p.a. from Male Artisan under Credit line- 2. Concession of 1% is provided to Female Artisan under both the Credit Lines.
## Benefits Concessional Credit to the beneficiaries among minority communities.
## Eligibility Criteria a) The applicant must be Indian and belong to one of the six notified minority communities: Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Parsi, or Jain. b) The annual family income of the applicant shall not exceed: Rs. 3.00 lakh per annum under Credit Line–1. Rs. 8.00 lakh per annum under Credit Line–2. c) The applicant must be an artisan or craftsperson engaged in a traditional occupation (such as handloom, handicraft, metalwork, leatherwork, embroidery, pottery, etc.). d) The applicant should have basic skills or certification in the relevant craft or trade, verified by a competent authority or local body. e) The loan shall be used for procurement of tools, equipment, raw materials, or working capital to enhance production and market linkage. f) Preference shall be given to women artisans and occupational clusters in minority-dominated areas. g) The applicant should not be a beneficiary of any other similar artisan financing scheme at the time of application. h) The beneficiary must possess a valid Aadhaar-linked bank account and minority certificate.
## Exclusions Other than Six Notified minority communities having annual family income of more than Rs. 3.00 Lakhs under credit line 1 and of more than Rs.8.00 Lakhs under credit line 2.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline NMDFC implements its schemes & programs through State Channelizing Agencies (SCA list: www.nmdfc.org/SCA ) nominated by the respective State Governments & Banking Partners (Presently through Canara Bank & Punjab Grameen Bank).

page_content:
# Agri-Clinics And Agri-Business Centres Scheme **Ministry:** Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment, Business & Entrepreneurship, Skills & Employment | **Tags:** Business, Entrepreneur, Student, Training, Agriculture, Employment | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description A welfare scheme by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare was launched in 2002. AC&ABC aims at agricultural development by supplementing the efforts of public extension by providing extension and other services to farmers either on a payment basis or free of cost as per the business model of agri-preneur, local needs, and affordability of the target group of farmers. AC&ABC creates gainful self-employment opportunities for unemployed agricultural graduates, agricultural diploma holders, intermediate in agriculture, and biological science graduates with PG in agri-related courses. NABARD is acting as a subsidy channelizing agency for this scheme.
Committed to this program, the Government is now also providing start-up training to graduates in Agriculture, or any subject allied to Agriculture like Horticulture, Sericulture, Veterinary Sciences, Forestry, Dairy, Poultry Farming, Fisheries, etc. Those completing the training can apply for special start-up loans for ventures. ## Benefits **Agri-Clinics -** Agri-Clinics are envisaged to provide expert advice and services to farmers on various aspects to enhance the productivity of crops/animals and increase the incomes of farmers. Agri-Clinics provide support in the following areas: 1. Soil health 1. Cropping practices 1. Plant protection 1. Crop insurance post-harvest technology clinical services for animals, feed and fodder management prices of various crops in the market, etc.
**Agri-Business Centres -** Agri-Business Centres are commercial units of agri-ventures established by trained agriculture professionals. These ventures may include maintenance and custom hiring of farm equipment, sale of inputs, and other services in agriculture and allied areas, including post-harvest management and market linkages for income generation and entrepreneurship development.
The scheme covers full financial support for training and handholding, provision of loans, and credit-linked back-end composite subsidy.
**Project activities -** 1. Extension consultancy services 1. Soil and water quality cum inputs testing laboratories (with Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometers) 1. Pest surveillance, diagnostic and control services 1. Maintenance, repairs, and custom hiring of agricultural implements and machinery including micro-irrigation systems (sprinkler and drip) 1. Agri Service Centres include the three activities mentioned above (Group Activity). 1. Seed Processing Units 1. Micro-propagation through Plant Tissue Culture Labs and Hardening Units 1. Setting up of Vermiculture units, production of bio-fertilizers, bio-pesticides, and bio-control agents. 1. Setting up of Apiaries (bee-keeping) and honey & bee products' processing units 1. Provision of Extension Consultancy Services 1. Hatcheries and production of fish fingerlings for aquaculture 1. Provision of livestock health cover, setting up veterinary dispensaries & services including frozen semen banks and liquid nitrogen supply 1. Setting up of Information Technology Kiosks in rural areas for access to various agriculture-related portals 1. Feed Processing and testing units 1. Value Addition Centres 1. Setting up of Cool Chain from the farm level onwards (Group Activity) 1. Retail marketing outlets for processed agri-products 1. Rural marketing dealerships of farm inputs and outputs ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The age of the applicant must be between 18 and 60 years. 1. The applicant must qualify as one of the following - - Graduates in agriculture and allied subjects from SAUs/ Central Agricultural Universities/ Universities recognized by ICAR/ UGC. Degree in Agriculture and allied subjects offered by other agencies are also considered subject to the approval of the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation, Government of India on the recommendation of the State Government. - Diploma (with at least 50% marks)/ Post Graduate Diploma holders in Agriculture and allied subjects from State Agricultural Universities, State Agriculture and Allied Departments, and State Department of Technical Education. - Diplomas in Agriculture and allied subjects offered by other agencies are also considered subject to the approval of the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation, Government of India on the recommendation of the State Government. - Biological Science Graduates with Post Graduation in Agriculture & allied subjects. - Degree courses recognized by UGC have more than 60 percent of the course content in Agriculture and allied subjects. - Diploma/Post-graduate Diploma courses with more than 60 percent of course content in Agriculture and allied subjects, after B.Sc. with Biological Sciences, from recognized colleges and universities. - Agriculture-related courses at intermediate (i.e. plus two) level, with at least 55% marks. ## Exclusions Retired Employees Getting Pensionary Benefits Are Not Eligible For Subsidy. However, They Can Undergo Training And Establish Self Financed Projects. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Official Portal/Link:** https://acabcmis.gov.in/ApplicantReg.aspx **Step 1:** Visit on the [Official Website](https://acabcmis.gov.in/ApplicantReg.aspx) **Step 2:** Fill in the mandatory fields correctly. Upload the required documents in the said format and size. **Step 3:** Click "Submit" to complete the application process.
The applicant can check his/her application status by visiting this[ link](https://acabcmis.gov.in/ApplicationStatus_new.aspx).

This initiative aligns with the objectives of "Samagra Shiksha" (holistic education) as outlined..

page_content:
# Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme **Ministry:** Ministry of Education | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** Delhi | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Education, Honorarium, Student, Undergraduate, Postgraduate | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme (VCIS)" by the University of Delhi aims to provide students with experiential learning opportunities, integrating academic knowledge with practical work experience. This initiative aligns with the objectives of "Samagra Shiksha" (holistic education) as outlined in the NEP 2020. The VCIS allows students to work in various departments, centers, and institutes within the university, offering a unique platform to broaden their skills and gain real-world experience. > **Objectives of VCIS, University of Delhi:** - Internship schemes allow young students to be associated with the university's work for mutual benefit. - It will expose university students to the several departments/centres/ institutes existing within the University of Delhi. - It will infuse in interns a sense of belongingness with the University system. - It will connect students of the University of Delhi to their local community and give them realworld experiences. - It will train students in collecting/streamlining documents and collating available data/resources. - It will inculcate professional aptitude, strengthen personal character, and provide a more significant opportunity for students to broaden their mental horizons. - It will give students the broadest spectrum of opportunities when seeking and applying for a job after college. - It will be beneficial for the University of Delhi as the involvement of interns with the institution will inculcate a sense of responsibility and strengthen bonding with the University. Young students with innovative ideas, abilities and skills for resolving problems will be instrumental in bringing systemic and holistic changes to the University system.
> **Kinds of Internships under VCIS:** - Internship - Summer Internship
> **Duration of the Internship:** - Summer internships are 8 weeks long with 15-20 flexible hours per week. - Regular internships during the academic session are 8-10 hours per week, with a maximum duration of six months.
## Benefits > **Stipend:** - ₹5,000/- per month for interns - ₹10,500/- per month for summer interns. **NOTE:** Stipend will be enhanced by 5% each financial year.
> **Certificate:** - Receive a certificate of experience from the Dean of Students' Welfare. ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a student. 1. The students pursuing Final year/ Final Semester are not eligible. 1. All bonafide full-time regular students of the University of Delhi, studying in any course or stream at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels, are eligible.
## Exclusions Those students who have already availed VCIS (Summer/ Part-time) are not eligible for the VCIS. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Apply Procedure:** **Step-01:** The interested applicant visits the [official website](https://dsw.du.ac.in/). **Step-02:** The applicant needs to fill out a [Google Form](https://forms.gle/Qy97xZrBWJRNfzzK9) to apply for the internship. **Step-03:** Fill in the required information and upload all the essential documents.
**Note:** List of selected candidates for the Vice Chancellor Internship Scheme show on the official website.
> **Selection Procedure:** Based on assessment and interaction with the selection committee, comprising members nominated by the Vice-Chancellor.

metadata.schemeName: Prime Minister’s Scholarship Scheme for the Wards of Central Armed Police Forces & Assam Rifles
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to encourage higher technical and professional education for dependent wards and widows of CAPFs/Assam Rifles personnel martyred during Terror/Naxal attacks. Through this scheme, Financial support per year for girls and boys is provided.

page_content:
# Prime Minister’s Scholarship Scheme for the Wards of Central Armed Police Forces & Assam Rifles

**Ministry:** Ministry Of Home Affairs | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Scholarship, Student, Assam Rifles, CAPF, Ward, Widow | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual

## Description
The “Prime Minister’s Scholarship Scheme (PMSS) for the Wards of Central Armed Police Forces & Assam Rifles” is a scholarship scheme which was introduced by the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India from the academic year 2006-07 to encourage higher technical & professional education for the dependent wards & widows of Central Armed Police Forces & Assam Rifles (CAPFs & AR) Personnel.
> **Number of Scholarship:**

For the wards of CAPFs & Assam Rifles, a total of 2000 Scholarships (equally for both girls & boys) under PMSS will be given for each academic year in addition to renewal cases of previous years. Shortfall in fresh cases shall not be adjusted from girls/boys, if applicants (Boys/Girls) are selected less than 1000.

## Benefits
**The benefits under the scheme is as follows:**
**Amount of Scholarship:**
•	₹3,000/- per month for girls.
•	₹2,500/- per month for boys 
**Note:** The above scholarship amount is to be paid annually after selection @ ₹36,000/- to each girl & ₹30,000/- to each boy.
**Duration of Scholarship:**
Up to 5 years (depending upon the duration of the course being pursued by the applicant and as approved by the respective regulatory body).

## Eligibility Criteria
**The eligibility criteria for availing financial assistance under this scheme are as follows:-**

   1. Wards/widows of deceased Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles (ARs) personnel who died in harness/election duty, wards of personnel disabled due to causes attributable to Government service, and Wards of Ex CAPFs & AR personnel in receipt of Gallantry Awards.
   1. Wards/widows of retired and serving CAPFs & AR Personnel. (Personnel below Officer Rank)
   1. Pursuing first professional degree programme in the field of Engineering, Medicine, Dental, Veterinary, BBA, BCA, B. Pharma, B.SC (Nursing, Agriculture, etc.), MBA and MCA, etc. in accordance with the [guidelines](https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/warb/G_1197_3001.pdf) as mentioned in Para- 8 (B).   1. Having a minimum of 60% marks in Minimum Entry Qualification (MEQ) i.e. 10+2/Diploma/Graduation or equivalent in case of a new applicant. (OR) For applicants applying under the renewal category, it is mandatory to pass each subsequent academic year of the professional courses being pursued by them with a minimum of 50% marks.
   1. A grace period of one year only for cases, where there is a delay on the part of the candidate for submission of application for renewal of scholarship may be entertained.

> **Order of Preference:**

Applications received from the eligible applicants under the Fresh category will be shortlisted on the basis of an order of preference as mentioned below and the percentage of marks obtained by them in MEQ:-
**Sl. No.****Category****Details**1Category-A Wards/Widows of CAPFs &amp;amp; AR personnel killed in action.2Category-BWards of Ex-CAPFs &amp;amp; AR personnel disabled in action.3Category-CWards/Widows of deceased CAPFs &amp;amp; AR personnel died for causes attributable to Government service including casualties during conduct of Election.4Category-DWards of Ex-CAPFs &amp;amp; AR personnel disabled while in service with disability attributable to Government Service5Category-EWards of Ex-CAPFs &amp;amp; AR personnel in receipt of Gallantry Awards.6Category-FWards of Ex- CAPFs &amp;amp; AR personnel (PBOR).7Category-GWards of serving CAPFs &amp;amp; AR personnel (PBOR) subject to availability of scholarship.**Note 01:** Wards of deceased CAPF/AR personnel will be considered for scholarship under Categories “A” to “F” as per their priority, even on compassionate appointment of spouse/NOKs in CAPFs.
**Note 02:** The Wards of Assistant Commandant, holding Local Rank of CAPFs & AR (who are not entailing the pay benefits of Assistant Commandant and drawing the Salary of Inspectors) are eligible for granting PMS under category “F” & “G” also.
**Note 03:** This scholarship is admissible for only two Children per family and should be ensured by the beneficiaries as well as by the respective CAPF & AR.
**Note 04:** The applicants irrespective of his /her marital status are eligible for PMSS.
**Minimum Entry Qualification (MEQ):**
For being eligible for the Scholarship under PMSS, an applicant should have secured a minimum of 60% marks in MEQ i.e. 10+2 / Diploma / Graduation as the case may be. MEQ for entry to various professional courses differs. For example, MEQ for MBBS is 10+2 whereas for BE/B.Tech, it is 10+2/Diploma. It is graduation for B. Ed and MBA.
Note:

  - Wards admitted in 2nd year of technical/professional Bachelor Degree Course (BE/B. Tech etc.) through lateral entry after completion of Diploma courses are eligible for PMSS.
  - In case of applicant passed the XII exam from CBSE, marks obtained in the best of five subjects out of 500 will be considered for calculating the percentage of marks in MEQ.

> **Courses applicable under PMSS :**


  - Only First professional degree courses like BE, B Tech, BDS, MBBS, B.Ed., BBA, BCA, B Pharma, B.Sc (Nursing, Agriculture, etc.) duly recognized by the respective Government Regulatory Bodies, such as All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), Medical Council of India (MCI), University Grant Commission (UGC).
  - Details of professional degree courses applicable for PMSS are mentioned at [Appendix – I](https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/warb/G_1197_3001.pdf).
> **Scholarship for Integrated Courses:**


  - The PMSS is restricted to first Professional Degree Courses only. It is applicable for B.Ed but not for BA+B.Ed. In the case of integrated ME/M.Tech/ M.Pharma, the scholarship will be given for an initial three/four years as the case may be.

## Exclusions
**The following applicants NOT eligible under PMSS are:**

   1. Wards of civilian employees of CAPFs, AR, and States/UTs Police personnel.
   1. Applicants who are pursuing professional courses through correspondence /distance learning.
   1. Applicants availing the benefit of other scholarship schemes/getting stipend and financial assistance.
   1. Applicants already availed scholarship under PMSS.
   1. Applicants pursuing courses, such as Diploma courses, not leading to the award of a degree or pursuing master's degree programme except MBA, MCA subject to first professional course.
   1. Applicants admitted on their own to the college/institute/university NOT APPROVED under UGC Act or not recognized by AICTE and not having NBA accredited courses (for Engineering Degree courses) or Not approved by Medical Council of India (for Medical Degree courses).
   1. Applicants studying Abroad.
   1. Change of course/college by the Selected Student and getting fresh admission in a subsequent academic year will lead to the rejection of his/her Scholarship forever.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Online
Online submission for the scholarship can be done through the website of the National Scholarship Portal with the required documents: [https://scholarships.gov.in/ ](https://scholarships.gov.in/)
> **Registration for New Applicant:**

**Step 01:** Open the official NSP website and click on "[New Registration"](https://scholarships.gov.in/registrations/#/) under Applicant Corner.
**Step 02:** Read the Instruction /Guidelines, provide the undertaking by clicking on the Check box then click on Continue.
**Step 03:** Start the registration by providing the required details.
>  **Registered Applicant:**

**Step 01:** Open the official NSP website and click on '[Fresh Application](https://scholarships.gov.in/fresh/loginPage)' under Applicant Corner.
**Step 02:** Login with your application ID & password.
**Step 03:** Select the Scholarship.
**Step 04:** Fill out the applicant form.
**Step 05:** Upload the required documents and Submit.
> **Letter from Hon’ble Prime Minister:**

All applicants selected under the new category will be given personal letters from the Hon’ble Prime Minister in appropriate language.
> **Payment of Scholarship:**

•	The Scholarship amount under PMSS for applicants selected under fresh and renewal categories would be credited/transferred directly into the Bank accounts of the selected applicants through the Public Finance Management System (PFMS) under the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Programme of the Government.
> **Important Instruction:**


   1. It will be the sole responsibility of the applicant to make sure that he/she is eligible to apply and fulfils all the conditions prescribed for the scholarship.
   1. If the in-eligibility of the applicant is detected at any stage, before or after applying for the scholarship scheme, or during at any stage by verification by authorities, his/her scholarship will be cancelled without any notice. Disciplinary action will be taken against him/her, further, he/she will be blacklisted to opt for a scholarship sponsored by the Central Government for a period of five years.
   1. An incomplete application form and failure to attach the requisite documents will lead to rejection of the application.
   1. All the requisite information should be clearly mentioned in the respective column. The information once is generated on the part of applicants, no change/amendment will be accepted.
   1. Mobile number and Email address of applicants or wards of CAPFs & AR personnel is mandatory so as to inform the candidate of any discrepancies or developments through SMS and Email.

**Wards of deceased/retired and serving personnel of CAPFs/AR may contact:**
Telephone number: 011-23063111
Email: secywarb- mha@nic.in.

metadata.schemeName: Nyaya Mitra Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to facilitate the expeditious disposal of ten to fifteen years old pending court cases. It provides legal advice, case assistance, and Lok Adalat referrals to marginalized litigants by engaging retired officers.

page_content:
# Nyaya Mitra Scheme **Ministry:** Ministry Of Law and Justice | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Public Safety,Law & Justice, Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Litigant, Justice, Court, Resolution, Judiciary | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The scheme "Nyaya Mitra Scheme" was launched by the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, in April 2017, and the scheme aims to facilitate the expeditious disposal of ten to fifteen-year-old pending cases in High Courts and Subordinate Courts. The scheme provides assistance to litigants suffering due to delayed trials by actively identifying cases, offering legal advice, and referring marginalized applicants to Lok Adalats for priority resolution. The applicant must be a retired judicial or executive officer with legal experience who acts as a Nyaya Mitra to support affected individuals. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Justice, and the applications for this scheme are accepted and managed at District Facilitation Centres housed within Common Service Centers.
## Benefits - Expeditious disposal of ten to fifteen-year-old pending cases in High Courts and Subordinate Courts, including matrimonial cases, accident claims, and criminal cases. - Active identification of delayed cases through the National Judicial Data Grid. - Provision of legal advice and connection of litigants to the District Legal Services Authority, Common Service Centers Tele Law, other government agencies, and civil society organisations. - Referral of marginalized applicants to Lok Adalats for prioritized dispute resolution. - Assistance towards prison reforms within the district in coordination with the district judiciary and other stakeholders. - Critical analysis of pending cases to assist Registrar Generals and district judges in understanding bottlenecks and finding solutions. - Coordination with state and district authorities to enable witnesses to arrive on time or within a stipulated time frame for the early disposal of cases. - Execution of follow-up actions such as issuing notices, summons, stays, injunctions, and letters to lower courts for summoning records pursuant to court orders.
## Eligibility Criteria ##### ***For Nyaya Mitras*** - The applicant must be a retired judicial officer or a retired executive officer. - The applicant must possess legal experience or an educational background in law. ##### ***For Beneficiaries (Litigants)*** - The applicant must be a litigant whose case has been languishing in the subordinate courts for more than ten years. - The applicant must be an individual for whom quality legal aid is not available due to social and economic barriers. - The applicant must be suffering due to a delay in investigations or trial.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The applicant must visit the designated District Facilitation Centres housed within the Common Service Centers of the selected districts to seek legal assistance. The designated Nyaya Mitra actively identifies pending cases through the National Judicial Data Grid and reaches out to the affected parties to initiate support. **Step 2:** The applicant must interact with the Nyaya Mitra to undergo a critical analysis of their pending case and understand the specific bottlenecks causing the judicial delay. The Nyaya Mitra then provides necessary legal advice and explores practical solutions in coordination with relevant government departments. **Step 3:** The applicant must follow the guidance of the Nyaya Mitra to connect with the District Legal Services Authority, Common Service Centers Tele Law, or other civil society organizations. Cases identified as suitable are systematically referred to Lok Adalats by the Nyaya Mitra for prioritized and expedited dispute resolution.
##### ***Place of Work*** - The sitting space for the Nyaya Mitra placed at the High Court will be allocated by the respective High Court. - The Nyaya Mitra will be provided sitting space either at the District Legal Services Authority or the District Court, and no clerical support will be provided.

metadata.schemeName: Mass Communication Internship Programme
metadata.briefDescription: The Mass Communication Internship Programme by the Department of Water Resources, River Development, and Ganga Rejuvenation. The intern program will offer work culture and environment knowledge about the functioning of the Government and its departments in information, education, and communication.

page_content:
# Mass Communication Internship Programme **Ministry:** Ministry Of Jal Shakti | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Education, Honorarium, Student, Mass Communication, Intern | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Mass Communication Internship Programme" was launched by the Department of Water Resources, River Development, and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti. The internship programme is short-term exposure designed to engage students in undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate studies in the field of mass communication. The internship offers hands-on experience in media and social media activities, aiming to create awareness about the importance of water resources conservation and management.
> **Framework of internship:** - **First month of internship:** Learn about the department's IEC activities, Create social media content (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn, YouTube), Plan social media strategy, and set targets. - **Second month of internship:** Promote services and raise awareness, Engage and build relationships with the audience, Drive traffic and establish KPIs, Draft press releases for Department events. - **Third month of internship:** Interact and research target audience, Analyze social media results, Publicize National Water Awards to attract applicants, and Draft speeches for senior officials on Department achievements. > **Duration of internship:** The internship duration is a minimum of three months, extendable up to six months on a monthly basis.
> **Number of students for internship:** A maximum of three interns are selected for each internship duration.
> **Terms & Conditions for the Intern:** - Pursue the program with dedication and maintain discipline. - Maintain 90% attendance. - Attend a full-time internship physically in the main secretariat. - Arrange your own accommodation. - Work hours: 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM, unless otherwise permitted. - Follow Department rules and regulations. - Internship is not a job or employment assurance. - Adhere to Department advice on external representations. - Poor performance may result in discontinuation of the internship. - Provide prior notice if disengaging from the internship. - Library use is for reference only; borrowing is not allowed. - Maintain confidentiality and do not disclose Department information.
## Benefits - **Honorarium****:**An honorarium of ₹10,000/- per month will be paid to each intern. - **Certificate:** A certificate will be received upon successful completion of the internship. - **Facilities:** The department provides working space, internet facility, and other necessities as deemed fit by the Heads. - **Placement:** Each selected intern will be posted with a Deputy Secretary, Director, Joint Secretary, or the office of the Secretary (WR, RD & GR) and will work closely with the IEC Section. ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a student. 1. The applicant should be pursuing a BA/MA/PG in mass communication, journalism, public relations, MBA (Marketing)/ related fields or completed their degrees/diplomas in aforesaid course(s) from any recognized college/university. 1. The applicant must have his own laptop for the internship. 1. **Required Skills and Interests:** - Writing, communication, time management, organization, traditional and digital marketing, customer service, relationship building, strategic and analytical thinking, and creativity. 1. **Academic Performance:** - **Undergraduate Students:** 1. Completed/appeared in term end exams of the second year/4th semester of their bachelor's degree. 1. Secured at least 60% or equivalent marks in 12th class.
- **Recent Graduates/PG Students:** 1. Appeared in the final exam or just completed Graduation/PG. 1. Waiting for admission for higher studies. 1. Secured 55% or more cumulative marks in all years/semesters of their graduation/post-graduation. - **Postgraduate Students:** 1. Completed/appeared in term end exams of the first year/2nd semester of their postgraduate program or pursuing research/PhD. 1. Secured at least 55% or equivalent marks in Graduation. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Step 01:** The student downloads the application form [Annexure-I](https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3a70dc40477bc2adceef4d2c90f47eb82/uploads/2023/08/2023081140.pdf) and the format of NOC is in [Annexure-II](https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3a70dc40477bc2adceef4d2c90f47eb82/uploads/2023/08/2023081140.pdf). **Step 02:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required). **Step 03:** Student can email their applications in the prescribed format to: iec-mowr@nic.in.
> **Submission of Report:** At the end of the internship, each intern shall submit a detailed report on the work carried out and. if required, make a presentation on it.
> **Selection Procedure:** Selected interns are advised to contact respective Offices/ Sections in the department for an entry pass during the internship.

metadata.schemeName: Internship Scheme Of The Department Of Economic Affairs
metadata.briefDescription: The Internship Scheme aims to familiarise students with macro-economic policy formulation and economic research. Through this scheme, internship opportunities with token remuneration are provided to eligible Post Graduate and PhD students.

page_content:
# Internship Scheme Of The Department Of Economic Affairs **Ministry:** Ministry Of Finance | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Internship, Student, Postgraduate, Education | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The Department of Economic Affairs of the Ministry of Finance manages the Internship Scheme for PhD or postgraduate students working on specific issues relating to macro-economic management, capital Markets, Economic Reforms, Exchange Management, Foreign Investment in India and India Investment abroad, Monetary Policy, Fiscal Policy, Inflation Management, Debt Market Operation and Debt Management (External & Domestic), Small Savings, Modernization of Budget Documents, Bilateral Investment Treaties, Infrastructure Financing, etc.
> **Objective** 1. To familiarize the selected candidates with the overall process of formulation of economic policies of the Government at a macro level. 1. To provide an opportunity to carry out brief research into a key and specific economic issue/problem faced by the country and offer solutions for the same.
> **Duration** 1. The duration of the Internship maybe 3 to 6 months. 1. Since the time duration is very short, interns would be required to carry out a very intense study to ensure desirable outputs in a short time frame.
> **Slots** 1. The number of Internships will be limited to a maximum of 15 paid interns. 1. Ten additional unpaid interns may also be selected, out of those ranking on top but could not be selected for the paid internship.
> **Attachment** The interns would be exclusively attached to a Joint Secretary / Director / Office of Chief Economic Adviser / Principal Economic Adviser. ## Benefits > **Remuneration** Token remuneration of ₹10,000/- per month per intern for PG students, and of ₹20,000/- per month per intern for PhD students is payable on satisfactory completion of their internship and on submission of their Report/Paper/Feedback.
> **Logistics Support** Interns will be provided with the necessary logistics support, i.e. office space and computer with internet facility.
> **Certificate** The Certificate of Internship shall be issued to the interns on satisfactory completion of their internship of not less than three months and on submission of their Report/Paper/Feedback/Attendance Certificate duly certified by the Divisional Head. ## Eligibility Criteria Outstanding Candidates pursuing Post Graduation or PhD in Economics/ Law/ Finance/ Management from Universities/ Institutions within the top 25 ranks as per the National Institutional Ranking Framework, by the Ministry of Human Resource Development or QS-ranked International Institutes.
**NOTE 1:** The Department reserves all rights for offering an internship to any candidate. **NOTE 2:** An internship can be refused without assigning any reasons.
> **Post-Selection Conditions** 1. Interns, whose performance is unsatisfactory, may be relieved prematurely. 1. The internship is neither a job nor any such assurance thereof in the Department of Economic Affairs. 1. **Submission of Paper:** The interns will have to present a Report/ Paper on the allotted subject to the concerned Divisional Head at the end of the internship. Simultaneously, they are required to give feedback on their experience of the Programme to the concerned Divisional Head. 1. **Declaration of Secrecy:** Interns are required to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement before commencing work. ## Exclusions This program is not meant for graduate students. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Official Portal/Link:** https://mofapp.nic.in/DEA_Internship.aspx **Step 1:** The applicant needs to register on the [MoF-DEA Internship Application Link](https://mofapp.nic.in/DEA_Internship.aspx) of the Ministry of Finance. **Step 2:** In the online, application form, fill in all the mandatory fields: area of interest, duration of availability with dates and three Divisions of their interest, in order of preference on which they would like to work during their internship.
**NOTE 1:** Details of business allocation to DEA and its Divisions are available on [DEA's website](http://dea.gov.in). **NOTE 2:** Applications not received through the web portal will not be considered. **NOTE 3:** The only means of communication between the Department and candidates shall be by email.

page_content:
# Craftsmen Training Scheme **Ministry:** Ministry Of Skill Development And Entrepreneurship | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Skills & Employment | **Tags:** Craftsmen, Training, Skill, Employment, Youth | **Target Beneficiaries:** Individual ## Description The "Craftsmen Training Scheme" was launched by the Directorate General of Training, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of India. The scheme aims to ensure a steady flow of skilled workers in different trades for the domestic industry, to raise quantitatively and qualitatively the industrial production by systematic training, to reduce unemployment among the educated youth by providing them with employable skills, and to cultivate and nurture a technical and industrial attitude in the minds of the younger generation. The scheme provides systematic vocational training through a network of Industrial Training Institutes and National Skill Training Institutes located all over the country, offering comprehensive skill development programs in various trades and conducting All India Trade Tests for certification.
## Benefits ##### ***Vocational Training and Skill Development*** - **Training Duration:** Varies from 6 months to 2 years, depending on the trade.- **Trade Certification:** National Council for Vocational Training certificate upon successful completion.- **Skill Development:** Hands-on practical training in various industrial trades.- **Employment Opportunities:** Enhanced employability in domestic and international markets. ##### ***Training Infrastructure and Facilities*** - **Training Network:** Access to 15,042 Industrial Training Institutes and 33 National Skill Training Institutes.- **Modern Equipment:** Training on the latest industrial equipment and technology.- **Expert Instruction:** Training by qualified instructors and industry experts.- **Workshop Facilities:** Well-equipped workshops for practical training. ##### ***Assessment and Certification*** - **All India Trade Tests:** Conducted by the Directorate General of Training under the aegis of the National Council for Vocational Training at the end of training.- **National Recognition:** Certificates recognized across India for employment.- **Industry Standards:** Training aligned with current industry requirements and standards. ##### ***Conditions*** - Minimum 80% attendance is required to appear in the Final Trade Test. - Regular participation in practical training sessions and workshops. - Compliance with the institute rules and regulations. - Successful completion of periodic assessments and tests.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be an Indian citizen. - The applicant must meet the age requirements as specified for different trades (generally between 14 to 40 years). - The applicant must have completed the minimum educational qualifications as prescribed for specific trades (ranging from 8th standard to 12th standard). - The applicant must be able to read and write in the local language / Hindi / English. - The applicant must be physically and medically fit to undergo the specific trade training. - The applicant must not have any physical disabilities that would prevent them from performing the trade activities. - The applicant must meet specific requirements for certain trades (such as color vision for electrical trades). - The applicant must demonstrate basic aptitude for the chosen trade.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The candidate must visit the Industrial Training Institute and obtain the prescribed application form. **Step 2:** The applicant should fill out the application form completely with accurate personal details, educational background, trade preference, and attach all required documents with proper attestation. **Step 3:** The candidate must pay the prescribed application and training fees as applicable and submit the completed application form along with all supporting documents to the authorised staff of the Institute, within the specified deadline. _*Request a receipt or acknowledgement from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, and a unique identification number (if applicabl_e). ***Post-Application Processes*** **Step 1:** _Merit List and Selection Process_ The institutes will prepare merit lists based on educational qualifications and other criteria, and selected candidates will be notified about their admission through official communication channels. **Step 2:** _Admission Confirmation and Document Verification_ Selected candidates must report to the institute on the specified date for document verification, admission confirmation, and completion of remaining formalities, including medical examination if required. **Step 3:** _Training Commencement_ After successful admission confirmation, candidates will begin their vocational training as per the institute's academic calendar and training schedule for their respective trades. > **Application Deadlines** Application deadlines vary by institute and are typically announced before the commencement of each academic session (usually April-May for the August session and October-November for the February session).
