metadata.schemeName: Nagar Van Yojana
metadata.nodalMinistryName: Ministry Of Environment,forests and climate change
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to develop 400 Nagar Vans and 200 Nagar Vatikas to create bio-diverse green spaces in urban areas. The scheme provides a grant of ₹4,00,000/- per hectare to Municipalities, Urban Local Bodies, and Institutions for afforestation and biodiversity conservation.

page_content:
# Nagar Van Yojana **Ministry:** Ministry Of Environment,forests and climate change | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Municipality, Institution, Forest, Grant, Environment, Plantation, Biodiversity | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme "Nagar Van Yojana" was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. The scheme aims to develop 400 Nagar Vans and 200 Nagar Vatikas to create green spaces in urban areas by protecting land from degradation. The scheme provides a one-time development grant of ₹4,00,000/- per hectare up to a maximum of ₹2,00,00,000/- for 50 hectares to cover costs such as fencing, soil-moisture conservation, theme-based plantations, and maintenance of tree cover. The applicant must formulate a detailed project proposal, include a Keyhole Markup Language map on a 1:10,000 or larger scale, ensure a commitment to bear the balance cost, and submit the plan for the identified land. The scheme is implemented by the State Forest Department and the National Afforestation and Eco-Development Board. The applications for this scheme are accepted offline through the concerned State Forest Department offices.
## Benefits - The Ministry will provide a one-time development and non-recurring grant of ₹4,00,000/- per hectare. - The maximum financial assistance for a Nagar Van is limited to ₹2,00,00,000/- for 50 hectares. - The State Forest Department is permitted to engage one technical consultant at a cost of ₹40,000/- per month until the completion of the project for monitoring and other works. - The State Forest Department will receive a lump sum grant of ₹50,000/- per project for monitoring, evaluation, and meeting overhead expenses. **Mode of Disbursal:** The funds will be released directly to the respective State Forest Departments from the National Fund under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority. **Frequency and Validity:** The grant is a one-time assistance, released in two separate instalments, and financial assistance is provided to each Nagar Van or Nagar Vatika for the first two years only.
##### ***Components*** - Fencing of the identified area must be undertaken. - Establishment and maintenance of woodlots or tree cover with an emphasis on locally appropriate species must be carried out. - Theme-based plantations such as Smriti Van or Nakshatra Van may be established. - Plants representing floral biodiversity, including ornamental trees, medicinal plants, and fruit trees, must be included. - Irrigation and rain water harvesting facilities must be established. - Establishment and maintenance of public conveniences, drinking water facilities, benches, walkways, and cycle tracks must be completed. - An Information and Extension Centre, including display boards and information brochures, must be established and maintained.
##### ***Conditions*** - The first instalment of 70% of the sanctioned amount is released to the State Forest Department after the approval of the project by the National Authority. - The remaining second instalment of 30% is released after 60% utilization of the first instalment and on the submission of the utilisation certificate and progress report. - The State Forest Department must further release the portion of the grant meant for an implementing agency within a period of seven days. - A corpus of the entire funds received by the implementing agency must be maintained as an interest-bearing account in a government or public sector bank. - Detailed accounts of receipts and expenditures must be maintained by each implementing agency and the State Forest Department. - All funds received by the implementing agency must be subjected to an annual audit by a chartered accountant.
## Eligibility Criteria - The applicant must be a Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Municipality, Urban Local Body, State Forest Department, Educational Institution, University, Government Organisation, or Non-Government Organisation. - The applicant must have possession of the proposed land. - The applicant must provide a commitment to bear the balance cost of the project beyond the provided grant. - The applicant must ensure that the proposed area is situated on forest land or other vacant non-forest public land. - The applicant must formulate a Development cum Management Plan with year-wise details of works under different components. ##### ***For Nagar Van*** - The applicant must develop the Nagar Van over a minimum area of 10 hectares. - The applicant must restrict the maximum area for grant calculation to 50 hectares. - The applicant must ensure the site is located within a 5-kilometre limit of the Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, or Municipality. - The applicant must maintain a minimum of 2/3rd of the Nagar Van area under woodland or tree cover. ##### ***For Nagar Vatika*** - The applicant must develop the Nagar Vatika in a minimum area of 1 hectare. - The applicant must restrict the maximum area of the Nagar Vatika to 10 hectares. - The applicant must ensure the site is located strictly within the city limits or congested parts of the cities. ##### ***Post-Selection Conditions*** - The applicant must keep all Nagar Vans and Nagar Vatikas open and accessible to the city dwellers and general public, subject to suitable restrictions. - The applicant should encourage a Public-Private Partnership mode to ensure the active participation of people, students, and other stakeholders in planning, implementation, and management. - The applicant should select trees from species that are best suited for local conditions. - The applicant should place an emphasis on enriching biodiversity, planting fruit-bearing trees, and cultivating medicinal plants. - The applicant should ensure sufficient revenue generation for maintenance by levying user fees, receiving grants from other agencies, and promoting economic activities like the sale of saplings or processed forest products from the first year. - The applicant should encourage the use of locally available material, energy conservation, and waste recycling.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline _*The application process entails the manual or offline formulation and submission of detailed project proposals by the implementing agencies._ _*There is no centralized online portal for direct applications by implementing agencies, as all submissions and communications occur strictly through the respective State Forest Departments._
**Step 1:** The implementing agency must formulate a comprehensive project proposal for the establishment of the Nagar Van or Nagar Vatika, ensuring that all mandatory documents and boundary maps are prepared in the prescribed formats. **Step 2:** The implementing agency must submit the formulated project proposal physically to the concerned State Forest Department for initial scrutiny and verification of the land details. **Step 3:** The State Forest Department will scrutinize the submitted proposal, verify the claims, and subsequently forward the approved applications to the National Afforestation and Eco-Development Board under the Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change. **Step 4:** The National Afforestation and Eco-Development Board will examine all received proposals from the State Forest Departments and present them to the National Authority for final consideration and the release of funds.
##### ***Post-Application Processes*** **Step 5:** The National Authority will accord approval and release the first instalment of the allocated grant directly to the respective State Forest Department as per the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act rules. **Step 6:** The State Forest Department must further release the designated portion of the grant to the respective implementing agency within a period of seven days from the receipt of the funds.

page_content:
# Saraswati Vidya Yojana: Free Distribution of Bicycles - DNH&DD

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Student, Girls, Bicycles, School, Social Empowerment | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra

## Description
“Free Distribution of Bicycles'' under the “Saraswati Vidya Yojana”has been implemented by the Directorate of Education, U.T. Administration Of DNH & DD. Under this scheme, bicycles are provided free of cost to all the girl students, studying in class VIII(8) each year in the Govt. & Govt. aided schools/ Institutes of the U.T. Administration.
> **Objective of the "Saraswati Vidya Yojana”:**

The UT Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu has launched “Saraswati Vidya Yojana”  on 25th February, 2021, for the girl students of UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. The scheme aims to encourage girl students to continue education keeping in view the aim of:- “Beti Bachao Beti Padhao”.
> **Objective of the "Free Distribution of Bicycles" Sub-scheme:**

The objective of the scheme is to retain the girl students at Secondary & Higher Secondary stage and thereby decreasing the Dropout of the girl students by providing Bicycles to the girl students of class VIII to commute to school.

## Benefits
- Bicycles will be provided to all the girl students.

## Eligibility Criteria
1. The applicant should be a girl.
   1. The applicant should be a student.
   1. The applicant should be studying in class VIII(8) in Government and Government Aided School of the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

## Exclusions
- The girl students once availed the benefit will not be provided with the same in any of the subsequent year.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Offline
- The Head Master/ In-charge Head Master will provide the number of enrolment of Girls in Std. VIII in Government and Government Aided Schools to the District Education Office.

**Note:**

  - The girl student does not required to make any application individually.
  - Bicycles will be provided to schools at the time of commencement of the New Academic Year as per the requirement of the respective schools.

metadata.schemeName: Banglashree for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: State Capital Investment Subsidy (CIS)
metadata.briefDescription: “State Capital Investment Subsidy (CIS)” incentives under “Banglashree for MSMEs” scheme implemented by the MSMEs Department, Government of West Bengal, aims to provide Capital Investment Subsidy for its approved project to an eligible micro or small enterprise.

page_content:
# Banglashree for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: State Capital Investment Subsidy (CIS) **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** West Bengal | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** MSME, Incentives, Subsidy, Financial Assistance, Entrepreneurship | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme “State Capital Investment Subsidy” is a sub-scheme under the “Banglashree for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises” scheme. It was launched on 1st April 2020 by the Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal, and shall remain in force till 31st March 2025. > **Objectives of the "Banglashree for MSME” Scheme** The objective of the scheme is to extend fiscal incentives to encourage entrepreneurs to set up Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises with a view to focusing on the balanced development of MSMEs across the State and creating a sustainable ecosystem in the MSME sector which can maximize the utilization of resource, generate new employment and widen the area of operation to make the State emerge as the MSME leader in the country. > **Objectives of the "State Capital Investment Subsidy" Scheme** Through this incentive, an eligible micro or small enterprise located in Zone C, D & E area will be entitled to State Capital Investment Subsidy for its approved project. ## Benefits The enterprise will be provided a subsidy as a percentage of the fixed capital Investment (FCA) for its approved project as follows: ***Micro Enterprise:*** 25% for Zone C; 40% for Zone D; 60% for Zone E. **Small Enterprise:** 15% for Zone C; 30% for Zone D; 40% for Zone E. - An additional subsidy of 20% on State Capital Investment Subsidy normally admissible will be provided to all eligible micro and small enterprises wholly owned (100%) by women, SC/ST, and minority community entrepreneurs. - An eligible micro or small enterprise wholly owned by women, SC/ST, and minority community entrepreneurs and set up in Zone – A and B will be entitled to a subsidy as a percentage of the fixed capital Investment (FCA) as follows: - _15% for Micro Enterprise, and 10% for Small Enterprise_ **NOTE 1:** The subsidy normally admissible and additional subsidy taken together will not exceed ₹ 50,00,00/- for a Small Enterprise located in Zone C & D. **NOTE 2:** The subsidy normally admissible and additional subsidy taken together will not exceed ₹ 75,00,000/- for a Small Enterprise located in Zone E. ## Eligibility Criteria - The business/organization should be a Micro/ Small/ Medium Enterprise. - The business/organization should belong to the manufacturing sector. - The business/organization should have started production on or after 1st April 2019. - The business/organization should be in the private sector/ cooperative sector/ joint sector undertaking or should be a company/ undertaking owned and managed by the State Government or the Industrial SHGs. - The Date of Commencement of Commercial Production (DOCCP) should be between 1st April 2020 to 31st March 2025. ## Exclusions > **Enterprises Excluded from this Scheme** - Enterprises registered and for which eligibility certificates have been issued /incentives have been sanctioned and/ or disbursed under the respective Incentive Scheme of the State. - Enterprises registered and for which eligibility certificates have been issued in terms of the respective Incentive Scheme of the State but no sanction or disbursement of incentive has been made. - Enterprises commenced production before 01.04.2019 and applied for incentive under the respective Incentive Scheme of the State within the stipulated date.
> ***Negative List Of Industries*** 1. Sponge Iron Factory. 2. Bricks (Excluding Fly Ash bricks, Sand lime Bricks, Refractory Bricks). 3. Any other industry notified by the State Govt. for inclusion in this list.
> **Items excluded while calculating the investment made in Plant & Machinery** - Equipment such as tools, jigs, dies, moulds and spare parts for maintenance and the cost of consumable stores. - Installation of Plant and Machinery. - Research and development equipment and pollution control equipment. - Power generation set and extra transformer installed by the enterprise as per the regulations of the State Electricity Board. - Bank charges and service charges paid to the National Small Industries Corporations or the State Small Industries Corporations. - Procurement or installation of cables, wiring, bus bars, electrical control panels (not mounted on individual machines), oil circuit breakers or miniature circuit breakers which are necessarily to be used for providing electrical power to the Plant and Machinery or for safety measures. - Gas producer plant. - Transportation charges for indigenous machinery from the place of their manufacture to the site of the enterprise. - Charges paid for technical know-how for the erection of the Plant and Machinery. - Such storage tanks which store raw materials and finished products only and are not linked to the manufacturing process. - Fire fighting equipment. **NOTE:** The cost of any second-hand plant and machinery purchased and installed for implementation of the project will be excluded in the calculation of the cost of the plant and machinery. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > ***Registration Process:*** **Step 1:** Visit the [Shilpasathi Portal](https://silpasathi.wb.gov.in/) and click ‘[Apply Online](https://silpasathi.wb.gov.in/)’. On the next screen, click ‘Create New’ for new registration. **Step 2:** Select the Applicant Type (Industry /Business /Commercial /Charitable Society/ Govt. entity) and enter the Registration Number. **Step 3:** On the ‘User Registration’ page, fill in all the mandatory fields and click ‘Register’.
> ***Application Process:*** **Step 1:** Visit the [Shilpasathi Portal](https://silpasathi.wb.gov.in/) and click ‘[Apply Online](https://silpasathi.wb.gov.in/)’. **Step 2:** Login to the portal using your username & password or via OTP using your registered mobile number. **Step 3:** You will be directed to the user dashboard. Click ‘ALL SERVICES’ and then select 'MSME Incentive' from the list of services. **Step 4:** Click ‘Create CAF’. Your CAF ID will be created. Click ‘Apply Online’ to proceed. **Step 5:** Fill in the "eligibility form" and click “Save and Continue” to get redirected to the common application form (CAF). **Step 6:** In the CAF, fill in all the mandatory fields, and click “Update and Continue” to preview the form. **Step 7:** After the form gets submitted, you will be taken to the “Dashboard” to view the application status. **Step 8:** From the Dashboard, continue with the application by clicking “Click to Proceed”. When done click “Save” to save the updated information. **Step 9:** Click "Preview" to preview the form before the final submission. **Step 10:** On the next screen, click "Go to Application" to fill out the "Online Form - A" application. **Step 11:** You will be taken to the "APPLY SUBSIDY" section to check year-wise subsidy items of the respective application you intend to apply for. Once complete, click "SAVE". **Step 12:** You will be taken to the "FILL UP SUBSIDY" tab. Provide the year-wise subsidy details for the incentive, and click "Add More" to see the multiple-year or year-wise breakup. **Step 13:** Upload the relevant documents, preview the details, click “VERIFY & SUBMIT”, check the declaration box and click “Submit Application”. **Step 14:** On final submission of Form-A application, you will be provided an application reference number. Use this number to check the status of your application.
> ***Date of submission of first application:*** _Within 12 months from the DOCCP or within 12 months from the date of notification of Banglashree, whichever is later._
> ***Helpdesk*** Protiti, 23, Abanindranath Tagore Sarani (Camac Street), Kolkata - 700017, West Bengal, India; **Phone:** +91 33 2255 3700; **Fax:** +91 33 2255 3737; **Email:** silpa.sathi@wbidc.com. **For any technical query or any critical issues faced while applying please mail to our Quick Response Team at:** qrt.silpasathiwb@gmail.com **Silpa Sathi Single Window Cell - Helpline Number (Toll-free):** 1800-345-5562

metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote investment in the Solar Equipments Sector by providing additional financial incentives to eligible enterprises. It supports investment, employment generation, energy cost reduction, and access to finance.

page_content:
# Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme (RIPS): Solar Equipments Sector **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** MSMEs, Entrepreneurship, Incentive, Business, Solar Equipments Sector | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The "Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme (RIPS)" is an umbrella scheme launched by the Commissioner Industries, Commerce, and CSR Department, Rajasthan. It aims to generate employment opportunities and promote rapid, sustainable, and balanced economic growth in the State of Rajasthan. Effective from December 12, 2019, to March 26, 2026, this initiative provides benefits to eligible manufacturing and services sector enterprises. This component aims to promote investment in the Solar Equipments Sector by providing additional financial incentives to eligible enterprises. It supports investment, employment generation, energy cost reduction, and access to finance.
## Benefits - **Additional Investment Subsidy:** 25% additional Investment Subsidy on State Tax Due and Deposited (STDD) for 7 years. - **Additional Employment Generation Subsidy:** 25% additional Employment Generation Subsidy through reimbursement of the employer’s contribution towards Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) and Employees’ State Insurance (ESI), subject to an overall upper limit of 75% per employee, for 7 years. - **Electricity Duty Exemption:** Exemption from payment of Electricity Duty for an additional 3 years. - **Interest Subsidy:** 5% Interest Subsidy on term loan taken from Financial Institutions, State Financial Institutions, or Banks recognized by the Reserve Bank of India, for investment in plant and machinery, for 5 years, subject to a maximum of ₹25,00,000/- per year. **Or,** - **Capital Subsidy:** Capital Subsidy equivalent to 20% of investment made on plant and machinery, subject to a maximum of ₹50,00,000/-.
## Eligibility Criteria - Entrepreneurs are eligible to apply for the scheme.
## Exclusions Investment not eligible for benefits of subsidies and/or exemptions under the Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme - Investment for manufacturing tobacco, tobacco products and pan masala. - Investment made in cow beef processing units. - Investment made in retail/trading activities. - Any activity which is prohibited by Central/State laws.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online - via CSC > **Mode of Online Application: e-Mitra** - The applicant can submit the online application by visiting the nearest [e-Mitra](https://emitra.rajasthan.gov.in/emitra/home) center or by using their own e-Mitra account. - The application is free of cost.

page_content:
# West Bengal Textile Incentive Scheme: Power Subsidy **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** West Bengal | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Textile, Incentives, Waiver, Entrepreneurship, Subsidy, Reimbursement, Power Subsidy | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme “Power Subsidy” is a sub scheme under “West Bengal Textile Incentive Scheme”. It was launched on 13 December, 2022, by the Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Textiles , Government of West Bengal, and shall remain valid upto five years. > **Objective of the "West Bengal Textile Incentive Scheme” Scheme:** The object of the scheme is to extend fiscal incentives to textile sector across the entire value chain starting from fibre to stitched garments for setting up such units in the State. The focus is on accelerated and focused development of the textiles sector across the state. This shall enable to maximize the utilization of resources, generate new employment and widen the area of operation to make the state emerge as the preferred destination for investment in the textile sector. > **Objective of the "Power Subsidy" Scheme:** Through this incentive, an eligible textile sector enterprise for its approved project will be entitled to power subsidy on electricity consumption for 5 years from the date of commencement of production from any licensee power supplier on reimbursement basis for the different manufacturing activity. ## Benefits - ₹ 2,00,00,000/- to 50,00,000/- per annum for 5 years.
## Eligibility Criteria - Industries in the manufacturing and processing of textiles, apparel and technical textiles products. - The unit should have started production on or after 1st April 2022. - The units may be in the private sector, co-operative sector, joint sector as also companies/undertakings owned or managed by the State Government. - Shall not be applicable to the industrial units/enterprises. - The project should have been approved and sanctioned by a Central Financial Institution or Commercial Banks or State Financial Institutions. - The unit should hold an Registration Certificate, Date of Commencement Certificate and Eligibility Certificate issued by the Director of Textiles on satisfaction of arrangement. ## Exclusions - The incentives shall not be applicable to the industrial units/ enterprises that have been registered and for which eligibility certificates have been issued /incentives have been sanctioned and disbursed under the respective Incentive Scheme of the State. - That has been registered and for which eligibility certificates have been issued in terms of the respective Incentive Scheme of the State but no claim and sanction of incentive has been made. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > ***Registration Process******:*** **Step 1:** Visit the registration page of the [Official Website](https://textiles.wb.gov.in/register). **Step 2:** Fill in all the mandatory details in that window and click on “Register”. **Step 3:** You will be registered successfully with a confirmation. > **Application Process****:** **Step 1:** Visit the user login page of the [Official website](https://textiles.wb.gov.in/register). **Step 2:** Login with your registered Mail Id and Password.. **Step 3:** Fill up the eligible form. **Step 4:** Check your eligibility in the portal. **Step 5:** Fill up your Common Application Form (CAF). **Step 6:** Fill up Form A and Form C (if any). **Step 7**: Download and Self sign Form A and Form C (if any). **Step 8:** Upload signed copy of Form A and copy of Form C (if any). **Step 9:** Submit Your Application. > **Helpdesk****:** [Directorate of Textile](https://textiles.wb.gov.in/contact-us).

page_content:
# The West Bengal Incentive Scheme: Additional Incentive on Generation of Employment

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** West Bengal | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Tourism, Incentives, Waiver, Tourism Units, Entrepreneurship, Subsidy, Reimbursement, Employment Generation | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra

## Description
“Additional Incentive on Generation of Employment” is a sub scheme under “The West Bengal Incentive Scheme 2021”. It was launched on 22nd February, 2021, by the Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal, and shall remain valid upto 31st December, 2025.
> **Objective of the “West Bengal Incentive Scheme” scheme:**

The objective of the Scheme is to provide financial assistance and help enthusiastic intending or prospective entrepreneurs to start their own business as a self-employed youth who will become an employer in upcoming days and generate more employment.
> **Objective of the “Additional Incentive on Generation of Employment” scheme:**

Through this incentive, an eligible unit will be entitled to an additional incentive for employment generation for paying its contribution towards Employees State Insurance (ESI) and Employees Provident Fund (EPF) Scheme.

## Benefits
- Group A, B, C & D areas: 60% for a period of 5 years
- Special Areas: 60% for a period of 10 years.

## Eligibility Criteria
- The Scheme shall be generally applicable to all eligible tourism projects/units/expansion projects of existing units set up on or after the effective date (i.e. 22nd February, 2021)  of this incentive scheme.

       Or,

  - Eligible Hotel Units who started their commercial operation on or after 7th January, 2015 to 31st December, 2020 but could not apply under previous scheme 2015 due to absence of a Bar in the Hotel.
  - The units may be in the private sector, co-operative sector, joint sector as also companies/undertakings owned or managed by the State Government.

metadata.schemeName: Application for Subsidy for Cinema/Film Studio/Other Film related Permanent Infrastructure
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme provides financial assistance to applicants for establishing and upgrading cinema halls, film studios, and other film-related infrastructure that supports film production, post-production, exhibition, and allied activities.

page_content:
# Application for Subsidy for Cinema/Film Studio/Other Film related Permanent Infrastructure **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship, Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Subsidy, Cinema, Film Studio, Infrastructure, Film Production | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme “Application for Subsidy for Cinema/Film Studio/Other Film related Permanent Infrastructure” has been introduced by the Culture and Archaeology Department, Government of Chhattisgarh under the Chhattisgarh Film Policy, 2021 to promote the development of permanent infrastructure that strengthens the state's film ecosystem. The scheme provides financial assistance to eligible applicants for establishing and upgrading cinema halls, film studios, and other film-related infrastructure that supports film production, post-production, exhibition, and allied activities. By encouraging private investment in modern film infrastructure, the initiative aims to enhance Chhattisgarh's capacity as a preferred destination for filmmaking, generate employment opportunities, and foster the sustainable growth of the state's film industry.
## Benefits - Capital subsidy of 15% of the eligible capital expenditure for the establishment of film studios, permanent film production infrastructure, installation of film-related equipment, and the development of museums, theme parks, and other permanent film-related infrastructure. - Maximum financial assistance of ₹500 lakh (₹5 crore) under the scheme. - The scheme promotes the creation of modern film infrastructure, encouraging investment and strengthening the film ecosystem in Chhattisgarh.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must establish a Film Studio, Film Production Infrastructure, Museum, Theme Park, or other permanent film-related infrastructure in Chhattisgarh. 1. The project must involve a minimum capital investment of ₹100 lakh (₹1 Crore). 1. The infrastructure created must be of a permanent nature and related to film production or promotion activities. 1. The project must comply with the provisions of the Chhattisgarh Film Policy 2021.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Application Process** **Step 1: Portal Access and Login** The applicant (or the authorized operator) must visit the [Sewa Setu Portal](https://sewasetu.cgstate.gov.in/home?lang=en) and login using either their Citizen credentials or through the Lok Sewa Kendra (LSK) login system to proceed with the application. **Step 2: Application Submission** The user must navigate to the application form of the scheme that they wish to apply for. In the form, enter all the required details accurately. In the form, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload all the mandatory documents in the specified format and size. Ensure that all documents are clear, legible, and in the accepted file format before uploading. Once all required documents are successfully uploaded and the entered information is verified by the applicant, they must finally submit the application. **Step 3: Application Reference Number Generation** The portal generates an Application Reference Number (ARN). The applicant should save the ARN for all future correspondence and status tracking regarding their submitted application. > **Post-Application Process** **Step 1:** Preliminary Verification by Film Facilitation Cell The application is routed online to the Film Facilitation Cell, where the submitted application details and supporting documents are examined for completeness and correctness. **Step 2:** Decision by Film Facilitation Cell If the application is found satisfactory, it is forwarded online to the Deputy Director for further examination. If any discrepancies or deficiencies are identified, the application is returned to the applicant for correction and resubmission. **Step 3:** Examination by Deputy Director The Deputy Director reviews the application, supporting documents, and other relevant records to assess eligibility and compliance with the prescribed guidelines. **Step 4:** Decision by Deputy Director Based on the examination: If approved, the application is forwarded to the Director for final review and approval. If additional information or documents are required, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application is found ineligible, it is rejected with recorded remarks. **Step 5:** Review by Director The Director scrutinizes the application, recommendations, and supporting documents to ensure that all requirements and eligibility conditions have been fulfilled. **Step 6:** Final Decision by Director Based on the review: If approved, the Director applies the Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) through the system. If additional information or documents are required, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application does not meet the prescribed criteria, it is rejected with recorded remarks. **Step 7:** Generation of Digitally Signed Sanction Order Upon approval, the system generates a Digitally Signed Sanction Order using the Director's Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). **Step 8:** Notification to Applicant The applicant is notified regarding the approval of the application and issuance of the Digitally Signed Sanction Order. **Step 9:** Application Closure After successful issuance of the Digitally Signed Sanction Order and completion of all processing formalities, the application status is updated as Completed and the case is formally closed in the system.

page_content:
# Grant-in-aid to Gaushalas **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Gaushala Grant, Cow Shelter, Animal Welfare | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description Started in 1st january, 2017, the scheme "Grant-in-aid to Gaushalas" by the Directorate of Gopalan, Government of Rajasthan, aims to support cattle welfare through providing financial assistance for fodder and water to registered Gaushalas and Kanjihouses. It benefits eligible institutions maintaining cattle. The assistance is provided for a maximum period of 270 days. An additional 90 days of assistance is provided as a special phase for visually impaired and disabled cattle in Gaushalas, and for male cattle (Nandi) maintained in Nandi Shalas.
## Benefits - **Fodder and Water Assistance:** ₹50/- per day per large cattle; ₹25/- per day per small cattle; provided for a maximum of 270 days. - **Additional Support:** Extra 90 days of assistance for disabled cattle and male cattle kept in Nandishalas (special phase).
## Eligibility Criteria - **Beneficiary Category:** Eligible registered cow shelters/Kanji house under Nidhi Niyam 2016 in Rajasthan - **Eligibility for the scheme:** 1. Cow shelter registered for 1 year. 1. Maintenance of a minimum of 100 cattle in the cow shelter and running regularly for 1 year. 1. Maintenance of 500 male cattle at the district level Nandi Shala. 1. Eligible after the maintenance of 250 male cattle after the construction of the Panchayat Samiti Nandi Shala. 1. Panchayat Samiti Nandishala should maintain 250 male cattle after construction.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Registration Process:** **Step 1:** Visit the official portal of the [Directorate of Gopalan](https://gopalanapp.rajasthan.gov.in/Default.aspx). Scroll down and then click on "Online Application for Gaushala Aid". User will be redirected to the Rajasthan Single Sign On portal: [https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/.](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/) **Step 2:** On the homepage, click on the "[Register here](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/register)" tab. **Step 3:** Select ‘Jan Aadhaar’ option for registration under the ‘Citizen’ tab. **Step 4:** Complete the registration process by entering your Jan Aadhaar Number. **Step 5:** After successful registration, you will receive a User ID (SSO ID) and a password. These credentials will allow you to check your application status and apply for the scheme in the future. > **Application Process:** **Step 1:** To apply under the scheme, revisit the official portal of Rajasthan Single Sign On: [https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/) **Step 2:** On the homepage, click on the "[Log in to RajSSO](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/signin)" tab. **Step 3:** Enter your username (SSO ID), password, and Captcha, then click ‘Login’. **Step 4:** Once logged in, update your profile. **Step 5:** Click on the "Gopalan" icon, then click on the "Apply Online For New Gaushala Aid" option. **Step 6:** Fill in the required information, and upload all necessary documents on the online portal. **Step 7:** After entering the information and uploading the documents, make sure to Submit/Save/Print your application form.

page_content:
# Gaushala Biogas Sahbhagita Yojna **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Rajasthan | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Gaushala, Biogas Plant, Cow Dung Utilization, Organic Farming | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description Launched on 7th june 2018, the scheme "Gaushala Biogas Sahbhagita Yojna" by the Directorate of Gopalan, Government of Rajasthan aims to increase income and achieve self-reliance in electricity through the installation of biogas plants of 100 cubic meters or more capacity in 25 selected registered Gaushalas. It focuses on making Gaushalas self-reliant in electricity and providing organic manure to farmers for biological agriculture.
## Benefits - **Financial Assistance (Subsidy):** 50% of the total cost of biogas plant installation is provided as subsidy, subject to a maximum limit of ₹40,00,000/-. - **Cost Sharing by Beneficiary:** The remaining 50% cost is borne by the beneficiary gaushala institution. - **BOOT Model Option:** The beneficiary can opt for the BOOT (Build Own Operate Transfer) model, where the implementing agency bears the remaining cost.
## Eligibility Criteria - The gaushala should be a registered gaushala. - The gaushala should have ownership of more than 25 bigha of land. - The gaushala should be maintaining at least 1,000 cattle. - The gaushala should be among the selected 25 gaushalas under the scheme.
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Registration Process:** **Step 1:** Visit the official portal of the [Directorate of Gopalan](https://gopalanapp.rajasthan.gov.in/Default.aspx). Scroll down and then click on "Online Application for Gaushala Aid". User will be redirected to the Rajasthan Single Sign On portal: [https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/.](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/) **Step 2:** On the homepage, click on the "[Register here](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/register)" tab. **Step 3:** Select ‘Jan Aadhaar’ option for registration under the ‘Citizen’ tab. **Step 4:** Complete the registration process by entering your Jan Aadhaar Number. **Step 5:** After successful registration, you will receive a User ID (SSO ID) and a password. These credentials will allow you to check your application status and apply for the scheme in the future. > **Application Process:** **Step 1:** To apply under the scheme, revisit the official portal of Rajasthan Single Sign On: [https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/) **Step 2:** On the homepage, click on the "[Log in to RajSSO](https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/signin)" tab. **Step 3:** Enter your username (SSO ID), password, and Captcha, then click ‘Login’. **Step 4:** Once logged in, update your profile. **Step 5:** Click on the "Gopalan" icon, then click on the "Apply Online For New Gaushala Aid" option. **Step 6:** Fill in the required information, and upload all necessary documents on the online portal. **Step 7:** After entering the information and uploading the documents, make sure to Submit/Save/Print your application form.

# Application for Subsidy in Feature Film **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Subsidy, Feature Film, Cinematic Works, Film Industry | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme “Application for Subsidy in Feature Film” has been introduced by the Culture and Archaeology Department, Government of Chhattisgarh under the Chhattisgarh Film Policy, 2021 to encourage the production of feature films in the state by providing financial assistance to eligible filmmakers and producers. The scheme offers subsidies for the production of feature films in accordance with the prescribed eligibility criteria and guidelines. By supporting quality filmmaking and creative cinematic works, the initiative aims to strengthen the film industry in Chhattisgarh, promote local talent, generate employment opportunities, and showcase the state's cultural heritage, scenic locations, and artistic excellence on national and international platforms.
## Benefits **First Feature Film** - Up to ₹1 Crore or 25% of the Cost of Production (COP), whichever is lower, if at least 50% of the shooting is completed in Chhattisgarh. - Up to ₹1.75 Crore or 25% of the Cost of Production (COP), whichever is lower, if at least 75% of the shooting is completed in Chhattisgarh. **Second Feature Film (Same Banner and Same Producer)** - Up to ₹1.25 Crore or 25% of the Cost of Production (COP), whichever is lower, for 50% shooting in Chhattisgarh. - Up to ₹2 Crore or 25% of the Cost of Production (COP), whichever is lower, for 75% shooting in Chhattisgarh. **Third and Subsequent Feature Films (Same Banner and Same Producer)** - Up to ₹1.50 Crore or 25% of the Cost of Production (COP), whichever is lower, for 50% shooting in Chhattisgarh. - Up to ₹2.25 Crore or 25% of the Cost of Production (COP), whichever is lower, for 75% shooting in Chhattisgarh. > **NOTE:** - A maximum of 60 feature films (20 first films, 20 second films, and 20 third/subsequent films) are eligible for subsidy in each financial year. - Attractive discounts on room bookings at accommodation units operated by the Chhattisgarh Tourism Board. - 30% of the approved subsidy is released after obtaining CBFC certification, while the remaining 70% is released after the film is commercially exhibited in at least 15 theatres/centres across a minimum of two states. - Producers may receive an additional incentive of up to ₹25 lakh or 50% of the admissible subsidy (whichever is lower) for providing significant acting opportunities to eligible local artists from Chhattisgarh in nationally released feature films.

## Eligibility Criteria 1. The film must be a Hindi or English feature film,produced in accordance with the provisions of the Chhattisgarh Film Policy, 2021. 1. At least 20% of the supporting artists, technical crew, and ground staff must be permanent residents of Chhattisgarh. 1. The feature film must be At least 50% or 75% of the total shooting days (depending on the subsidy slab) must be completed within the State of Chhattisgarh. 1. For the second and subsequent film subsidy, the application must be submitted by the same producer under the same banner. 1. The number of shooting days in Chhattisgarh must be certified by the District Collector of the concerned district. 1. To claim the additional incentive for local artists, at least 5 principal artists/characters in the film must be permanent residents of Chhattisgarh.

## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Application Process** **Step 1: Portal Access and Login** The applicant (or the authorized operator) must visit the [Sewa Setu Portal](https://sewasetu.cgstate.gov.in/home?lang=en), and login using either their Citizen credentials or through the Lok Sewa Kendra (LSK) login system to proceed with the application. **Step 2: Application Submission** The user must navigate to the application form of the scheme that they wish to apply for. In the form, enter all the required details accurately. In the form, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload all the mandatory documents in the specified format and size. Ensure that all documents are clear, legible, and in the accepted file format before uploading. Once all required documents are successfully uploaded and the entered information is verified by the applicant, they must finally submit the application. **Step 3: Application Reference Number Generation** The portal generates an Application Reference Number (ARN). The applicant should save the ARN for all future correspondence and status tracking regarding their submitted application. > Post-Application Process **Step 1: Preliminary Verification by Film Facilitation Cell** The application is received online by the Film Facilitation Cell, where the submitted application details and supporting documents are examined for completeness and correctness. If any discrepancies are found, the application is returned to the applicant for necessary corrections. **Step 2: Committee Recommendation and Forwarding** Upon satisfactory verification, the Film Facilitation Cell uploads the Script Committee Letter and Finance Committee Letter and forwards the application online to the Deputy Director for further examination. **Step 3: Examination by Deputy Director** The Deputy Director reviews the application, committee recommendations, and all supporting documents to assess eligibility and compliance with the applicable guidelines. **Step 4: Decision by Deputy Director** Based on the examination, the Deputy Director may forward the application with recommendation to the Director for approval. If any required document is incomplete or deficient, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application is found ineligible, it is rejected with recorded remarks. **Step 5: Review by Director** The Director scrutinizes the application, recommendations, and supporting documents to ensure that all requirements have been fulfilled and that the case is suitable for approval. **Step 6: Final Decision by Director** The Director may approve the application and initiate digital sanction processing. If additional information or documents are required, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application does not meet the prescribed criteria, it is rejected with remarks. **Step 7: Generation of Digitally Signed Sanction Order** Upon approval, a Digitally Signed Sanction Order is generated through the system using the Director's Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). **Step 8: Issuance of Sanction Order** The approved Digitally Signed Sanction Order is issued and made available to the applicant through the system. **Step 9: Disbursement of Subsidy through DBT** After issuance of the Sanction Order, the approved subsidy amount is processed through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism and transferred to the beneficiary's registered bank account. **Step 10: Notification to Chairman** Notification to Chairman, Chhattisgarh Film Vikas Nigam Upon issuance of the Digitally Signed Sanction Order, the system notifies the Chairman, Chhattisgarh Film Vikas Nigam, regarding the approval and sanction of the application. **Step 11: Application Closure** After successful issuance of the Sanction Order and completion of all processing formalities, the application status is updated as Completed and the case is formally closed.

metadata.schemeName: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Science City
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to create an immersive, experiment-based learning attraction that builds scientific temper. Financial assistance for capital cost and corpus fund is provided to State/Union Territory Governments and their Societies.

page_content:
# Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Science City **Ministry:** Ministry Of Culture | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Capital Cost, Corpus Fund, Organising Exhibitions, Seminars, Science Camps | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The component "Science City" under the "Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science" by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to create a popular tourist attraction at the location that provides an experiment-based immersive learning ambience to inculcate a spirit of inquiry, foster creative talent and create scientific temper in the community as a whole. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and corpus fund is provided to State Governments, Union Territories, and the Societies/Authorities promoted by them. A Science City is characterised by its two-pronged channel of communication, namely exhibits and activities; while the exhibits, both indoor and outdoor, are mostly interactive, the demonstrations and training programmes are fully participatory and help children and adults alike to learn the basics of science through fun and enjoyment. It will be large in dimension with a focus on frontier areas of Science and Technology and edutainment, and shall be financially self-sustainable. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To portray the growth of science and technology and their application in industry and human welfare, with a view to developing a scientific attitude and temper. - To create awareness and enhance public understanding, appreciation and engagement of the public in the process of Science and Technology. - To popularise science and technology by organising exhibitions, seminars, popular lectures, science camps and various other programmes. - To supplement science education given in schools and colleges, and to organise out-of-school educational activities. - To design, develop and fabricate science museum exhibits, demonstration equipment and scientific teaching aids. - To organise training programmes for science teachers, students, young entrepreneurs, technicians, physically challenged persons, housewives and others.
## Benefits > **Project Cost:** **Location****Capital Cost****Corpus Fund****Total Project Cost**All locations other than North Eastern Region including Sikkim, Hilly Terrain and Island territories₹179.00 crore₹53.70 crore₹232.70 croreNorth Eastern Region including Sikkim₹214.80 crore₹64.50 crore₹279.30 croreHilly Terrain and Island Territories other than location in North Eastern Region including Sikkim₹214.80 crore₹64.50 crore₹279.30 crore> **Conditions Attached to the Benefit:** 1. A Science City is not to be set up under Type A funding, that is, full funding from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. 1. Under Type B funding, the capital cost is shared on a 60:40 basis between the Government of India and the State Government/Union Territory, except for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim, where it is shared on a 90:10 basis. 1. The corpus fund is shared 20:80 between the Government of India and the State Government/Union Territory; the Government of India share shall in no case exceed 20 per cent of the total Corpus Fund. 1. Under Type C funding, the State Government/Union Territory fully funds the project and sets it up with technical support from NCSM against payment of consultancy charges. 1. The corpus fund meets the operational deficit funding. The principal shall in no case be utilised for any activity. Not more than 85 per cent of the interest can be utilised to meet the operational deficit after inauguration, and a minimum of 15 per cent is to be added back to the corpus fund to compensate for inflation on a year to year basis. 1. The recurring expenditure is completely borne by the State/Union Territory Government, except where the Government of India decides to fully fund the project and manage it through NCSM. 1. Pile foundation, if required, will be considered after getting the Soil Test Report; the additional cost is entirely borne by the State Government. 1. Third-party quality assurance charges at 1 per cent of the estimated cost are entirely borne by the State Government. 1. Escalation of project cost is governed by the successive cost index over DPAR-2019 as published by the Central Public Works Department; the extra cost is borne by the State Government/local authority. > **Indicative Break-up of the Capital Cost:** 1. **Expenditure on Building construction works:** Grand Total ₹110.81 crore, which includes Science Centre building of 14,000 square metres minimum with indoor exhibition halls, internal electrification, external Light Emitting Diode lighting, water supply and sanitary installation, firefighting, car and bus parking, underground reservoir of 2,50,000 litres, lifts, escalators, air-conditioning, Diesel Generator set, Closed Circuit Television surveillance, chairs and carpet, contingency at 3 per cent as per Central Public Works Department norms, and architect fee.1. **Expenditure on Exhibits, Equipment and Stores:** Grand Total ₹68.00 crore, which includes large format film projection unit with laser projectors and accessories (₹25.00 crore), simulator and 3D film theatre (₹4.00 crore), thematic exhibits for Face to Face with Science and Technology (₹8.00 crore), interactive exhibits for experimentation and curriculum supplement (₹2.00 crore), projection equipment for auditorium (₹1.00 crore) and for digital panorama with laser projectors (₹22.00 crore), workshop tools and machineries (₹1.00 crore), development of Science park exhibits (₹1.50 crore), salary of project staff (₹2.50 crore), Travelling Allowance/Daily Allowance for project staff (₹0.40 crore), other administrative expenses (₹0.40 crore), and advertisement and publicity (₹0.20 crore).1. **Corpus Fund for Operational Deficit funding after inauguration:** at 30 per cent of the project cost.**Mode of Disbursement:** 1. The project shall normally be undertaken by NCSM on a turn-key basis. The funds are received by NCSM, both from the Central Government and the State Governments/Union Territories. NCSM sets up the Science City and hands it over to the State Government/Society for operation and management. 1. In case a State/Union Territory Government seeks financial support for a project to be implemented by themselves, a society should be formed by the respective State/Union Territory Government, and funds will be released by the Government of India to the society based on the recommendations of a Project Implementation Committee constituted by the Ministry of Culture with representatives of the Ministry of Culture, NCSM, experts in the field and the State Government. > **Frequency of Disbursement — Year-wise Utilization of Capital Expenditure:** 1. **For all locations other than North East including Sikkim/hilly terrain and island territories:** 15 per cent in the first year, 25 per cent in the second year, 25 per cent in the third year, 25 per cent in the fourth year, and 10 per cent in the fifth year. The Government of India releases ₹16.11 crore, ₹26.85 crore, ₹26.85 crore, ₹26.85 crore and ₹10.74 crore respectively, totalling ₹107.40 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹10.74 crore, making ₹118.14 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹114.56 crore upfront prior to starting of the project, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹42.96 crore.1. **For North Eastern Region including Sikkim:** The Government of India releases ₹29.00 crore, ₹48.33 crore, ₹48.33 crore, ₹48.33 crore and ₹19.33 crore, totalling ₹193.32 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹12.90 crore, making ₹206.22 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹73.08 crore upfront, including the minimum share of the corpus fund of ₹51.60 crore.1. **For hilly terrains and island territories other than the above:** The Government of India releases ₹19.33 crore, ₹32.22 crore, ₹32.22 crore, ₹32.22 crore and ₹12.89 crore, totalling ₹128.88 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹12.90 crore, making ₹141.78 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹137.52 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹51.60 crore. 1. The share of the corpus fund of the Government of India and the State Government/Union Territory is to be released upfront after approval of the project and prior to commencement of the works. > **Expected Time of Completion:** 1. Completion time from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work 60 months. 1. Project timeline from the date of placing of order for construction of building: Construction of building including space theatre, science exploration hall, panorama and so forth 48 months; Development of Entrance Plaza 12 months; Development of Science Park 36 months; Fabrication of exhibits 30 months; Installation of exhibits 12 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre 60 months approximately. **Validity/Post-Sanction Obligations:** 1. Over a period of 5 years from opening, the Science City should strive to generate at least 50 per cent of its operating cost, achieve an annual visitors footfall of around 10,00,000 (5,00,000 for the North East Region), and organize a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually, in-house and outreach, including activities on climate change, biodiversity, nature conservation, topical issues and skill development.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society/Authority promoted by the State/Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant should propose a location, preferably where no major Science Centre exists. 1. The applicant may alternatively propose upgradation of an existing science centre to a Science City in locations where footfall to the science centre is substantial. 1. The applicant may alternatively propose a separate Science City in a State capital or the largest city of the State, provided that the Science City is viable and financially self-sustainable. 1. The applicant should provide at least 25.0 acres of land; however, 30.0 acres would be preferable to do justice to exhibits and facilities, especially those requiring open spaces and future expansion. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is preferably centrally located, easily accessible, fully developed, without any low-lying area, of fairly regular shape, and secured with a boundary wall without any encumbrances. 1. The applicant State Government/Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for operation and management. 1. The applicant should obtain all other statutory clearances and approvals required by the local authorities of the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory Government or other bodies. 1. The applicant should choose the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, NCSM. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is free from all encumbrances and encroachment. 1. The applicant should ensure that electricity, water, sewerage connection and telecommunication facilities are available in the nearby vicinity. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land has good road connectivity for easy access and transport. 1. The applicant should not change the land once offered; if any such incident is noticed after release of grant, the released amount shall be recovered from the organisation with the applicable rate of interest. 1. The applicant should provide provisions for the solar rooftop in the Detailed Project Report, which is mandatory for the implementing agency. 1. The applicant should ensure that buildings are designed keeping in view applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with NCSM for implementation, if the project is undertaken and implemented by NCSM. 1. The applicant should form the Society before the start of execution of the project so that it is able to receive monetary grants from both Central and State/Union Territory Governments, private/corporate/industry sources, as well as raise loans from financial institutions.
## Exclusions 1. A Science City is not to be set up under Type A funding, that is, full funding from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. 1. The land requirement relaxation for scarce land in the heart of the city is available only for science centres and innovation hubs, and not for a Science City.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** Check basic criteria. Confirm the location criteria (preferably where no major Science Centre exists, or a State capital/largest city of the State, provided the Science City is viable and financially self-sustainable) and the land criteria of at least 25.0 acres, preferably 30.0 acres. **Step 2:** Decide the funding type. Only Type B (shared 60:40, or 90:10 for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim; corpus fund 20:80) or Type C (full State funding with technical support from the National Council of Science Museums against consultancy charges). A Science City is not to be set up under Type A. **Step 3:** Select the land with approval of the National Council of Science Museums. The land shall be chosen in consultation with, and with the approval of, the National Council of Science Museums, and cannot be changed later; otherwise the released amount shall be recovered with applicable interest. **Step 4:** Obtain the format. The Detailed Project Report format is enclosed with the guidelines at [Annexure E](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf), with [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) for the Physical Report on Site. **Step 5:** Prepare the Detailed Project Report. It should include the feasibility report, demand survey, commitment of land free of cost and recurring cost, projected footfall, and expected revenue generation. It will preferably be a hard-bound volume in A4 size in portrait alignment, with A3 drawings as foldouts. An incomplete Detailed Project Report will render the application liable for rejection. **Step 6:** Attach mandatory documents: Copy of Registration, Memorandum of Association or Trust Deed, Letter of Support from State Government, Letter of Recommendation from District Authority, Authorisation Certificate, Commitments for space and operation, and Audited Statement of Accounts for last three years, along with the filled [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) with Site Map, Google Map and Non-Encumbrance Certificate. **Step 7:** Submit the proposal to _Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture, Government of India, Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi-110001_ **Step 8:** Challenge method consideration. The proposal shall be considered on the basis of challenge method guidelines, as and when issued by the Government of India. **Step 9:** Appraisal by the Project Appraisal Committee, comprising the Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Director/Deputy Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Representative from the Integrated Finance Division, Ministry of Culture; Director General, National Council of Science Museums; and Director, National Council of Science Museums dealing with SPoCS. **Step 10:** Approval from the Government of India is required for setting up the Science City. Population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability may be relaxed in special cases. **Step 11:** Sign the Memorandum of Understanding between the National Council of Science Museums and the State/Union Territory Government, if implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. **Step 12:** Form the Society before the start of execution of the project, by the State/Union Territory Government in consultation with the National Council of Science Museums, so that it can receive grants and raise loans. **Step 13:** Release funds and begin construction. Funds are received by the National Council of Science Museums from both Central and State Governments, where it implements the project on a turn-key basis; where the State implements it, funds are released to the society on the recommendations of a Project Implementation Committee. The corpus fund share is released upfront after approval and prior to commencement of works. The State/Union Territory Government releases ₹114.56 crore, ₹73.08 crore or ₹137.52 crore upfront depending on location. **Step 14:** Recruit staff: 22 posts within 6 months of release of funds and 22 posts within two years, totalling 44 posts. **Step 15:** Execute as per the timeline 60 months from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work. **Step 16:** Monitoring by an Executive Council set up by the State/Union Territory Government with representation from the Ministry of Culture, the National Council of Science Museums, the State Government, private or corporate partners, and at least five eminent personalities. **Step 17:** Handover and outcome evaluation. The National Council of Science Museums hands over the Science City to the State Government/Society for operation and management. Over 5 years from opening, it should generate at least 50 per cent of operating cost, achieve an annual footfall of around 10,00,000 (5,00,000 for the North East Region), and organise a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually.

If the application does not meet the prescribed criteria, it is rejected with remarks. **Step 7:** **Generation of Digitally Signed Sanction Order** Upon approval, a Digitally Signed Sanction Order is generated through the system using the Director's Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). **Step 8:** **Issuance of Sanction Order** The approved Digitally Signed Sanction Order is issued and made available to the applicant through the system. Upon issuance of the Sanction Letter, the Chairman, Chhattisgarh Film Vikas Nigam, is also informed. **Step 9:** **Disbursement of Subsidy through DBT** After issuance of the Sanction Order, the approved subsidy amount is processed through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism and transferred to the beneficiary's registered bank account. **Step 10:** **Application Closure** After successful issuance of the Sanction Order and completion of all processing formalities, the application status is updated as Completed and the case is formally closed.

metadata.schemeName: Matsya Jeebi Credit Card (MJCC)
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to provide institutional short-term credit support to fish farmers and fisher folk for working capital requirements, reducing dependence on informal credit sources while promoting self-reliance, employment generation, income generation, and enhanced fish production.

page_content:
# Matsya Jeebi Credit Card (MJCC) **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** West Bengal | **Categories:** Banking,Financial Services and Insurance | **Tags:** Fish Farmer Credit, Fisheries Loan, Working Capital, Institutional Credit, Inland Fisheries, Aquaculture | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The "Matsya Jeebi Credit Card (MJCC)" is implemented by the Department Of Fisheries, Government of West Bengal. The scheme aims to provide institutional short-term credit support for the working capital requirements of fish farmers and fisher folk. It reduces dependence on the informal banking sector for credit while promoting self-reliance, employment generation, income generation, and increased fish production. The scheme offers cash credit at a subsidised rate of interest with flexible repayment facilities and other credit-related benefits.
## Benefits - **Cash Credit Facility:** Cash credit is provided to farmers at a subsidised rate of interest. - **Credit Limit:** Credit limit is available as per the applicable scheme, generally up to ₹3,00,000/-. - **Flexible Repayment:** Repayment is allowed after harvest and marketing, with rescheduling available in case of a bad crop season. - **Multiple Withdrawals:** Any number of withdrawals can be made within the sanctioned credit limit. - **Collateral-Free Loan:** No collateral is required for loans up to ₹1,60,000/-. - **Interest Subvention:** Interest subsidy is available for timely repayment of the loan.
## Eligibility Criteria > **Inland Fisheries & Aquaculture:** - Fishers, Fish farmers (individual & groups/partners/share croppers/lease holder farmers), Self Help Group, Joint Liability Groups & Women Groups, are eligible. > **Marine Fisheries:** - Owner of registered fishing vessels / boats. - Possess necessary license / permission from competent authority for fishing in estuary and in sea, fish farming / pisciculture activities in estuaries and in open seas.

## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline > **Login:** **Step 1:** Visit the official website of [WBMJCC](https://mjcc-fisheries.wb.gov.in/). Click on "Login"> “Fisherman Login” button. **Step 2:** Click on “Apply for MJCC” button or you can also click on “Application Form”. **Step 3:** Fill the details of your MJCC project and your bank related information. **Step 4:** Then upload all the relevant documents. Now click on "Save" and then click on the ‘SUBMIT’ button to complete the application process. > **Status Check:** **Step 1:** You can see your MJCC Loan status by clicking on ‘Status Timeline’. **Step 3:** If your application returns by FEO then you can check the reasons by simply clicking on the ‘VIEW REASONS’. **Step 4:** You can see your rejection reasons by clicking on ‘VIEW REASONS’ button or you can resubmit your application by clicking on ‘RESUBMIT APPLICATION’ button.

metadata.schemeName: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The "NHDP: Research & Development Scheme" is introduced to generate feedback on economic, social, aesthetic, and promotional aspects of various crafts and artisans in the handicraft sector. The surveys and studies are sponsored/conducted to generate suitable inputs for planning purposes.

page_content:
# National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme **Ministry:** Ministry Of Textiles | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Sports & Culture, Skills & Employment | **Tags:** Handicraft, Textile, Research, Grant-in-Aid | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The "Research & Development Scheme" is a component of the Umbrella Scheme "National Handicrafts Development Programme (NHDP)" by the Ministry of Textiles, Govt. of India. The scheme is introduced to generate feedback on the economic, social, aesthetic, and promotional aspects of various crafts and artisans in the handicraft sector. Under this scheme, the surveys and studies are sponsored/conducted to generate suitable inputs for planning purposes. Also, workshops, seminars, conferences, radio programs, etc. are organized in online as well as offline mode to sensitize the artisans on the latest development in the Handicrafts sector.
> **Key Highlights:** 1. Surveys & Studies a) Surveys/ Studies of specific crafts and mapping and documentation of a database on craft clusters and specific craft pockets, present market trend and status, existing export and future export openings, etc. b) Problem relating to the availability of raw materials, technology, design, common facilities, etc. c) Socioeconomic condition of the artisan. d) Market evaluation studies of specific crafts for either domestic or overseas markets. e) Techno-economic feasibility studies and post-evaluation of the various promotional projects programs undertaken in the handicrafts sector. 2. Financial Assistance for registration of GI crafts (including registration of authorized users), preparation of legal para, standards, audits, and other documentation leading to labeling/certification. 3. Financial Assistance to organizations for evolving, and developing a mechanism for protecting crafts including Endangered crafts, design, heritage, and traditional knowledge. 4. Conducting a Census of Handicraft artisans of the country and publishing the same in handbook/e-book format for future reference. 5. Assisting handicrafts exporters in the adoption of global standards, including handicrafts marks, branding, bar coding, and other similar standards 6. Conducting workshops/seminars on issues of specific issues relating to the handicrafts sector. 7. Evaluation / Impact Assessment Studies of Handicrafts Schemes. 8. Need-based financial assistance to Government departments/ministries, institutes of national importance and export promotional councils, etc. ## Eligibility Criteria **Grants-in-aid can be given to a public body or an institution having a distinct legal entity viz.** 1. Institutions or Organizations setup as Autonomous Organisations, under a specific statute or as a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, or Indian Trusts Act, 1882. 1. Producer Companies and Section-8 Companies (Company Act, 2013). 1. Non-Government Organizations. 1. Educational and Other Institutions. 1. Urban and Rural Local Self-government Institutions. 1. Export Promotion Councils. 1. Central Cottage Industries Emporium (CCIC). 1. National Crafts Museum & Hastkala Academy, New Delhi. 1. State/Central [Govt. Agencies](http://www.handicrafts.nic.in/EmpanelledGovtList.aspx?MID=Zdw7bw+50oGAn2GA6qArNg==) etc.
**The applicant should certify the following in the application form:** 1. No financial assistance has been received from any other source for the same purpose. 1. The provision of the scheme has been fully understood and we take responsibility for the successful completion of the project within the sanctioned project duration. 1. All infrastructure is available with the organization to conduct the programs as per the scheme. 1. There is no duplication of efforts taking Place with existing schemes of the Ministries. 1. No UC is pending in any scheme of the O/o DC (Handicrafts). 1. The organization is registered with Public Finance Management System and will adhere to the Provisions/guidelines of the Department of Expenditure from time to time, in this regard. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Official Portal/Link:** http://www.handicrafts.nic.in/ApplyOnline/Login.aspx
