The corpus fund is shared 20:80. - The Digital Planetarium could be operated and managed under Type A, Type B and Type C, as detailed for science centres. - Under Type C, the State Governments and Union Territories shall fully fund the project and set it up with technical support from the National Council of Science Museums against payment of consultancy charges. - The corpus fund shared by the Government of India shall in no case exceed 20 per cent of the total Corpus Fund; the principal shall in no case be utilized for any activity; not more than 85 per cent of the interest can be utilised to meet the operational deficit after inauguration, and a minimum of 15 per cent is to be added back to compensate the inflation on a year to year basis. - The share of corpus fund of the Government of India and the State Government or Union Territory is to be released upfront after approval of the project and prior to commencement of the works. - The recurring expenditure will be completely borne by the State Government. Every year, provision for the annual recurring expenditure for maintenance of the equipment and organizing new planetarium shows shall be made by the State Government. - For Hilly Region, Island Territory and North Eastern Region, 20 per cent extra on the entire Capital Cost has been considered. - The building construction cost is considered based on normal foundation. If any special foundation is required to be done based on the Soil Test Report, the additional cost will have to be borne by the State Government. - Escalation of project cost shall be governed by successive cost index over DPAR-2019 as published by the Central Public Works Department at the time of the project work; the extra project cost on this account is to be borne by the State Government or Local Authority. > **Content and Facilities Provided:** - **Category 1:** Main Opto-mechanical Star field Projector capable of projecting 8,500 stars down to 6.5 magnitude on a tilted or horizontal Projection Dome; the Projector will have Space or Earth mode system, or a Full dome digital planetarium projector system, or both, depending upon available fund. Dome Size 12 metre diameter; Seating Capacity 120 to 125 unidirectional. The capital cost includes Civil and allied works ₹4.02 crore; Chairs ₹0.15 crore; Air Conditioning of Planetarium theatre and exhibition areas only ₹0.50 crore; Carpet in planetarium theatre ₹0.06 crore; Firefighting System ₹0.25 crore; Pure Digital Full-dome solution with High Contrast Light Emitting Diode or Solid State light source projection system with effective resolution of 4.5K after blending, including cost of 12.0 Metre Diameter inner Aluminium Dome ₹10.00 crore; Uninterruptible Power Supply ₹0.15 crore; Telescope and accessories for sky observations ₹1.00 crore; Office furniture, furnishing and tools ₹0.25 crore; Exhibits on Astronomy within the circular passage around the planetarium theatre with exhibition space of 350 Square Metres approximately ₹1.00 crore; Transportation, Installation and Commissioning of Exhibits at site ₹0.20 crore; Travelling Allowance or Daily Allowance, Training and Miscellaneous Expenditure ₹0.20 crore; and Architects Fee ₹0.22 crore.- **Category 2**: Main Opto-mechanical Star field Projector capable of projecting 8,500 stars down to 6.5 magnitude. Dome Size 10 metre diameter; Seating Capacity 80 to 85 unidirectional. The capital cost includes Civil and allied works ₹3.00 crore; Chairs ₹0.01 crore; Air Conditioning ₹0.35 crore; Carpet ₹0.04 crore; Firefighting System ₹0.20 crore; High Contrast Light Emitting Diode or Solid State light source projection system with effective resolution of 3K after blending ₹3.00 crore; 10 Metre Diameter Inner Aluminium Dome ₹1.25 crore; Uninterruptible Power Supply ₹0.05 crore; Telescope and accessories ₹0.10 crore; Office furniture ₹0.15 crore; Exhibits on Astronomy with exhibition space of 275 Square Metres approximately ₹1.25 crore; Transportation, Installation and Commissioning ₹0.15 crore; Travelling Allowance or Daily Allowance, Training and Miscellaneous Expenditure ₹0.20 crore; and Architects Fee ₹0.16 crore.- **Category 3:** Mini Digital Projection System. Dome Size 8 metre diameter; Seating Capacity 50 unidirectional. The capital cost includes Civil and allied works ₹2.22 crore; Chairs ₹0.06 crore; Air Conditioning ₹0.30 crore; Carpet ₹0.02 crore; Firefighting equipment, standalone using portable fire extinguisher ₹0.20 crore; Single projector fish eye lens equipment with effective resolution 2K ₹1.00 crore; 8 Metre Diameter Inner Aluminium Dome ₹1.00 crore; Uninterruptible Power Supply ₹0.05 crore; Telescope and accessories ₹0.06 crore; Office furniture ₹0.10 crore; Exhibits on Astronomy with exhibition space of 200 Square Metres approximately ₹0.75 crore; Transportation, installation and commissioning ₹0.10 crore; Travelling Allowance or Daily Allowance, Training and Miscellaneous expenditure ₹0.12 crore; and Architects Fee ₹0.12 crore. - **Additional Items for Category 1 and Category 2:** Special Effect Projectors and Attachments; Complete sound system for the Planetarium Theatre; Projection dome; and Cove lights. - **Additional Facilities for Category 1 and Category 2:** Interactive exhibition on astronomy and space science; Activity area for students on astronomy; Sky observation through a Global Positioning System-enabled telescope; Lecture hall for astronomy lectures by specialists; and Office, maintenance workshop, and show development room. - **Additional Facilities for Category 3:** Activity area for students on astronomy; Sky observation through a Global Positioning System-enabled telescope; Lecture hall for astronomy lectures by specialists; and Office, maintenance workshop and show development room. > **Mode of Disbursement:** Normally, the digital planetarium will be set up by the National Council of Science Museums on a turn-key basis, including construction and commissioning of the equipment, and handed over after completion to the State Government or Union Territory. The construction work shall start only after the share or funding is received from the State or Union Territory Government. Preferably, the construction of the building shall be undertaken by the State Government, Union Territory or agency within the allocated budget as per inputs and supervision by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Frequency of Disbursement — Year-wise Utilization of Capital Expenditure:** For all three categories, the capital expenditure is released at 60 per cent in the first year and 40 per cent in the second year.

The project can be completed within 24 months time from the date of commencement of construction for Category 1, Category 2 and Category 3. > **Recurring Expenditure and Projected Revenue:** - Category 1: Recurring expenditure of ₹50,00,000 per annum, comprising ₹30,00,000 salary, ₹15,00,000 maintenance and ₹5,00,000 activities and spares approximately, for operating the planetarium, shall be borne by the agency or society running the Planetarium or by the State Government. Considering 60 per cent occupancy, that is 60 per cent public and 40 per cent students, and 5 shows a day, revenue from tickets would be ₹19.44 lakh per year from the public (60 per cent of 360 persons a day at ₹30 per person for 300 days in a year) and ₹8.64 lakh per year from students (40 per cent of 360 students a day at ₹20 per student for 300 days in a year), totalling ₹28.08 lakh per year. - Category 2: Recurring expenditure of ₹40,00,000 per annum, comprising ₹25,00,000 salary, ₹10,00,000 maintenance and ₹5,00,000 activities and spares approximately. Revenue from tickets would be ₹13.00 lakh from the public (60 per cent of 240 persons a day at ₹30 per person for 300 days) and ₹5.76 lakh from students (40 per cent of 240 students a day at ₹20 per student for 300 days), totalling ₹18.76 lakh per year. - Category 3: Recurring expenditure of ₹40,00,000 per annum, comprising ₹25,00,000 salary, ₹10,00,000 maintenance and ₹5,00,000 activities and spares approximately. Revenue from tickets would be ₹8.1 lakh from the public (60 per cent of 150 persons a day at ₹30 per person for 300 days) and ₹3.6 lakh from students (40 per cent of 150 students a day at ₹20 per student for 300 days), totalling ₹11.7 lakh per year. > **Validity and Post-Sanction Obligations:****** The Digital Planetariums and Astronomy Education Centres should strive to achieve the following over a period of 5 years from opening: - Generate at least 50 per cent of their operating cost. - Achieve an annual visitors footfall of around 1,00,000 for Category 1 (75,000 for the North East Region), around 75,000 for Category 2 (50,000 for the North East Region), and around 25,000 for Category 3. - Organize a minimum of 5 to 10 astronomy education programmes in a year.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society or Authority promoted by the State or Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 1, that is, a city or town with a population of 15,00,000 or more, and the planetarium shall have a 12 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 2, that is, a city or town with a population between 5,00,000 and 15,00,000, and the planetarium shall have a 10 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 3, that is, a city, town or location with a population of less than 5,00,000, and the planetarium shall have an 8 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 2.0 acres of land, or 1.0 acre if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 2.0 acres of land, or 1.0 acre if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 1.0 acre of land. 1. The applicant may either collocate the Centre with an existing Science Centre, or attach it to one, or set it up independently in another non-formal educational institution which is engaged in science popularization activities. 1. The applicant State Government or Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for the operation and management of the Digital Planetarium. 1. The applicant should obtain all other statutory clearances and approvals required by the local authorities of the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory Government or other bodies. 1. The applicant should choose the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, the National Council of Science Museums. 1. The applicant should not change the land once offered; if any such incident is noticed after release of grant by the Ministry, the released amount shall be recovered from the organisation with the applicable rate of interest. 1. The applicant should provide provisions for the solar rooftop in the Detailed Project Report, which is mandatory for the implementing agency. 1. The applicant should ensure that all buildings constructed under the scheme are designed keeping applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should form a Registered Society immediately after the release of the fund by the State Governments or Union Territories towards their share of the capital cost of the project. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Council of Science Museums for implementation of the project, if undertaken and implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Preference, Priority and Relaxation:** - The land requirement is relaxed to 1.0 acre for Category 1 and Category 2 if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. - The Digital Planetarium is to be preferably co-located in the existing Science Centres, science museums or non-formal education institutions that promote science communication, especially astronomy education. - Preferably, the State Government, Union Territory, or agency shall undertake the construction of the building within the allocated budget, with inputs and supervision from the National Council of Science Museums. - The eligibility criteria of population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability of the project considering the intangible outcome of the facility in terms of knowledge gain may be relaxed and/or modified in special cases or circumstances by the Honourable Chief Minister, Government of India, as stated in the document. - In the construction of the building, priority or preference may be given to local material, labour and expertise; wherever possible, community participation may be encouraged; use of renewable energy and energy-saving devices may be given top preference.
## Exclusions - The principal of the corpus fund shall in no case be utilized for any activity.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** Determine the Category 1 with a 12 metre dome at a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre Category 1, Category 2 with a 10 metre dome at a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre Category 2, and Category 3 with an 8 metre dome at a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre Category 3, and confirm the land availability of 2.0 acres, 2.0 acres and 1.0 acre respectively, or 1.0 acre for Category 1 and Category 2 if inside the Science Centre Campus. **Step 2:** Decide the funding Type A, Type B (shared 50:50, or 90:10 for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim, with corpus fund 20:80) or Type C (full State funding with technical support against consultancy charges). **Step 3:** Select the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, the National Council of Science Museums; the land cannot be changed later, otherwise the released amount shall be recovered with applicable interest. **Step 4:** Obtain the Detailed Project Report format at [Annexure E](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf), with [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) for the Physical Report on Site. **Step 5:** Prepare the Detailed Project Report, including the feasibility report, demand survey for the need of the facility at the location, commitment of land free of cost and the recurring cost, projected footfall and expected revenue generation, to determine whether the proposed Digital Planetarium is viable and financially self-sustainable. It will preferably be a hardbound volume in A4 size in portrait alignment; an incomplete Detailed Project Report will render the application liable for rejection. **Step 6:** Attach the mandatory documents, along with the filled [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) with Site Map, Google Map and Non-Encumbrance Certificate. **Step 7:** Submit the proposal with the Detailed Project Report to: > _Joint Secretary (Museums)_ > _Ministry of Culture, Government of India,_ > _Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi-110001_ **Step 8:** The proposal shall be considered on the basis of challenge method guidelines, as and when issued by the Government of India, and per the criteria and parameters prescribed for the purpose in the scheme. **Step 9:** The Detailed Project Report will be appraised by the Project Appraisal Committee, comprising the Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Director or Deputy Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Representative from the Integrated Finance Division, Ministry of Culture; Director General, National Council of Science Museums; and Director, National Council of Science Museums dealing with the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science, for further recommendation to obtain approval of the competent authority. **Step 10:** Obtain approval from the Government of India for setting up the Digital Planetarium under the scheme. **Step 11:** Sign the Memorandum of Understanding between the National Council of Science Museums and the State or Union Territory Government for implementation of the project, if undertaken and implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. **Step 12:** Form the Registered Society immediately after the release of the fund by the State Governments or Union Territories towards their share of the capital cost of the project. A representative of the National Council of Science Museums shall be an ex-officio member of this Society or its Governing Council. The Society shall ensure that the Planetarium functions as per the requirements of its objectives without any deviations. The corpus fund share is released upfront after approval of the project and prior to commencement of the works. **Step 13:** Normally, the digital planetarium will be set up by the National Council of Science Museums on a turnkey basis, and construction shall start only after the share or funding is received from the State or Union Territory Government. Preferably, the construction of the building shall be undertaken by the State Government, Union Territory or agency within the allocated budget as per inputs and supervision by the National Council of Science Museums. **Step 14:** The Registered Society shall complete the recruitment of the required core staff members within 6 months of the release of funds, with the National Council of Science Museums providing professional support to the Executive Council for recruitment and training of staff, the cost of training being borne by the Society. The required staff strength is as follows: - **Category 1 and Category 2, total 6 posts:** To be recruited and posted within 3 months after the commencement of the project — Curator or Education Officer, Master of Science (1); Education assistant, Bachelor of Science (1); Lower Division Clerk (1). To be recruited and posted during the installation of the equipment in the planetarium — Technical Assistant, Diploma (1); Technicians, Electronics 1 and Electrical 1 (2).- **Category 3, total 4 posts:** To be recruited and posted within 3 months after the commencement of the project — Education Officer, Master of Science, or Education Assistant, Bachelor of Science (1); Lower Division Clerk (1). To be recruited and posted during the installation of the equipment in the planetarium — Technicians, Electronics 1 and Electrical 1 (2).- Security and Conservancy shall be run on contract. The National Council of Science Museums shall provide an organic link for the activities and upgradation, and will train the staff members recruited by the Society for the Centre. **Step 15:** Complete the project within 24 months from the date of issue of the Letter of Intent for the construction work, that is, 24 months from the date of commencement of construction. **Step 16:** Monitoring of Digital Planetariums set up as individual Autonomous Societies under Type B and Type C shall be done by an Executive Council set up by the respective State or Union Territory Government, with due representation from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, the National Council of Science Museums, the concerned State Government, their private or corporate partners if any, and at least five eminent personalities in the fields of education, Astrophysics, Science and Technology, industry and Science Communication, for recruitment of staff, budgeting, planning and execution of the Annual Plan of activities of the digital planetarium. In case the planetarium is set up in the existing science centres, the existing Executive Council shall monitor the working of the digital planetarium. **Step 17: T**he Digital Planetarium or Space and Astronomy Education Centres will be operated and maintained by a Registered Society formed by the State Government for this purpose. The Planetarium shall be run by an agency or society formed for this purpose or by a suitable Society. Over 5 years from opening, it should generate at least 50 per cent of its operating cost, achieve an annual footfall of around 1,00,000 for Category 1 (75,000 for the North East Region), around 75,000 for Category 2 (50,000 for the North East Region) and around 25,000 for Category 3, and organise a minimum of 5 to 10 astronomy education programmes in a year. > **Jurisdiction:** All disputes arising out of the scheme shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Courts of Delhi and New Delhi only.

metadata.schemeName: Application for Subsidy on Other Regional Film
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote the production of regional language films and encourage filmmakers to create quality cinematic content by providing financial assistance to eligible film producers in accordance with prescribed eligibility criteria and policy guidelines.

page_content:
# Application for Subsidy on Other Regional Film **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Sports & Culture, Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Subsidy, Regional Film, Producer, Filmmaker | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme “Application for Subsidy on Other Regional Film” has been introduced by the Culture and Archaeology Department, Government of Chhattisgarh under the Chhattisgarh Film Policy, 2021 to promote the production of regional language films and encourage filmmakers to create quality cinematic content. The scheme provides financial assistance to eligible film producers for the production of regional films in accordance with the prescribed eligibility criteria and policy guidelines.
## Benefits - Subsidy amount: Up to ₹50 lakh or 25% of the total Cost of Production (COP) of the film, whichever is lower. - Attractive discounts shall be provided on room reservations in the accommodation units operated by the Chhattisgarh Tourism Board. - Upon issuance of the CBFC (Censor Board) Certification, 30% of the approved assistance may be released. The remaining 70% may be released after the film is exhibited (released) in at least 15 theatres/centres. - A maximum of 10 films per calendar year shall be eligible to receive benefits under the subsidy/grant scheme.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. At least 50% of the total shooting days of the film must be conducted within the State of Chhattisgarh. 1. A minimum of 20% of the supporting artists, technical crew, assistant artists, and ground staff engaged in the film production must be permanent residents of Chhattisgarh.
## Exclusions

If additional information or documents are required, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application does not meet the prescribed criteria, it is rejected with remarks. **Step 7: Generation of Digitally Signed Sanction Order** Upon approval, a Digitally Signed Sanction Order is generated through the system using the Director's Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). **Step 8: Issuance of Sanction Order** The approved Digitally Signed Sanction Order is issued and made available to the applicant through the system. **Step 9: Disbursement of Subsidy through DBT** After issuance of the Sanction Order, the approved subsidy amount is processed through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism and transferred to the beneficiary's registered bank account. **Step 10: Notification to Chairman** Notification to Chairman, Chhattisgarh Film Vikas Nigam Upon issuance of the Digitally Signed Sanction Order, the system notifies the Chairman, Chhattisgarh Film Vikas Nigam, regarding the approval and sanction of the application. **Step 11: Application Closure** After successful issuance of the Sanction Order and completion of all processing formalities, the application status is updated as Completed and the case is formally closed.

# Application for Subsidy on Special Branding of Chhattisgarh **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Film Makers, Handicrafts, Heritage | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme “Application for Subsidy on Special Branding of Chhattisgarh” has been introduced by the Culture and Archaeology Department, Government of Chhattisgarh under the Chhattisgarh Film Policy, 2021 to promote films that highlight the unique identity and distinct features of the state. The scheme provides financial assistance to eligible filmmakers for producing films centered on Chhattisgarh's culture, cuisine, handicrafts, local festivals, distinguished personalities, heritage, history, and stories. By encouraging cinematic storytelling focused on the state, the initiative aims to promote and enhance the branding of Chhattisgarh and showcase its rich cultural and historical identity through films.
## Benefits - Financial assistance is provided for eligible films as follows: - Financial assistance of 75% of the project cost of the film or ₹1 crore, whichever is lower. - The benefit is available for up to 3 released films per year, as per the prescribed rules and conditions.

## Eligibility Criteria 1. The film should be centred on Chhattisgarh and showcase significant aspects of the State. 1. The film should be based on themes such as Chhattisgarh's culture, food, handicrafts, local festivals, distinguished personalities, heritage, history, and stories . 1. The film should be produced/filmed in accordance with the conditions and guidelines prescribed under the scheme. 1. Financial assistance is subject to approval by the competent authority and availability of the prescribed annual limit of 3 released films.

## Exclusions

If any required document is incomplete, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application is found ineligible, it is rejected with remarks. **Step 5: Review by Director** The Director scrutinizes the application, recommendations, and supporting documents to ensure that all requirements have been fulfilled and that the case is suitable for approval. **Step 6: Final Decision by Director** The Director may approve the application and initiate digital sanction processing. If additional information or documents are required, the application is returned to the applicant for correction. If the application does not meet the prescribed criteria, it is rejected with remarks. **Step 7: Generation of Digitally Signed Sanction Order** Upon approval, a Digitally Signed Sanction Order is generated through the system using the Director's Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). **Step 8: Disbursement of Financial Assistance** After issuance of the Digitally Signed Sanction Order, the approved financial assistance is processed through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system and transferred to the beneficiary's registered bank account. **Step 9: Notification to Stakeholders** The system notifies the applicant regarding the issuance of the Sanction Order. Simultaneously, the Chairman, Chhattisgarh Film Vikas Nigam, is also informed of the approval and sanction. **Step 10: Application Closure** After successful issuance of the Sanction Order and completion of all processing formalities, the application status is updated as Completed and the case is formally closed.

metadata.schemeName: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Science Centre (Category-I, Category-II, Category-III)
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme component aims to promote hands-on "doing science" through experimental, self-discovery exhibits. Financial assistance for capital costs and corpus fund under three categories is provided to State/Union Territory Governments and their Societies.

page_content:
# Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Science Centre (Category-I, Category-II, Category-III) **Ministry:** Ministry Of Culture | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Capital Cost, Corpus Fund, Museums, Science Category | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The component "Science Centres - Category-I, Category-II, Category-III" under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to provide the scope of "doing science" by adopting a hands-on approach, offering the visitor a number of experimental options through which they can discover scientific concepts themselves. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and corpus fund is provided to State Governments, Union Territories, and the Societies/Authorities promoted by them, under three categories based on the population of the city or town. This mode of education has so far proved to be very effective in supplementing formal science education in the country. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To portray the growth of science and technology and their application in industry and human welfare, with a view to developing a scientific attitude and temper. - To create awareness and enhance public understanding, appreciation and engagement of the public in the process of Science and Technology. - To popularise science and technology by organising exhibitions, seminars, popular lectures, science camps and various other programmes. - To supplement science education given in schools and colleges, and to organise out-of-school educational activities. - To design, develop and fabricate science museum exhibits, demonstration equipment and scientific teaching aids. - To organise training programmes for science teachers, students, young entrepreneurs, technicians, physically challenged persons, housewives and others.
## Benefits > **Science Centre – Category I:** **Location****Capital Cost****Corpus Fund****Total Project Cost**All locations other than the North Eastern Region, including Sikkim, Hilly Terrain and Island territories₹31.50 crore₹9.50 crore₹41.00 croreNorth Eastern Region including Sikkim₹37.80 crore₹11.30 crore₹49.10 croreHilly Terrain and Island Territories other than location in North Eastern Region including Sikkim₹37.80 crore₹11.30 crore₹49.10 crore
> **Science Centre – Category II:** **Location****Capital Cost****Corpus Fund****Total Project Cost**All locations other than the North Eastern Region, including Sikkim, Hilly Terrain and Island territories₹17.10 crore₹5.15 crore₹22.25 croreNorth Eastern Region including Sikkim₹20.50 crore₹6.20 crore₹26.70 croreHilly Terrain and Island Territories other than locations in North Eastern Region including Sikkim₹20.50 crore₹6.20 crore₹26.70 crore
> **Science Centre – Category III:** **Location****Capital Cost****Corpus Fund****Total Project Cost**All locations other than the North Eastern Region, including Sikkim, Hilly Terrain and Island territories₹5.10 crore₹1.55 crore₹6.65 croreNorth Eastern Region including Sikkim₹6.10 crore₹1.85 crore₹7.95 croreHilly Terrain and Island Territories other than locations in North Eastern Region including Sikkim₹6.10 crore₹1.85 crore₹7.95 crore
> **Conditions Attached to the Benefit:** - Under Type A funding, for Science Centres to be set up in locations/regions where Science Centre activities have not yet started, or in priority areas, the Ministry of Culture may consider providing full funding for such Centres through NCSM. In no case will more than one Science Centre be set up in any State/Union Territory in future under the scheme. In States/Union Territories where NCSM centres already exist, such provision shall not be applicable. - Under Type B funding, the capital cost for a Science Centre (Category 1, 2 and 3) is shared on a 50:50 basis, except for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim, where it is shared on a 90:10 basis. The corpus fund is shared 20:80. - Under Type C funding, the State Government/Union Territory fully funds the project and sets it up with technical support from NCSM against payment of consultancy charges. - The corpus fund meets the operational deficit funding. The principal shall in no case be utilised for any activity. Not more than 85 per cent of the interest can be utilised to meet the operational deficit after inauguration, and a minimum of 15 per cent is to be added back to the corpus fund. - Pile foundation, if required, will be considered after getting the Soil Test Report; the additional cost is entirely borne by the State Government. - Third-party quality assurance charges at 1 per cent of the estimated cost are entirely borne by the State Government. - Escalation of project cost is governed by the successive cost index over DPAR-2019 as published by the Central Public Works Department. - The Mobile Science Exhibition bus facility will be added to the Science Centre only on allotment of a separate budget by the State Government/Union Territory. > **Indicative Break-up of the Capital Cost:** - **Category I:** Expenditure on Building construction works – Grand Total ₹23.07 crore, for a Science Centre of 4,000 square metres minimum. Expenditure on Exhibits, Equipment and Stores – Grand Total ₹8.43 crore, which includes three thematic galleries of approximately 600 square metres with 50 exhibits each (₹3.75 crore), Science Park of approximately 4 acres with pathway and 50 required exhibits (₹1.00 crore), inflatable dome planetarium system called Taramandal (₹0.10 crore), fully functional exhibit development laboratory (₹0.25 crore), other facilities like Computer training area, Library, Conference Room, Stores and Office (₹0.80 crore), training of required staff members and other miscellaneous expenses (₹0.15 crore), 3D theatre facility with equipment and furniture (₹1.00 crore), miscellaneous building or auditorium furnishing, signage and murals (₹0.25 crore), and salary and Travelling Allowance/Daily Allowance of project staff (₹1.130 crore). Corpus Fund at 30 per cent of the project cost.- **Category 2:** Expenditure on Building construction works – Grand Total ₹12.60 crore, for a Science Centre of 2,000 square metres minimum. Expenditure on Exhibits, Equipment and Stores – Grand Total ₹4.50 crore, which includes two thematic galleries of approximately 250 square metres with 25 exhibits (₹2.00 crore), Science Park of approximately 3 acres with pathway and required exhibits (₹0.80 crore), inflatable dome planetarium system (₹0.10 crore), fully functional exhibit development laboratory (₹0.20 crore), other facilities like Computer training area, Library, Conference Room, Stores and Office (₹0.40 crore), and salary and Travelling Allowance/Daily Allowance of project staff (₹1.00 crore). Corpus Fund at 30 per cent of the project cost.- **Category 3:** Expenditure on Building construction works – Grand Total ₹3.55 crore, for a Science Centre of 500 square metres minimum. Expenditure on Exhibits, Equipment and Stores – Grand Total ₹1.55 crore, which includes one Fun Science Gallery of approximately 100 square metres with 20 exhibits (₹0.50 crore), setting up of Temporary Exhibition cum Multipurpose hall of approximately 100 square metres (₹0.40 crore), Innovation and Activity Centre (₹0.50 crore), and salary and Travelling Allowance/Daily Allowance of project staff (₹0.15 crore). Corpus Fund at 30 per cent of the project cost. > **Mode of Disbursement:** - For a Science Centre set up under **Type A** and **Type B**, NCSM will complete the Science Centre on a turn-key basis, including construction and commissioning, and hand over the project after completion to the State Government/Union Territory. NCSM shall start the construction work only after the share of funding is received from the State/Union Territory Government.- For a Science Centre set up under **Type C**, the State Government/Union Territory shall do the construction of the building as per inputs from NCSM and develop the Science Park as per the advice of NCSM. NCSM shall provide technical and professional support at cost and consultancy charges to the State/Union Territory Government for the project. > **Frequency of Disbursement — Year-wise Utilization of Capital Expenditure:** > **Category 1: 40 per cent in the first year, 40 per cent in the second year and 20 per cent in the third year:** - All locations other than North East including Sikkim/hilly terrain and island territories: Government of India releases ₹6.30 crore, ₹6.30 crore and ₹3.15 crore, totalling ₹15.75 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹1.90 crore, making ₹17.65 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹23.35 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹7.60 crore. - North East region including Sikkim: Government of India releases ₹13.61 crore, ₹13.61 crore and ₹6.80 crore, totalling ₹34.02 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹2.26 crore, making ₹36.28 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹12.82 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹9.04 crore. - Hilly terrains and island territories other than the above: Government of India releases ₹7.56 crore, ₹7.56 crore and ₹3.78 crore, totalling ₹18.90 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹2.26 crore, making ₹21.16 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹27.94 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹9.04 crore. > **Category 2:** **40 per cent in the first year, 40 per cent in the second year and 20 per cent in the third year:** - All locations other than North East, including Sikkim: Government of India releases ₹3.42 crore, ₹3.42 crore and ₹1.71 crore, totalling ₹8.55 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹1.03 crore, making ₹9.58 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹12.67 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹4.12 crore. - North East regions including Sikkim: Government of India releases ₹7.38 crore, ₹7.38 crore and ₹3.69 crore, totalling ₹18.45 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹1.24 crore, making ₹19.69 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹7.01 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹4.96 crore. - Hilly terrains and island territories other than the above: Government of India releases ₹4.10 crore, ₹4.10 crore and ₹2.05 crore, totalling ₹10.25 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹1.24 crore, making ₹11.49 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹15.21 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹4.96 crore. > **Category 3:** **60 per cent in the first year and 40 per cent in the second year:** - All locations other than North East, including Sikkim: Government of India releases ₹1.53 crore and ₹1.02 crore, totalling ₹2.55 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹0.31 crore, making ₹2.86 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹3.79 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹1.24 crore. - North East regions including Sikkim: Government of India releases ₹3.30 crore and ₹2.19 crore, totalling ₹5.49 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹0.37 crore, making ₹5.86 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹2.09 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹1.48 crore. - Hilly terrains and island territories other than the above: Government of India releases ₹1.83 crore and ₹1.22 crore, totalling ₹3.05 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹0.37 crore, making ₹3.42 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹4.53 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹1.48 crore. > **Expected Time of Completion:** - Completion time from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work: Category 1 – 42 months; Category 2 – 36 months; Category 3 – 30 months. - Project timeline from the date of placing of order for construction of building: - Category 1: Construction of Building – 27 months; Development of Science Park – 12 months; Fabrication of exhibits – 30 months; Installation of exhibits – 9 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre – 42 months approximately. - Category 2: Construction of Building – 21 months; Development of Science Park – 12 months; Fabrication of exhibits – 24 months; Installation of exhibits – 6 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre – 36 months approximately. - Category 3: Construction of Building – 21 months; Fabrication of exhibits – 18 months; Installation of exhibits/Innovation and creative corner facility – 8 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre – 30 months approximately. > **Validity/Post-Sanction Obligations:** - Over a period of 5 years from opening, the Science Centre should strive to generate at least 50 per cent of its operating cost, achieve an annual visitors footfall of around 2,50,000 for Category 1 (2,00,000 for the North East Region), around 1,50,000 for Category 2 (75,000 for the North East Region) and around 30,000 for Category 3, and organize a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually, in-house and outreach.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society/Authority promoted by the State/Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Science Centre should locate it in a city or town with a population of 15,00,000 or more. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Science Centre should locate it in a city or town with a population between 5,00,000 and 15,00,000. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Science Centre should locate it in a city, town or location with a population of less than 5,00,000. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Science Centre should provide a minimum of 7.0 acres of land. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Science Centre should provide a minimum of 5.0 acres of land. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Science Centre should provide a minimum of 2.0 acres of land. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is preferably centrally located, easily accessible, fully developed, without any low-lying area, of fairly regular shape, and secured with a boundary wall without any encumbrances. 1. The applicant State Government/Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for operation and management. 1. The applicant should obtain all other statutory clearances and approvals required by the local authorities. 1. The applicant should choose the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, NCSM. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is free from all encumbrances and encroachment. 1. The applicant should ensure that electricity, water, sewerage connection and telecommunication facility are available in the nearby vicinity. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land has good road connectivity for easy access and transport. 1. The applicant should not change the land once offered; if any such incident is noticed after release of grant, the released amount shall be recovered with the applicable rate of interest. 1. The applicant should provide provisions for the solar rooftop in the Detailed Project Report. 1. The applicant should ensure that buildings are designed keeping in view applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with NCSM for implementation, if the project is undertaken and implemented by NCSM. > **Preference/Priority/Relaxation:** - For Category 2 Science Centres in the North East region, hilly terrains and island territories, 2.5 to 3.0 acres of land will be acceptable provided the land has good vicinity and accessibility. - In case the land is located in the heart of the city where land availability is scarce, the land requirement may be relaxed in the case of science centres. The building may be constructed in multiple stories utilising the available Floor Space Ratio of the location. However, the Science Park shall be an integral part of the science centre. - Under Type B operational mode, State Governments/Union Territory administrations desirous of having more than one science centre, or wanting accelerated development of Science Centres, shall be given priority, provided they agree to bear the entire operating cost of the centre after it is developed and handed over to the States/Union Territories. - Under Type C, State Governments agreeing to fully fund the science centre project, provide land and other required facilities, and operate and manage them shall be accorded priority. - Under Type A, priority areas and locations/regions where Science Centre activities have not yet started may be considered for full funding from the Ministry of Culture. - The eligibility criteria of population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability may be relaxed and/or modified in special cases/circumstances by the Honourable Chief Minister, Government of India, as stated in the document. - In construction, priority/preference may be given to local material, labour and expertise; use of renewable energy and energy-saving devices may be given top preference.
## Exclusions 1. Under Type A funding, in no case will more than one Science Centre be set up in any State/Union Territory in future under the scheme. 1. In States/Union Territories where NCSM centres already exist, the provision of full funding under Type A shall not be applicable. 1. The principal of the corpus fund shall in no case be utilised for any activity.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** Determine the Category 1 for a population of 15,00,000 or more with a minimum of 7.0 acres; Category 2 for a population between 5,00,000 and 15,00,000 with a minimum of 5.0 acres (2.5 to 3.0 acres for the North East region, hilly terrains and island territories); Category 3 for a population less than 5,00,000 with a minimum of 2.0 acres. **Step 2:** Decide the funding Type A (full funding from the Ministry of Culture), Type B (shared 50:50, or 90:10 for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim) or Type C (full State funding). **Step 3:** Select the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, the National Council of Science Museums. **Step 4:** Obtain the Detailed Project Report format at [Annexure E](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf), with [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) for the Physical Report on Site. **Step 5:** Prepare the Detailed Project Report, including the feasibility report, demand survey, commitment of land free of cost and recurring cost, projected footfall and expected revenue generation. An incomplete Detailed Project Report will render the application liable for rejection. **Step 6:** Attach the mandatory documents, i.e., Copy of Registration, Memorandum of Association or Trust Deed, Letter of Support from State Government, Letter of Recommendation from District Authority, Authorisation Certificate, Commitments for space and operation, and Audited Statement of Accounts for last three years. **Step 7:** Submit the proposal to the _Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture, Government of India, Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi-110001_. **Step 8:** The proposal is considered on the basis of challenge method guidelines, as and when issued by the Government of India. **Step 9:** The Detailed Project Report is appraised by the Project Appraisal Committee for recommendation to the competent authority. **Step 10:** Obtain approval from the Government of India. **Step 11:** Sign the Memorandum of Understanding with the National Council of Science Museums, if implemented by it. **Step 12:** Form the Society immediately after approval of the project and release of the State/Union Territory share of capital cost and corpus fund; the corpus fund share is released upfront prior to commencement of works. **Step 13:** Construction under Type A and Type B, the National Council of Science Museums completes the centre on a turn-key basis and starts work only after the share of funding is received; under Type C, the State constructs the building as per its inputs. **Step 14:** Complete recruitment of core staff within 6 months of the release of funds for 18 posts for Category 1, 8 for Category 2 and 4 for Category 3. **Step 15:** Complete the project within 42 months for Category 1, 36 months for Category 2 and 30 months for Category 3, from the date of issue of the Letter of Intent. **Step 16:** Monitoring is done by an Executive Council set up by the State/Union Territory Government under Type B and Type C. **Step 17:** After opening, achieve the Outcome Evaluation Indicators over 5 years for at least 50 per cent of operating cost generated, annual footfall of around 2,50,000 for Category 1, 1,50,000 for Category 2 and 30,000 for Category 3, and a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually.

# Mukhyamantri Kamdhenu Yojana: Fodder Entrepreneurship Programme **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Odisha | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Green Fodder Cultivation, Livestock Feed Development, Farmer, Dairy Cost Reduction, Subsidy, DBT | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme “Fodder Entrepreneurship Programme” by the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Odisha, under Mukhyamantri Kamdhenu Yojana. It aims to produce green fodder on farmers’ land to feed their livestock and to generate extra income by selling surplus green fodder and planting materials. Through this scheme, subsidy support is provided to eligible farmers and groups for the establishment and maintenance of perennial fodder cultivation over the approved land area. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Odisha, Cuttack, through the Chief District Veterinary Officers and their field functionaries. A physical target of covering 6,000 acres across all districts has been fixed, and district-wise targets are enclosed in Annexure-VI. The programme mandates the cultivation of perennial fodder for 3 consecutive years, and subsidy is released in 3 phases, subject to inspection and verification. > **Objectives** 1. To produce green fodder in farmers' land to feed their livestock and fetch extra income by selling surplus green fodder and planting materials. 1. To build the capacity and sensitize the farming community for the production of green fodder, and regarding feeding practices for their livestock. 1. To encourage farmers for consistent fodder cultivation and hence increase the area under fodder cultivation in Odisha. 1. To maintain the optimum productive and reproductive health status of the livestock. 1. To minimize the milk production cost. 1. To increase the overall milk production of the locality.
## Benefits > **Subsidy Support (Back-Ended, 3 Phases)** - Financial assistance is provided in the form of a back-ended subsidy based on plot size. The subsidy is released in three phases over three years. - Subsidy amount shall be calculated proportionately for plot size up to 10 acres (for groups). - For any item costing ₹20,000/- or more, beneficiaries must make online payments (RTGS/NEFT/UPI). Submission of the online transaction receipt is mandatory for subsidy release. ***Subsidy Amount as per Plot Size*** **Area (in Acres)****1st Year (₹)****2nd Year (₹)****3rd Year (₹)****Total (₹)**0.25₹3,750/-₹3,000/-₹2,000/-₹8,750/-0.5₹7,500/-₹6,000/-₹4,000/-₹17,500/-0.75₹11,250/-₹9,000/-₹6,000/-₹26,250/-1₹15,000/-₹12,000/-₹8,000/-₹35,000/-2₹30,000/-₹24,000/-₹16,000/-₹70,000/-3₹45,000/-₹36,000/-₹24,000/-₹1,05,000/-4₹60,000/-₹48,000/-₹32,000/-₹1,40,000/-5₹75,000/-₹60,000/-₹40,000/-₹1,75,000/-> **Mode of Disbursement** 1. Subsidy is released through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the beneficiary’s bank account in 3 phases: - 1st Phase – After establishment and verification. - 2nd Phase – After 12 months of the go-ahead letter and verification. - 3rd Phase – After continued maintenance and verification in the 3rd year.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must be a resident/domicile of Odisha. 1. The applicant must be a willing farmer (individual or group) to avail support under the Fodder Entrepreneurship Programme. 1. MPCS / WSHG / VSS / FPOs / FPCs / JLGs may apply through their President / Secretary. 1. The applicant must own the land or possess notarized leased land for a minimum period of 3 years. 1. The land on which fodder cultivation is proposed must have an assured irrigation facility. 1. Only one individual per household shall be eligible to avail assistance under the programme. 1. The applicant must mandatorily cultivate fodder on the applied land area for 3 consecutive years. 1. The applicant must submit a declaration for mandatory cultivation for 3 years as prescribed in [Annexure-I (in the guidelines pdf)](https://fard.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-09/Guidelines%20for%20Fodder%20Entrepreneurship.pdf).
## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Registration Process:** **Step 1:** The applicant interested in availing of the subsidy shall apply to the Go-Sugam Portal through a registration process by submitting the requisite documents. **Step 2:** Visit the official website: [https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/home](https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/home) **Step 3:** Click on “Apply” and then click on “Register Now” **Step 4:** On the registration page, fill in the mandatory details (Name, Email, Mobile Number, Address, and Password) and click on "Register". The login credentials will be sent to your registered Email ID / Mobile Number. > **Application Process:** **Step 1:** Visit the official website: [https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/home](https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/home) **Step 2:** Click on “Scheme & Services” and then select the scheme by its name. **Step 3:** Click “Apply” and log in. [https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/citizen-portal/login](https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/citizen-portal/login) **Step 4:** On the application page, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload therequired documents in the appropriate file size and file type. Upon successful submission of the application, the applicant will get an Application Reference ID. > **Check Application Status:** **Step 1:** Click on the “Track Status” link on the menu. **Step 2:** Enter the Application ID or Mobile Number to get the application status. > **Verification, Approval & Subsidy Release Process:** **Step 1:** After submission, the Block Veterinary Officer (BVO) compiles block-wise applications. The Block Level Inspection Team (BLIT) (minimum two members) conducts joint verification of the proposed fodder unit and uploads geo-referenced photographs on the GO-SUGAM portal. **Step 2:** Verified applications are forwarded by the BVO to the Chief District Veterinary Officer (CDVO) within 20 days. The CDVO places the list before the District Task Force for Boosting Fodder Production (under the Chairmanship of the Collector & District Magistrate) for approval. **Step 3:** Upon approval, the CDVO issues the Go-ahead Letter within 7 days. The beneficiary must establish a perennial fodder crop on the approved land within 60 days and report completion on the GO-SUGAM portal. BLIT inspects within 7 days of reporting. **Step 4:** Based on the inspection and recommendation of the BVO, subsidy is released in three phases through DBT to the beneficiary’s bank account (1st year, 2nd year after 12 months, and 3rd year after subsequent inspection). All subsidy releases and inspections are processed through the GO-SUGAM portal. > **Note:** 1. Annexure-I: Declaration for mandatory fodder cultivation for 3 consecutive years (to be submitted by beneficiary). 1. Annexure-II: Initial Field Verification Report by BLIT. 1. Annexure-III: Go-ahead Letter issued by CDVO. 1. Annexure-IV: Intimation by Beneficiary after establishment of perennial fodder crop. 1. Annexure-V: Asset Verification Report for release of subsidy phases. 1. Annexure-VI: District-wise physical targets for implementation. 1. These annexures are all integrated into the [guidelines](https://fard.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-09/Guidelines%20for%20Fodder%20Entrepreneurship.pdf) document. 1. The scheme is given under the name "Fodder Entrepreneurship" in the Go-Sugam Portal.

metadata.briefDescription: The "Women Self Employment Scheme" encourages women to become self-reliant and supports their efforts in establishing small-scale industries or trade ventures, thereby improving their economic status & promoting self-employment opportunities across the state providing them financial assistance.

page_content:
# Women Self Employment Scheme **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Himachal Pradesh | **Categories:** Women and Child, Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Women, Business, Self-Employment | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The "Women Self Employment Scheme" was launched by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of Himachal Pradesh. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to women to start small businesses or trades. This scheme encourages women to become self-reliant and supports their efforts in establishing small-scale industries or trade ventures, thereby improving their economic status and promoting self-employment opportunities across the state.
> ***Purpose:*** The assistance will be given for establishing Tea stall/ Karyana shops/ Pan bidi/cigarette shops/Stationery shop/Tea biscuit shop/Tailor shop/Wool/Khadi/Embroidery shop/Poultary farm/ Maniyari shop/ and any other income generation activities/needs base/identified at local level. ## Benefits - **Financial Assistance of ₹5,000/- provides women to help them start small businesses or trade activities.** ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a woman. 1. The applicant should set up their own business trade, and small industry to earn their livelihood. 1. The applicant's annual income does not exceed ₹35,000/-. 1. Physically handicapped individuals are also eligible to apply under this scheme. ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The interested applicant should visit (during office hours) the District Welfare Officer and request a hard copy of the prescribed format of the application form (Annexure-I) from the staff exclusively entrusted to issue and collect filled-in applications. **Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required). **Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the District Welfare Officer. **Step 4:** Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the District Welfare Officer to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, and a unique identification number (if applicable).

page_content:
# E-YUVA Scheme: E-YUVA Centers

**Ministry:** Ministry Of Science And Technology | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Transport & Infrastructure | **Tags:** E-YUVA, Centers, University, Institution, Bio-incubator, Infrastructure, Equipment | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra

## Description
“Empowering Youth for Undertaking Value Added Innovative Translational Research (E-YUVA)” scheme was started by the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) to promote a culture of applied research and need-oriented (societal or industry) entrepreneurial innovation among young students and researchers. The scheme provides funding support (through fellowship and research grant), technical and business mentoring, exposure to bio incubation model, orientation to an entrepreneurial culture, etc. to students at various levels including undergraduates, post-graduates, and post-doctoral.
> **E-YUVA Centers (EYCs):**

The BIRAC’s E-YUVA scheme is implemented through dedicated hubs called “E-YUVA Centers (EYCs)” housed within the University/Institute set up and mentored by a BIRAC BioNEST-supported bio-incubator. EYCs act as anchors and extend requisite support and mentoring to students. Each EYC has a BIRAC-supported pre-incubation space which offers infrastructure and equipment for basic research and experimentation by selected students. Advanced research needs are fulfilled through Bio-incubator Connect. 
**BIRAC-supported EYCs encompass the following:**

  - Pre-incubation space (3,000 sq. ft. or more)
  - Manage Fellowships for students
  - Conduct Entrepreneurial Awareness Workshops for students

**Roles and Responsibilities of EYCs:**

  - View and process online applications received for fellowship
  - Screen applications for eligibility and suitability for the scheme
  - Carry out online Technical Review of eligible applications through Subject Experts (Reviewers)
  - Shortlist proposals for interview(F2F/skype/telephonic) by an Expert Panel
  - Communicate decision to applicants at each step of selection
  - Seek BIRAC approval on the final selection of fellows or their eligibility
  - Issue fellowship award letters to the selected candidates on behalf of BIRAC
  - Release fellowship and research grant received from BIRAC
  - Provide mentorship, handholding, and access to facilities at EYC and EYC Knowledge Partner for BIRAC’s Innovation and E-YUVA Fellows
  - Monitor the targeted milestones
  - Organize periodic review meetings
  - Provide mentorship and handholding for domain expertise, entrepreneurship, and activities including but not limited to IP management, mobilizing resources, and other business development-related activities
  - Provide platforms/opportunities for interaction with experts.
  - Provide periodic updates and reports on the progress of Fellows to BIRAC
  - Conduct entrepreneurial workshops
  - Any other activity required for effective implementation of fellowships on mutual consent with BIRAC.

> **Tenure of EY Centres:**

EYCs will be engaged for an initial duration of 3 years, extendable further based on performance review. The performance of the EYCs would be evaluated annually.
> **E-Yuva Knowledge Partner:**

For the mentoring of Innovation Fellows and for providing overall guidance to EYCs, BIRAC will assign engagement with BioNEST-supported Bio-incubators. Each EYC will be formally associated with a BioNEST-supported bio incubator, which shall provide necessary handholding and mentoring to EYCs and Innovation Fellows. The knowledge partner will engage with the fellows throughout the award period and provide overall guidance. Bio-incubators will act as brand ambassadors for the program and will help in its outreach.

## Benefits
**Financial Support to each EYC:**
**A. Non-recurring Head (Creating pre-incubation space):**

**Year 1 (INR in Lakhs)****Year 2 (INR in Lakhs)****Year 3 (INR in Lakhs)****Total (INR in Lakhs)**4 Workshops @1 lakh each44412Manpower for EYC (@5% increase/year) Coordinator – 1 @₹75,000/-, Project assistant – 1 @₹25,000/- and Office assistant – 1 @₹15,000/-13.8014.4915.2143.50Travel for EYC staff1113Outreach, publications etc.1113Honorarium for conducting review meetings1113Contingency1113**Sub Total (B)****21.80****22.49****23.21****67.50**T**otal Support (A+B)****61.80****22.49****23.21****107.50**

## Eligibility Criteria
1. University/Institution established as a legal entity under the relevant Law of India having at least 51% Indian stakeholders (owners/partners/trustees/members/associates etc.) from Tier II/III cities is eligible to apply.
   1. The University/Institution could be Public (Central/State)/Private owned.
   1. Other mandatory conditions are as follows: 


  - Applicant University/Institution should have a Department in the Life Sciences stream (Biotechnology/ Biosciences/ Agriculture /Horticulture/ Food technology etc.) for technical support.
  - Age of the applicant University/Institution should be at least 3 years or more.
  - Presence of an Innovation supporting formal body, such as E-Cell/ Institutional Innovation Councils/ IP Cells/ TTOs / Incubation centres, etc. is a must.
  - Offer dedicated space of approx. 3,000 sq. ft. & relevant infrastructure ready for use.

**The applicant organization should have:**

  - Connect with a Bio-incubator.
  - Network of experts who can provide technical/business mentorship to fellows.

**Note:** The Head of the University/ Institution shall appoint/nominate the Project Lead as a contact point for BIRAC EYC until a dedicated staff is appointed for the same.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Online
> **Application Process:**

**Step 01:** Applications for EYCs need to be routed through the Head of the University/Institution.
**Step 02:** The applicant University/Institution allows only online submission of proposals.
**Step 03:** For proposal submission, the applicant University/Institution can [register](https://www.birac.nic.in/login.php) & apply on the BIRAC website “[www.birac.nic.in](https://www.birac.nic.in/cfp_view.php?id=82&scheme_type=31)”.
> **Criteria for selection of BIRAC’s E-Yuva Centers:**

The BIRAC EYC Committee will be responsible for the selection of the new centers taking following criteria into consideration:

  - Allocation of dedicated space & relevant infrastructure ready for use.
  - Past experience of conducting innovation-promoting/entrepreneurial programs desirable
  - Number of Startups formed by the students (in biotech or any other area)
  - Number of Patents filed from the University/ Institution
  - No. of Industry projects handled or Industry connects
  - Funds received or raised for supporting Innovations
  - Accessibility to experts/mentors
  - Willingness & commitment from the Head of the University/Institution to support the program
  - Availability of IP, regulatory, and business support to the EYC fellows. The Institute should be willing to support EYC fellows to facilitate networking through individuals/groups.
  - Connects with bio incubators and other organizations actively promoting Entrepreneurship

**Note:** BIRAC encourages applications from Tier II/III cities for EYCs.
> **Selection Process:**


  - The EYC Committee will be responsible for the evaluation and selection process.
  - After the eligibility check, the proposals received will be evaluated by the EYC Expert Committee on various parameters mentioned in the previous section.
  - The shortlisted proposals will be called for presentation at BIRAC.
  - On the basis of the presentation, the Committee will recommend the proposals for a site visit or direct consideration.
  - After the site visit (if recommended) the recommendations of the site visit committee would be presented to the EYC committee chair for final decision on funding.
  - Once recommended for support, GLA signing will be done with the applicant after financial due diligence.

page_content:
# National Awards For Empowerment Of Persons With Disabilities: National Awards For Institutions Engaged In Empowering Persons With Disabilities: Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan Ke Karyanvayan/badhamukta Vatavaran Ke Srijan Mein Sarvshrestha Rajya/ Ut/ Zila **Ministry:** Ministry Of Social Justice and Empowerment | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Award, District, Person With Disability, Social Welfare | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The "National Awards for Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities" are being awarded by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment every year since 1969 in recognition of the skills and contribution of persons with disabilities, individuals and institutions engaged in the empowerment of persons with disabilities.
> **Award Categories** 1. National Awards for Individual Excellence 2. National Awards for Institutions Engaged in Empowering Persons With Disabilities
The **"Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan Ke Karyanvayan/Badhamukta Vatavaran Ke Srijan Mein Sarvshrestha Rajya/ UT/ Zila"** award is given by DoEPwD for outstanding work in Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan and the creation of a barrier-free environment/working conditions for persons with disabilities, the working place with easy mobility, toilet facilities and directions in the sign language and other indicators, which facilitate easy movements and integrate the persons with disabilities in its overall working milieu. The Department confers national awards to commemorate the 'International Day of Persons with Disabilities' which falls on 3rd December every year. The ceremony of the National Awards is held at Vigyan Bhawan. The National Awards are presented through the Hon'ble President or Hon'ble Vice President of India. ## Benefits > **Decoration** 1. The Awardee is given a Certificate and a Shield
> **Award Categories** 1. One Award for providing holistic comprehensive Rehabilitation Services. 1. One Award for promoting and imparting Inclusive Education or educational institutions that are preparing children with disabilities for inclusive education for higher studies.

> **Presentation of Award (Ceremony Details)** 1. The ceremony of the National Awards is held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi on 3rd December, every year which has been declared as the “International Day of Persons with Disabilities”. 2. The National Awards are presented through the Hon'ble President or Hon'ble Vice President of India. 2. The boarding and lodging expenses of the awardees and one escort shall be borne by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 3. To and fro travelling expenses and accommodation for up to one day prior to and after the day of the awards ceremony shall be arranged and the expenditure shall be reimbursed by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 4. The TA/DA admissibility of the awardees and their escorts shall be equivalent to a Class-I officer of the Central Government. ## Eligibility Criteria > **Criteria 1, Weightage: 15%** 1. Total number of Public buildings in the State* 1. Total Number of Public buildings* identified for the creation of the barrier-free environment. 1. Total number of public buildings out of the above made accessible from Accessible India Campaign funds. * Offices, Cinema Halls, theatres, Parks, Hospitals, Museums, Police Stations, tourist places, Monuments, Educational Institutes, Banks, Post offices, ATMs, Commercial Complexes, Market places, Streets, Libraries, Courts etc.
> **Criteria 2, Weightage: 15%** 1. Total number of cost estimates sent to the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities 1. Total number of buildings for which funds have been given and utilized. (financial year-wise details to be given beginning 2015-16 onwards)
> **Criteria 3, Weightage: 30%** 1. The total number of buildings retrofitted with the following details: a) Accessible Parking with marking as per accessibility standards b) Accessible route connecting parking to alighting point c) Tactile tiles/pavers from parking to the main accessible entrance and till rooms d) Accessible reception counter e) Accessible entrance/doors/corridors f) Ramps – wherever there are level differences or a lift is absent g) Accessible lift h) Signage (audio-visual) conspicuously placed i) Accessible toilet on each floor j) Accessible staircase (colour contrasting strip and Continuous handrails)
> **Criteria 4, Weightage: 20%** 1. The total number of buildings made accessible from state funds. 1. Other important initiatives are taken up to improve the accessibility of public buildings.
> **Criteria 5, Weightage: 20%** Screening Committee may devise any other assessment parameter which may facilitate short-listing of applicants
> **Agencies Eligible to Make Nominations** Any State/UT/ Autonomous Body / PSU and nongovernmental organization registered under the Trust Act/Society Act/Section 8 of Company Act, 2013. ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Official Portal/Link:** https://awards.gov.in/Registration/SignUp > **Call for Applications** Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan) shall intimate the opening of the National Awards Portal as well as the prescribed period for submission of applications through advertisement in the newspapers/website of the Department. Applications/nominations are invited through online mode only on the centralized portal of the Ministry of Home Affairs. (www.awards.gov.in) which is open (w.e.f. 15th June to 31st July).
> **Registration** **Step 1:** Visit the [National Awards Portal](https://awards.gov.in). On the top right of the homepage, click "[Register](https://awards.gov.in/Registration/SignUp)". **Step 2:** You will be directed to the Registration Page. Fill in all the mandatory fields (marked with a Red Asterisk). **Step 3:** Check the "Declaration" checkboxes provided at the bottom of the page. Fill in the Captcha Code, and click "Submit".You will receive the Login Credentials on your Registered Mobile Number.
> **Application** **Step 1:** Visit the [National Awards Portal](https://awards.gov.in/). On the top right of the homepage, click "Login". **Step 2:** Login using credentials. From the list of awards, select "National Awards for Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities", then click "Nominate / Apply Now". **Step 3:** On the next page, fill in all the mandatory fields in the online application form, and then click "Submit".
**Note 1:** The Application should be in Hindi or English language only.
> **Calendar of Activities** 1. Advertisement of National Awards/Opening of National Awards Portal: 1st May 2. Last date of receipt of applications: 31st July 3. Constitution of Screening Committees and National Selection Committees: 31st August 4. Meetings of the Screening Committees: 30thSeptemebr 5. Meeting of the National Selection Committee: 15th October 6. Verification of short-listed candidates: 15th October 7. Information/confirmation to awardees: 31st October 8. Presentation of National Awards: 3rd December (International Day of Persons with Disabilities)

# Reimbursement of membership Fee in Government promoted E-Commerce Portals **Ministry:** Ministry Of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Business, Entrepreneurship | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description Reimbursement of Membership fee of Government promoted e-commerce portals Scheme is a sub scheme under National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub (NSSH) scheme. The component has provision for reimbursement of Annual Membership / Subscription fee of Government promoted e-commerce portals such as GeM, e-khadi, Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED), Tribes India, MSME Mart, etc. to SC/ST Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs).
## Benefits > The financial assistance may be provided 80% or a maximum of ₹ 25,000/- (excluding applicable taxes) whichever is less, per financial year for new as well as renewals for SC/ST MSE. ## Eligibility Criteria 1.
