metadata.schemeName: Museum Grant Scheme: Digitization of Museum Collections
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to funds digitization of museum art objects and collections. Financial assistance up to ₹50,00,000/- is provided to eligible Government and non-Government museums for digitisation, cataloguing and hardware.

page_content:
# Museum Grant Scheme: Digitization of Museum Collections **Ministry:** Ministry Of Culture | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** JATAN, Financial Assistance, Digitization, Cataloguing, Upgradation Of Hardware, Financial Grant, Upgradation Of Software | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme "Museum Grant Scheme: Digitization of Museum Collections" by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, aims to provide financial assistance for digitization of art objects in museums across the country, to make their images/catalogues available on the website. Through this component, financial assistance for Category I museums and Category II museums is provided to Government-owned State/Central level museums (including museums of Public Sector Undertakings) and to eligible Societies, Autonomous Bodies, Local Bodies, Public Sector Undertakings, Academic Institutions and Trusts. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, using the "JATAN" software developed with the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Pune, with digitized art objects uploaded to the website [https://museumsofindia.gov.in/](https://museumsofindia.gov.in/).
## Benefits 1. Category I museums: maximum financial assistance of ₹50,00,000/-. 1. Category II museums: maximum financial assistance of ₹25,00,000/-. 1. Maximum assistance is 80% of the total project cost (90% for museums in the North-Eastern region including Sikkim), subject to the ceilings above; balance to be arranged by the applicant with an undertaking. 1. Admissible components: - Digitization of collections using "JATAN" software developed by the Ministry of Culture and C-DAC Pune. - Photography of artworks for digitization purposes. - Creation of a digital catalogue of museum works for public dissemination through the museum website. - Procurement of hardware (servers, clients, LAN, scanners, cameras, etc.) for digitization works. - Development of an online museum library. - Development of interactive information kiosks for the museum. - Development of a QR Code for the museum. 1. The grant is for works of a capital nature (procurement of computer hardware/software, scanners, cameras, website development) and shall not be used for recurring expenditure such as website hosting/management charges or salaries to IT staff. 1. Financial grant for digitization of museum collections and website development is given only once in 10 years; any further requirement for upgradation of hardware/software in subsequent years must be met by the applicant museum from its own funds. > **Mode of Disbursement:** - Released by the Ministry of Culture in 2 equal instalments. - Release of the 2nd and final instalment is subject to receipt of a Utilization Certificate (as per GFR 2017 with Annexure of UC), interest earned on the Ministry's grant, and a financial year-wise statement of accounts audited by a firm of Chartered Accountants, covering the previous instalment as well as the matching share of the museum. > **Frequency of Disbursement** - 1st instalment (50% of Central Government's share): sanctioned and released after obtaining approval of the Competent Authority on the recommendation of the Expert Committee. - 2nd/final instalment (remaining 50%): released after the grantee institution has utilized 100% of the 1st instalment along with its matching share. > **Validity** - The digitization project must be completed within 2 years from the date of release of the 1st instalment of grant; extension may be sought from the Ministry with full justification for delay, failing which the subsequent instalment will not be released. - If delayed without the Ministry's permission, the museum must refund the entire grant amount along with 10% penal interest.
## Eligibility Criteria > Museums are classified into two categories for this component: > **Category I:** 1. The applicant must be a Government-owned State/Central level museum, including museums of Public Sector Undertakings. > **Category II:** 1. The applicant must be a Society, Autonomous Body, Local Body, Public Sector Undertaking, Academic Institution, or Trust registered as a society under the Indian Societies Act of 1860 (XXI) or similar state legislation, or as a Public Trust under any law in force. 1. The applicant institution should have been in existence after registration for at least 3 years prior to the application. 1. The applicant should have a well-defined constitution and laid-down rules/bye-laws for its functioning. 1. The applicant should be in ownership and possession of a substantial collection of objects of historical and/or cultural importance being displayed in the museum; the nature and number of objects possessed and displayed should be clearly indicated in the proposal. 1. The applicant should produce a certificate from the State Government (Department of Culture or equivalent) attesting to its satisfactory performance. 1. The applicant should not be run for any profit. 1. The applicant institution must be willing to share its collections for online viewing on a website for public information. **Preference/Relaxation:** - The 3-year existence condition for Category II applicants can be relaxed in exceptional and deserving cases by the Secretary (Culture), upon recommendation of the Expert Committee, with reasons recorded in writing.
## Exclusions - The grant shall not be used for recurring items of expenditure such as website hosting and management charges, or salaries to IT staff employed for the purpose.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Step 1:** The applicant visits [www.csms.nic.in](https://www.csms.nic.in/) and applies online; the scheme is open throughout the year with no fixed last date for submission of proposals. **Step 2:** The applicant fills in the prescribed Form B ("Form of Application for Financial Grant under the Scheme for Financial Assistance for Digitization of Museum Collections") and attaches all the documents listed in the document section. **Step 3:** Applications are processed and appraised on a first-come-first-served basis. **Step 4:** The applications are scrutinized by an Expert Committee under the Chairmanship of the Additional Secretary, set up by the Ministry of Culture, and grants are sanctioned on the basis of the Committee's recommendations. **Step 5:** Once the recommendation is accepted by the Competent Authority (Secretary, Culture), the concerned Joint Secretary releases funds in instalments, in consultation with the Integrated Finance Division of the Ministry. **Step 6:** The final instalment is released only after physical inspection by a committee of officers from the Ministry of Culture and receipt of documents for the 1st instalment.

metadata.schemeName: Promotion of Research & Development in Iron & Steel Sector
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote Research & Development (R&D) in the iron & steel sector by providing financial support to stakeholders to address R&D needs of national importance, and to catalyse innovation, sustainability and global competitiveness in the steel sector.

page_content:
# Promotion of Research & Development in Iron & Steel Sector **Ministry:** Ministry Of Steel | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship | **Tags:** Financial Assistance, Research & Development, Iron, Steel, Stakeholder | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The "Promotion of Research & Development in Iron & Steel Sector" scheme launched by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India. It aims to promote Research & Development (R&D) in the iron & steel sector by providing financial support to stakeholders to address R&D needs of national importance, and to catalyse innovation, sustainability and global competitiveness in the steel sector. Under this scheme, financial assistance for R&D projects at lab scale, bench scale and pilot or demonstration scale is provided to reputed academic institutions, research laboratories and Indian steel companies, with access to scheme-funded facilities for individual innovators and start-ups. > **Thrust Areas** - Innovative or path-breaking technologies for using iron ore fines and non-coking coal. - Beneficiation of raw materials like iron ore and coal, and agglomeration. - Improving the quality of steel produced through various steelmaking routes, including the Induction Furnace route. - Commercially viable technology for using steel plant and mine wastes, including LD (Linz-Donawitz), EAF (Electric Arc Furnace) and IF (Induction Furnace) slag. - Indigenous technologies for improved processes. - Indigenous technologies for product development aimed at reducing import dependency in the iron & steel sector. - R&D for achieving global benchmarks in productivity, quality, and consumption of raw materials, energy, water and refractories. - Low carbon technologies for reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions. - Innovative technology for effective recovery of waste heat in iron & steel making processes, including downstream processes. - R&D on steel-intensive design of buildings, bridges and structures, to increase the use and consumption of steel. - Innovative solutions for challenges faced by the iron & steel industry. - R&D on any other subject of national importance concerning the iron & steel sector.
## Benefits > **Financial Assistance** - Financial assistance is provided for R&D work at lab scale or bench scale, and for scale-up to pilot scale or demonstration plants. - Industrial or commercial organizations pursuing R&D projects with Plan Fund get financial assistance of up to 50% of the total project cost. - Academic institutions and national or regional research laboratories get financial assistance of up to 70% of the total project cost. - For pilot or demonstration scale R&D projects, the contribution from the Plan Fund is limited to up to 40%. The balance must be met by the industrial partner. - Financial assistance of up to 100% may be given to a multidimensional team. This is at the discretion of the Secretary, Steel, based on the merit of the proposal. - The total budget allocated for the scheme is around ₹5,00,00,000 to ₹10,00,00,000 per year. > **Non-Monetary Benefits** - The Ministry will create a categorized pool of industrial partners, including Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), aligned with key thrust areas. If a Principal Investigator (PI) cannot secure an industry partner, the Ministry will route the proposal to the relevant pool for review and potential funding or collaboration. - Individual innovators and start-ups in the steel sector will get access to scheme-funded facilities and equipment, for example at the National Metallurgical Laboratory (NML) and IIMT. - Based on the merit of their proposals, individual innovators and start-ups will be provided suitable industry and institutional partners. - PIs of successfully completed and commercially adopted projects will get recognition awards or certificates. They will also get attribution in official repositories, the digital repository of indigenous technologies, and compendiums. - The grantee institution will possess the Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) arising from the Ministry-funded project. The patent may be filed in the name of the inventor(s) or the institution(s). - The grantee institution may retain the benefits and earnings from the IPR, to be ploughed back into research or research-related activities. > **Conditions Associated with the Benefits** - Overheads are capped at 10% to 15% of the project cost, up to ₹25,00,000. An industry partner funding at least 15% of research expenditure may claim first use of the outcomes. - Funds are released pro-rata, after other funding agencies pay their share. Organisations with substantial unspent grants will not get new project grants and may be asked to use those funds. - Grants must be used only for the project. Misused grants must be refunded with 6% annual interest. - Interest earned must be returned yearly, and any surplus returned at project end, with transaction details. - Assets, prototypes, pilot plants, materials and scrap from the project cannot be disposed of within 10 years without written permission from the Ministry of Steel (MoS). Sale proceeds must be returned to the Government proportionately. - Equipment must display the Ministry and scheme name, with due credit in later work. The residual value of equipment scrapped under the General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017 must be reported. Working surplus items may be gifted to educational institutions. - The MoS gets a royalty-free licence for non-commercial IP. Commercial licensing terms are mutually agreed, and exclusive licensing needs Ministry approval. The Ministry may take over IP for national priority without compensation. - Jointly developed technology and Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) stay with the partners. Others need partner approval and must pay a royalty, shared by contribution. Results cannot be published before patenting without MoS permission. > **Expected Time of Disbursement** - Funds under the capital head are released only when the R&D agency is ready to place orders for equipment. This means the technical specifications must be finalised and the supplier selected and finalised for order placement. - The last instalment, which is 10% of the total revenue grant, is released only after the Project Completion Report is submitted in the prescribed format and accepted by the Ministry of Steel. - If the Project Review Committee (PRC) recommends the project as foreclosed or failed, the last instalment will not be released. - The MoS may take an undertaking from institutes that they will pay the final 10% to the PIs on behalf of the MoS. The MoS will then reimburse this amount to the institutes once the Project Completion Report is received and approved.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a reputed academic institution, a research laboratory, or an Indian steel company. 1. The applicant may be an industrial or commercial organisation pursuing R&D projects. 1. The applicant may be an individual innovator or a start-up in the steel sector. Such applicants are eligible for access to scheme-funded facilities and equipment. 1. The applicant's proposal should fall under one of the thrust areas of the scheme. 1. The applicant's project should have a heavy bias in favour of commercialisation and technology development. 1. The applicant should have an institutional mechanism for taking completed R&D projects towards commercialisation. 1. The applicant should give a written commitment that, on successful completion, the project will be taken forward through the existing institutional mechanism. 1. The applicant should not have availed any grant-in-aid for the same purpose from any other Ministry or Department of the Government of India or of a State Government. 1. The applicant should declare that similar projects have not been pursued earlier by them or by other organisations. 1. The applicant should accept the Scheme Guidelines and the Terms & Conditions of the sanction. 1. The applicant's proposal should be duly signed and forwarded by the Head of the Institution, Organization or Company.
## Exclusions 1. Basic research should not be funded or should be funded in much smaller amounts and numbers, since other Government agencies such as the Department of Science and Technology (DST) promote basic research. 1. Organizations with substantial unspent grants will not be released grants for new projects. 1. R&D agencies or industrial partners not pursuing projects as per the envisaged objectives will be debarred from funding for new projects. 1. If delays due to negligence occur repeatedly within a single project, or across multiple projects led by the same PI or industry entity, that PI or entity will be ineligible for future Government grants. 1. The R&D agency must not hand over execution of the project to another institution or organization, unless the Project Approval and Monitoring Committee (PAMC) approves it.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Application Process** **Step 01:** Go through the scheme guidelines, formats and Terms & Conditions given in Annexure-1, Annexure-2, Annexure-3 and Annexure-4 of the scheme. **Step 02:** Prepare the R&D proposal using the Guiding Format in Annexure-3, attaching all required documents and declarations. **Step 03:** Get the proposal signed and forwarded by the Head of the Institution, Organization or Company. For joint proposals, it must be forwarded jointly and signed by the Heads of all executing and collaborating agencies. **Step 04:** Upload the proposal to the Ministry of Steel R&D portal. **Step 05:** Send the proposal as a PDF to mosteel-rd@gov.in. **For queries** contact the Technical Division, Ministry of Steel, at 011-26773364. > **Evaluation and Approval** **Step 01:** An Evaluation Group evaluates the proposals. It has members from the office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, the Defence Research and Development Organization (DRDO), DSIR, DST, premier academic institutions and industry. **Step 02:** The PAMC is the second-stage approving body for proposals recommended by the Evaluation Group. It is chaired by the Additional Secretary & Financial Adviser and Joint Secretary, Ministry of Steel. Its members are the Director of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur, the Director of the Institute of Minerals and Materials Technology (IMMT), the Director of NML, and a representative from MSME. **Step 03:** The designated authority gives final approval, based on the project cost, as per the guidelines of the Department of Expenditure. > **Post-Sanction Reporting and Monitoring** **Step 01:** Submit Progress Reports and the Asset Register monthly and quarterly, each within 7 days of the period's end, endorsed by the Head of the Organization. Also submit Quarterly Project Status Reports in the Annexure-4 format, including the status of expenditure uploaded in the Expenditure, Advance and Transfer (EAT) module of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). The Asset Register will be in the public domain. **Step 02:** Submit the Utilization Certificate and Statement of Account quarterly, within 7 days of the quarter's end. Submit the Utilization Certificate and Audited Statement of Account within 1 month of the financial year's end. Both must be endorsed by the Head of the Organization. **Step 03:** The Project Review Committee (PRC) reviews the project every 6 months, preferably online. For delayed projects caused by negligence, a show cause notice is issued to the PI and industry partner, with copies to the Director of the Institute and the CEO of the industry partner. **Step 04:** Procure equipment through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM). If the equipment is not on GeM, it may be procured from outside while it is onboarded onto GeM in parallel. **Step 05:** Send 5 copies of the Project Completion Report to the Ministry of Steel within 1 month of project completion. **Step 06:** Inform the Ministry within 6 weeks of closing any agreement to trade, sell, transfer or license the IP.

metadata.schemeName: Mukhyamantri Krushi Udyog Yojana: Top-up subsidy for Commercial Dairy Farming
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to encourage large dairy farmers/entrepreneurs to procure high-yielding cattle from outside the state. Through this scheme, an additional 15% subsidy on animal cost as a Top-Up will be provided to the entrepreneurs towards the purchase of animals from outside the state.

page_content:
# Mukhyamantri Krushi Udyog Yojana: Top-up subsidy for Commercial Dairy Farming **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Odisha | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Subsidy, MKUY, Agri-Entrepreneurship, DBT | **Target Beneficiaries:** Infra ## Description The scheme “Top-up subsidy for Commercial Dairy Farming” was launched by the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Odisha, under Mukhyamantri Krushi Udyog Yojana (MKUY). It aims to encourage large dairy farmers/entrepreneurs to procure high-yielding cattle from outside the state. Through this scheme, an additional 15% subsidy on animal cost as a Top-Up will be provided to the entrepreneurs towards the purchase of animals from outside the State. The scheme shall be implemented by the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Odisha, Cuttack in collaboration with APICOL. The top-up subsidy will be calculated based on the eligible Capital Investment for cattle as per MKUY guidelines. Top-up subsidy will not be considered for the calculation of up-front subsidy, rather it will be released only after the completion of the project during the final release of CIS. Only MKUY dairy entrepreneurs are eligible to avail the “Top-up subsidy” under this scheme, and it is mandatory to bring cattle from outside the state. > **Objectives** 1. To encourage large dairy farmer/entrepreneurs to procure high-yielding cattle from outside the state
## Benefits 1. Mukhyamantri Krushi Udyog Yojana (MKUY) is a flagship programme of the State Govt. Under this scheme, 40% subsidy on capital investment is being provided to the general category, & 50% subsidy to SC/ ST/ Women/ PWD/ Transgender category and Agriculture & allied graduate. 1. Under "Top-up subsidy for MKUY Commercial Dairy Farming under MKY", an additional 15% subsidy on animal cost as TорUp will be provided to the entrepreneurs towards the purchase of animals from outside the State. 1. The top-up subsidy will be calculated based on the eligible Capital Investment for cattle as per MKUY guidelines and will be released by APICOL in DBT mode. 1. Top-up subsidy will not be considered for the calculation of the up-front subsidy; rather, it will be released only after the completion of the project during the final release of CIS.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must be a resident/domicile of Odisha. 1. The applicant must be an MKUY dairy entrepreneur. 1. The applicant must be any Individual / Partnership Enterprise / Group of Individuals / Registered Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) / Farmer Producer Company (FPC) / Farmer Producer Group (FPG) / Non-Government Organisation (NGO) (Society only) / Self-Help Group (SHG) / Gram Panchayat Level Federation (GPLF) / Block Level Federation (BLF) / District Level Federation (DLF) / Primary Agriculture Cooperative Society (PACS) / Large Area Multipurpose Society (LAMPS) / Farmers Cooperative Societies / Apex Federations such as OMFED / OPOLFED / FISHFED / Companies registered under Companies Act, 2013. 1. The applicant shall bring cattle from outside the state to avail the Top-up subsidy. 1. The applicant who purchased the cattle after the release of this guideline (even though a go-ahead letter was issued earlier) can avail the subsidy. 1. The applicant shall be at least 18 years old on the date of submission of the online application. 1. The applicant shall hold land in his/her own name, or in the name of their spouse. 1. The applicant shall hold land under a registered lease for a minimum period of 15 years in the State of Odisha. 1. The applicant shall possess a valid Aadhaar. 1. The applicant may establish more than one enterprise in different sectors. 1. The applicant shall be eligible for a subsidy for multiple enterprises, subject to the overall subsidy limit per beneficiary/family. 1. The applicant’s subsidy limit shall apply per beneficiary/family. 1. The family shall include the individual, spouse, unmarried sons/daughters, married sons, and dependent parents. 1. The applicant shall complete the project within the stipulated time period as prescribed in the guidelines. 1. The applicant shall be liable for subsidy deduction or cancellation in case of delay beyond the permissible period. > **Preference / Priority / Reservation / Relaxation** 1. The applicant belonging to the SC/ST/Women/Transgender/PwD category shall be eligible for a higher subsidy rate. 1. The applicant, being a Graduate in Agriculture or an allied discipline, shall be eligible for a higher subsidy rate.
## Exclusions 1. The applicant who does not bring cattle from outside the state is not eligible for the Top-up subsidy.
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online > **Registration Process:** **Step 1:** The applicant interested in availing of the subsidy shall apply to the Go-Sugam Portal through a registration process by submitting the requisite documents. **Step 2:** Visit the official website: [https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/home](https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/home) **Step 3:** Click on “Apply” and then click on “Register Now” **Step 4:** On the registration page, fill in the mandatory details (Name, Email, Mobile Number, Address, and Password) and click on "Register". The login credentials will be sent to your registered Email ID / Mobile Number. > **Application Process:** **Step 1:** Visit the official website: [https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/home](https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/home) **Step 2:** Click on “Scheme & Services” and then select the scheme by its name. **Step 3:** Click “Apply” and log in. [https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/citizen-portal/login](https://sugam.odisha.gov.in/website/citizen-portal/login) **Step 4:** On the application page, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload the required documents in the appropriate file size and file type. Upon successful submission of the application, the applicant will get an Application Reference ID. > **Check Application Status:** **Step 1:** Click on the “Track Status” link on the menu. **Step 2:** Enter the Application ID or Mobile Number to get the application status. > **Post-Application & Top-Up Subsidy Process:** **Step 5:** The MKUY beneficiary shall upload the option with respect to the outside purchase of an animal in the Go-Sugam portal at the time of submission of the completion report. **Step 6:** The animal procured by the beneficiary shall be verified by the District Nodal Officer (DNO). **Step 7:** The DNO shall upload the certificate regarding the outside purchase as per Annexure-XXI. **Step 8:** The Chief District Veterinary Officer (CDVO) shall submit a proposal along with a certificate to APICOL for sanction and release of additional top-up subsidy at 15% on animal cost, along with the final Capital Investment Subsidy (CIS) proposal as per MKUY guidelines. **Step 9:** The Top-up subsidy shall be released by APICOL in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode as per MKUY guidelines. > **Note:** 1. [Annexure-XXI](https://fard.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-09/Top-up%20subsidy%20.pdf) – Certificate regarding outside purchase of cattle (to be uploaded by DNO).

metadata.schemeName: Scheme of Financial Assistance to New Writers of Gujarati Language and Literature for Publishing Original Works of Creative and Fine Literature
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to financially support new writers in the Gujarati language who wish to publish original works of creative and literary merit.

page_content:
# Scheme of Financial Assistance to New Writers of Gujarati Language and Literature for Publishing Original Works of Creative and Fine Literature

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Gujarat | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Gujarati Literature, Author, Book Printing Aid

## Description
The "Scheme of Financial Assistance to New Writers of Gujarati Language and Literature for Publishing Original Works of Creative and Fine Literature" has been designed to encourage first-time authors who lack financial means to publish original and high-quality creative works in the Gujarati language. Administered by the Gujarat Sahitya Academy, the scheme provides grants to cover partial printing costs for eligible manuscripts. Works eligible for assistance include novels, short stories, essays, poetry, and plays that promote cultural awareness, national unity, and intellectual development. The manuscript must be original, unpublished, and reviewed positively by expert evaluators.

## Benefits
> **Financial Assistance:**


- **For manuscripts with up to 112 pages:** Up to ₹10,000/-.- **For manuscripts exceeding 112 pages:** Up to ₹15,000/-.
> **Printing Size Guidelines:**


- **For “Crown” size:** ₹2,100/- (paperback), ₹2,200/- (hardcover).- **For “Demy” size:** ₹2,300/- (paperback), ₹2,500/- (hardcover).- **For “Double Crown” size:** ₹2,700/- (paperback), ₹2,800/- (hardcover).
> **Note:** The lower of the printing cost or the above ceiling will be granted as assistance.

## Eligibility Criteria
- The applicant must be a first-time writer in the Gujarati language and literature.
  - The manuscript must be an original literary work such as a novel, play, essay, poetry collection, or autobiography.
  - The manuscript must not be edited work or related to non-literary subjects.
  - The applicant must not have received more than five grants from any language academy affiliated with Gujarat Sahitya Academy.
  - The manuscript must be typed, bound, paginated, and submitted in two copies.
  - The applicant must not change the title, content, or format after submission without written permission from the Academy.

Note: Only one application per financial year is allowed per author.

**Step 3:** Click on the checkbox and verify the captcha.
**Step 4:** Click on the "Submit" button to complete the application process.

# Intensive Fisheries Development Programme - Subsidy on Purchase of Fishing Nets (Scheduled Caste)

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Haryana | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Fishing Nets, Subsidy, Fishermen, Scheduled Caste, Fisheries

## Description
The "Subsidy on Purchase of Fishing Nets" is a scheme component under the Intensive Fisheries Development Programme, introduced by the Fisheries Department, Government of Haryana. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to individuals from Scheduled Caste families engaged in fishing activities for the purchase of fishing nets. Under this scheme, eligible beneficiaries can avail a subsidy of up to 60% on the cost of fishing nets.

## Benefits
**Financial Assistance is provided to Fish Farmers under the scheme:** 

- Financial assistance of 60% subsidy on the purchase of fishing nets of amounting to ₹40,000/-.
- The maximum subsidy amount is ₹24,000/-.

> **Note:** Subsidy is available only once in two years per beneficiary.

## Eligibility Criteria
1. The applicant should be a permanent resident of Haryana.

1. The applicant should present a GST-paid bill for the purchase of fishing nets.

## Description
The scheme "Working Women Hostel" by the Women and Child Development Department, Government of Haryana aims to provide secure, affordable, and conveniently located housing to employed women to enable them to become socially and economically independent. The scheme also intends to ensure a supportive environment for working women, particularly those away from their homes. The scheme is implemented by the respective designated implementing organizations managing the hostels. These hostels are meant to serve women who are working professionals and need residential support in cities or towns where they are employed.

page_content:
# PMMSY: Establishment of large RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Haryana | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment, Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Fish, Aquaculture, Biofloc, Farming, RAS ## Description The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana: Establishment of Large RAS / Biofloc Culture System, introduced by the Ministry Of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, aims to provide capital assistance for setting up large-scale Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and Biofloc culture systems to promote high-yield, sustainable fish farming. It is a centrally funded scheme with a 50:50 cost-sharing pattern between the Central and State Governments. - For RAS: A minimum of 8 tanks of 90 m³ each (capacity: 40 tons/crop).- For Biofloc: 50 tanks of 4 m diameter and 1.5 m height. The scheme encourages the adoption of modern aquaculture infrastructure, particularly by trained and certified individuals. It offers enhanced subsidy support for SC and Women beneficiaries, aiming to boost inclusive and sustainable fish farming practices.



## Benefits - The project cost is ₹50,00,000/- > **RAS (Recirculating Aquaculture System) Subsidy:** 1. A 20% subsidy is available for the General Category. 1. A 25% subsidy is offered for SC (Scheduled Caste) and Women beneficiaries. > **Biofloc Subsidy:** 1. A 40% subsidy is available for the General Category. 1. A 60% subsidy is offered for SC (Scheduled Caste) and Women beneficiaries. ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant must be a permanent resident of Haryana and possess a valid Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP). 1. The applicant must belong to either the General, Scheduled Caste (SC), or Women category. 1. The applicant must be the owner or legal leaseholder (with a minimum 10-year lease) of the land intended for setting up the unit. 1. The applicant must have access to either surface water or groundwater for aquaculture purposes. 1. The applicant must hold a valid training certificate in fisheries or aquaculture. 1. The applicant must be willing to maintain and operate the unit at personal cost after the initial setup. 1. The applicant must submit a complete Detailed Project Report (DPR) or a Self-Contained Proposal (SCP) for evaluation. 1. The applicant must agree to sign an official agreement with the Fisheries Department to avail of benefits under the scheme. ## Exclusions

metadata.briefDescription: Self-employment loan scheme for Rabari and Bharwad women in Gujarat, offering up to ₹2 lakh at 5% annual interest to promote economic independence.

page_content:
# NEW SWARNIMA (Gopalak Nigam) **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Gujarat | **Categories:** Business & Entrepreneurship, Social welfare & Empowerment, Women and Child | **Tags:** Rabari Bharwad Scheme, Gopalak Vikas Nigam, Women Entrepreneurs, Gujarat Loan Scheme ## Description The **New Swarnima Scheme** is a financial empowerment initiative by the **Gujarat Gopalak Vikas Nigam** under the **Social Justice and Empowerment Department**. It aims to provide **100% loan** support to women from the **Rabari and Bharwad communities** to promote self-employment and entrepreneurship. Eligible women between the **age of 21 and 45 years**, with an **annual family income up to ₹3 lakh**, can receive a **loan of up to ₹2 lakh** at a subsidized **interest rate of 5% per annum** to start a business of their choice. The scheme is designed to increase economic independence and livelihood generation among backward class women. ## Benefits - **100% loan** assistance provided to eligible women- Loan amount up to **₹2.00 lakh**- Interest rate fixed at **5% per annum**- Loan can be used to **start a business** of the beneficiary’s choice- Meant for **economically backward women** of specific castes- **Encourages entrepreneurship and self-reliance** ## Eligibility Criteria 1. Be a permanent **resident of Gujarat**1. Be a **woman**1. Belong to the **Rabari or Bharwad caste**1. Belong to a **socially and educationally backward class** as recognized by the Government of Gujarat1. Be between **21 to 45 years** of age1. Have a **total annual family** income not exceeding **₹3.00 lakh**1. Intend to start your **own business or self-employment** venture using the loan ## Exclusions
## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Step 1:** Visit the official [**DAADC**](https://daadconline.gujarat.gov.in/) online portal. **Step 2:** **Register/log in** using your credentials. **Step 3:** Fill out the application form with accurate personal and scheme-specific details. **Step 4:** Upload the **required documents** and submit.

# Training for Horticulture Skill Development for Self-Employment at Centre of Excellence

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Gujarat | **Categories:** Skills & Employment | **Tags:** Horticulture Training, Skill Development, Self-Employment, Student

## Description
The scheme "Training for Horticulture Skill Development for Self-Employment at Centre of Excellence" introduced by the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Gujarat,  aims to offer structured training programs ranging from 10 to 30 days, focusing on horticultural skills to enable self-employment. Beneficiaries gain access to a complete learning experience, including expert sessions, training literature, educational tours, and practical kits.

page_content:
# Rajya Dairy Udhyamita Vikas Yojna **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Agriculture, Animal, Dairy, Financial Assistance ## Description the scheme "Male Pig Distribution Scheme" is an Animal Husbandry scheme by the Animal Husbandry Department, Government of Chhattisgarh, aims to promote dairy entrepreneurship among youth. With the increasing demand for milk and dairy products, the scheme supports high-breed cow/buffalo rearing as a profitable business.
**Objectives:** Encourage self-employment in the dairy sector. Boost dairy farming as an additional income source. Increase milk production and improve nutrition. Support the expansion of existing dairy units. ## Benefits **Dairy Unit Grant Details** **1. Financial Assistance for Dairy Units** - **Eligible Animals:** Indian dairy breeds (Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Gir, Tharparkar, etc.), advanced crossbreed cows, and high-breed buffaloes.- **Maximum Limit:** Financial support for up to two milch animals.- **Total Finance Cost:** ₹1,40,000/- (₹70,000/- per animal, including three years of insurance). **2. Subsidy Details** **For General Category Beneficiaries:** - 50% subsidy on the actual cost, up to ₹70,000/- per unit. - For SC/ST Beneficiaries: 66.6% subsidy, up to ₹93,200/- per unit. **Note:** Unit cost per animal is based on the Government of India’s guidelines (Letter No. F 1-1/2009-DP, dated 02 May 2018). ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a resident of Chhattisgarh for at least five years. 1. The applicant should be purchase a maximum of two milch animals under the scheme. 1. The applicant should be entitled to 50% subsidy (up to ₹70,000/-) for general category and 66.6% subsidy (up to ₹93,200/-) for SC/ST category. 1. The applicant should be responsible for any additional costs beyond the scheme’s provisions, with no subsidy provided for the excess amount. 1. The applicant should ensure that the purchased animal is in milk production, not older than five years, and capable of producing at least 10 liters of milk per day at the time of purchase. 1. The applicant should have the animal insured for a minimum period of three years (total five years recommended) at the time of unit setup. 1. The applicant should be a landless, small or marginal farmer, BPL family member, milk co-operative society member, village resident on a milk collection route, Garva Yojana beneficiary, women SHG member, or an existing dairy farmer, as they will receive priority. 1. The applicant should be the only eligible beneficiary from a joint family. 1. The applicant should not own at least two high-breed dairy animals at the time of applying for the scheme. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Registration of Application:** - Applications will be registered at the development block-level institution (Veterinary Hospital / Artificial Insemination Centre / Main Village Block). - The prescribed register will record Date, Financial Year, Institution Name, and Registration Date. **Submission of Application:** - Applications must be submitted in the prescribed form at the nearest veterinary institution, such as a veterinary dispensary, artificial insemination sub-centre, main village unit, veterinary hospital, or artificial insemination centre within the development block. **Verification and Forwarding:** - After registration at the block level, applications will be sent to the departmental district office for verification. - Bank-linked applications will be verified and forwarded to banks, with details maintained in official records.

metadata.schemeName: State Goat Entrepreneurship Development Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The "State Goat Entrepreneurship Development Scheme", initiated by the Animal Husbandry Department of Chhattisgarh, aims to promote goat farming as a sustainable livelihood option. Goat rearing has been a traditional occupation, and with increasing demand for milk and meat.

page_content:
# State Goat Entrepreneurship Development Scheme **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Agriculture, Animal, Goat, Financial Assistance ## Description The "State Goat Entrepreneurship Development Scheme" is an Animal Husbandry scheme by the Animal Husbandry Department, Government of Chhattisgarh, which aims to promote goat farming as a sustainable livelihood option. Goat rearing has been a traditional occupation, and with increasing demand for milk and meat, advanced goat farming presents a profitable self-employment opportunity in rural areas.
**Objectives** - To boost the supply of milk and meat through organized goat farming. - To provide an additional source of income for rural households. - To offer technical and financial support for setting up goat farming units.
**Key Features** - Low Investment, High Returns: Goat farming requires minimal investment but yields significant income. - **Nutritional Benefits:** Goat milk is highly nutritious and easily digestible, making it ideal for children and patients.- **High-Quality Meat:** Goat meat is rich in protein and has high market demand.- **Fast Breeding Rate:** Goats have a short reproductive cycle and can produce multiple offspring.- **Drought Resilience:** Goats can survive in harsh conditions, making them a reliable source of income even during droughts.
## Benefits **Financial Assistance Under the State Goat Entrepreneurship Development Scheme** - **Total finance cost:** ₹1,00,000/- per goat unit (30 goats + 2 improved breed goats).- **For general category beneficiaries:** 25% subsidy on the total cost, up to a maximum of ₹₹25,000/-- **For SC/ST beneficiaries:** 33.3% subsidy on the total cost, up to a maximum of ₹33,300/-.
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a resident of Chhattisgarh for at least five years. 1. The applicant should be linked to a loan from a Nationalized, Cooperative, or Regional Rural Bank. 1. The applicant should be willing to sign a contract with the department to operate the unit for at least three years. 1. The applicant should be eligible for the grant only after obtaining the Unit Establishment Verification Certificate, a demand letter from the bank, and submitting necessary documents. 1. The applicant should be the only person from a joint family applying for the grant. 1. The applicant should be aware that a joint family receiving benefits under the scheme cannot reapply for the next five years. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Application Submission** - The applicant must submit the application in the prescribed format at the nearest veterinary institution (veterinary dispensary, artificial insemination sub-centre, main village unit, veterinary hospital, artificial insemination centre, or main village block). - The application will be registered at the development block-level veterinary institution. **Forwarding to Bank** - The Department will forward the application to the bank branch suggested by the applicant for loan approval. **Loan Approval & Animal Purchase** - After loan approval from the respective bank (nationalized, cooperative, or regional rural bank), the applicant will purchase the animals. **Grant Release** - Once the bank approves the loan and the beneficiary purchases the animals, the bank will submit a demand letter along with the verification report to the Joint/Deputy Director, Veterinary Services of the concerned district. - Based on the report, the grant will be approved, and the amount will be disbursed to the bank.

metadata.schemeName: Distribution of Horticulture Kit to Urban and Rural Areas
metadata.briefDescription: Through this scheme, all the horticulture growers in rural & urban areas are provided with a horticulture kit worth ₹ 3,000 per kit to urban and rural areas, during Aadipattam/Thaipattam, through the Additional Director of Agriculture (Horticulture).

page_content:
# Distribution of Horticulture Kit to Urban and Rural Areas

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Puducherry | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Horticulture, Agriculture, Farmer, Subsidy, DBT

## Description
The scheme “Distribution of Horticulture Kit to Urban and Rural Areas" was launched by the Department of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare, Union Territory of Puducherry. Through this scheme, all the horticulture growers in rural & urban areas are provided with a horticulture kit worth ₹ 3,000 per kit to urban and rural areas, during Aadipattam/Thaipattam, through the Additional Director of Agriculture (Horticulture).

## Benefits
75% subsidy, i.e. distribution of horticulture kit worth ₹ 3,000 per kit to urban and rural areas (homestead/backyards), through the Additional Director of Agriculture (Horticulture), during Aadipattam/Thaipattam seasonality.

## Eligibility Criteria
All horticulture growers of rural & urban areas are eligible.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Offline
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should visit (during office hours) the [Uzhavar Udhaviyagam (Farmers' Help Centres) or the Office of the Additional Director of Agriculture (Horticulture)](https://agri.py.gov.in/emailcontact.html) and request the hard copy of the prescribed format of the application form from the Agricultural Officer.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form and the documents to the concerned authority.
**Step 4:** On receipt of the application, necessary entries will be made in the application receipt register and a unique number is assigned to the applicant for identifying each applicant which shall be used for all further references and also as acknowledgement for the receipt of the application.

metadata.schemeName: Paddy Transplantor Machine se Dhan Ropayee par Anudan
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme aims to promote mechanized paddy transplantation under the Agriculture Development and Farmer Welfare and Biotechnology Department, Chhattisgarh. It provides ₹3,000 per acre for land preparation, including ploughing and weeding, up to 2 hectares.

page_content:
# Paddy Transplantor Machine se Dhan Ropayee par Anudan **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Agriculture, Farming, Farmer, Financial Assistance ## Description The scheme was launched on December 26, 2014, The Paddy Transplanter Machine Se Dhan Ropayee Par Anudan, under the Agriculture Development and Farmer Welfare and Biotechnology Department, Chhattisgarh. The scheme aims to promote paddy transplantation using advanced technology, expand the area under transplantation, and improve efficiency in rice cultivation. The scheme is applicable across the entire state, benefiting farmers by providing financial assistance for land preparation. A grant of ₹3,000 per acre will be given for activities such as ploughing and weeding, up to a maximum limit of 2 hectares. This assistance covers the preparation of a mat-type nursery and the transplantation of paddy using a paddy transplanter machine, ensuring improved efficiency and higher yields. ## Benefits **(A) Field Preparation Expenditure per Hectare:** - Field Ploughing (5 hours @ ₹700 per hour): ₹3,500/- - Field Weeding (6 hours with Rotavator @ ₹700 per hour): ₹4,200/- - Total Field Preparation Cost: ₹7,700/- **(B) Expenditure for Seedling Preparation per Hectare:** - Plastic Sheet for Nursery (15 Kg @ ₹100 per Kg): ₹1,500/- - Field Weeding (6 hours with Rotavator @ ₹500 per hour): ₹3,000/- - Other Expenses (Soil, Manure, Sand, Water - arranged by the farmer): Not Included - Additional Contingencies: ₹500/- - Total Seedling Preparation Cost: ₹5,000/- **Total Expenditure per Hectare:** - Field Preparation (A) + Seedling Preparation (B): ₹7,700 + ₹5,000 = ₹12,500/- per hectare - Cost per Acre: ₹5,080/- **Subsidy Details:** - Subsidy Amount: 75% of the cost - Maximum Subsidy Limit: ₹3,800/- per acre
## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should be a farmer residing in the Chhattisgarh. 1. The applicant should be engaged in paddy cultivation. 1. The applicant should be willing to use a paddy transplanter machine for transplantation. 1. The applicant should be preparing a mat-type nursery for paddy transplantation. 1. The applicant should have suitable land for ploughing and weeding. 1. The applicant should have a cultivable area of up to 2 hectares to be eligible for the grant. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Offline **Step 1:** The interested applicant should visit (during office hours) the office of the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer and request the hard copy of the prescribed format of the application form from the concerned authority. **Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required). **Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents, within the prescribed period (if any), to the authority. **Step 4:** Request a receipt or acknowledgement from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, and a unique identification number (if applicable). **NOTE:** Ensure that the application is submitted within the prescribed period, if any.

metadata.schemeName: Male Pig Distribution Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: The "Male Pig Distribution Scheme", under the Animal Husbandry Department, Government of  Chhattisgarh, provides a grant to beneficiaries from the SC/ST category for purchasing one male pig of an improved breed (Middle White Yorkshire).

page_content:
# Male Pig Distribution Scheme

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Chhattisgarh | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** Animal, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Male Pig

## Description
The "Male Pig Distribution Scheme", implemented by the Animal Husbandry Department, Government of Chhattisgarh, provides financial assistance to beneficiaries from the Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) categories for purchasing one male pig of an improved breed (Middle White Yorkshire).
The beneficiary can purchase one breeding male pig of Middle White Yorkshire breed, aged 6 months to 1 year, from a government pig rearing project or locally.

## Benefits
90% of the unit cost (purchase price) or a maximum subsidy of ₹3,500/-, whichever is lower (for Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST)  category).

## Eligibility Criteria
1. The applicant should belong to the Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe category.
1. The applicant should be a resident of Chhattisgarh.
1. The beneficiary should purchase a male pig of the improved breed (Middle White Yorkshire).
1. The pig should be between the 6th months the 1st year of age.
1. The purchase should be made from a Government-rearing project or a local authorized source.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Offline
**Step 1:** The eligible beneficiary should fill out the prescribed application form, including mandatory details like bank account information, and submit it to the Gram Panchayat for recommendation.
**Step 2:** The recommended application should be sent to the Janpad Panchayat for approval and then forwarded to the District Panchayat (Agriculture Standing Committee) for final approval.
**Step 3:**  After approval, the District Officer should direct the selected beneficiary to purchase the breeding male pig from a government pig rearing center or locally.
**Step 4:** The purchase should be physically verified by the Sarpanch, Urban Councillor, local Veterinary Assistant Surgeon, and Assistant Veterinary Field Officer. The verified bill and Panchayat fee receipt (if applicable) should be submitted to the District Officer.
**Step 5:** Upon successful verification, the District Officer should transfer the prescribed grant amount to the beneficiary’s bank account and notify the beneficiary.

Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to fishers for purchasing refrigerated vehicles to maintain the freshness and quality of fish during post-harvest handling and transportation. ## Benefits **Financial Assistance provided under the scheme:** - Project Cost: ₹25,00,000/- per unit - Subsidy will be limited to 40% of the project cost for the General Category of beneficiaries. - Subsidy will be limited to 60% of the project cost for Weaker sections/Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe/Women and their co-operatives of beneficiaries. ## Eligibility Criteria 1. The applicant should ensure that the refrigerated vehicle remains operational for fish transportation. 1. The applicant will be eligible for a subsidy for the purchase of only one refrigerated vehicle. 1. The applicant should utilize the refrigerated vehicle solely for fishery-related transportation activities. 1. The Government of India and the Government of Haryana will not be responsible for any loss incurred in the purchase, operation, maintenance, and management of fish transport facilities. ## Exclusions

metadata.schemeName: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
metadata.briefDescription: The scheme "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" by the Women and Child Development Department, Haryana, aims to provide a cash incentive of ₹5,000/- during maternity to eligible pregnant and lactating women on the birth of a second child (boy).

page_content:
# Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Haryana | **Categories:** Women and Child | **Tags:** Women, Maternity Benefit, Lactating Mothers, Pregnancy Care, Child

## Description
Launched on 8th March, 2022, the scheme "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" by the Women and Child Development Department, Government of Haryana, aims to offer partial compensation for wage loss to promote adequate rest before and after childbirth, and to encourage health-seeking behaviour among pregnant and lactating women. This initiative particularly targets women delivering their second child (boy) and intends to promote institutional delivery and immunization adherence. The benefit of ₹5,000/- is disbursed through direct benefit transfer (DBT) into the beneficiaries’ accounts. The is provided after the fulfillment of specified conditions including child registration and first immunization cycle.

## Benefits
- **Monetary Benefit:** A cash incentive of ₹5,000/- is provided in one instalment after the birth of a second child (boy).

## Eligibility Criteria
> **The following are eligible to apply for the scheme:**


  - Women belonging to the Scheduled Castes(SC) and the Scheduled Tribes (ST).
  - Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan).
  - Women holding of BPL ration card.
  - Women beneficiaries under Pradhan Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana (PMJAY) under Ayushman Bharat.
  - Women holding E-shram card.
  - Women farmers who are beneficiaries under Kishan Samman Nidhi.
  - Women holding MGNREGA job card.
  - Women whose net family income is less than Rs. 8 lakh per annum.
  - Pregnant and Lactating AWWs/ AWHs/ ASHAs.
  - Any other category as may be prescribed by the Central Government.

> **Conditions for Disbursement:**


  - The child born on or after 08.03.2022 in any family in state of Haryana.
  - Child birth is registered.
  - Child has received first cycle of BCG, OPV, DPT and Hepatitis-B or its equivalent/substitute.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Online
> **Registration Process on Antyodaya-SARAL Portal:**

**Step 1:** Visit the Official Portal: [Antyodaya-SARAL Portal.](https://saralharyana.gov.in/)
**Step 2:** For registration, click on “New User/Register Here” and fill in all the mandatory details i.e. Name, Email ID, Mobile Number & password. Click on ‘Submit’.
**Step 3:** Verify the OTP received in the provided Email and Mobile Number. Alternatively, click on the Verification Link to activate the profile.
> **Login to Apply for the Scheme:**

**Step 1:** Visit the Official Portal: [Antyodaya-SARAL Portal.](https://saralharyana.gov.in/)
**Step 2:** The “Sign in here” option is available on the right side of the screen. Fill in the required credentials and click on the ‘Login’ button.
**Step 3:** In the opened window, click on “Scheme/Services list” and a list of schemes will appear on the screen.
**Step 4:** Now, select the scheme and click on “Apply for Service/Scheme”.
**Step 5:** Fill in all the details in the online application form and click on "Submit".
> **Track Your Service Online:**


  - **Track Application/Appeal:** [Click here](https://status.saralharyana.nic.in/).  - **Track Ticket:** [Click here](https://eticketing.saralharyana.nic.in/CitizenViewComplaints.aspx).
> **Track Your Service Through SMS:**


  - **Registered Mobile Number:** Type SARAL and send to 9954699899 to track your application.  - **Other Mobile Number:** Type SARAL<space><Application ID/Ticket No.> and send to 9954699899 to track your application/ticket.
> **Contact Us:**

 **Helpline:** 0172-3968400
**Email:** saral.haryana@gov.in

# Punjabi Language Scholarship Scheme **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Haryana | **Categories:** Education & Learning | **Tags:** Scholarship, Punjabi Language, Financial Support, Merit, Student | **Target Beneficiaries:** #N/A ## Description The scheme “Punjabi Language Scholarship Scheme” was introduced during the year 2005-2006 by the Department of Education, Government of Haryana under the Education Encouragement for Excellence (EEE) – Scholarships for High/Senior Secondary School Students. page_content:
# Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for Translation of Scholarly Works

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Gujarat | **Categories:** Sports & Culture | **Tags:** Book Translation Grant, Scholarly Works Support

## Description
The "Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for Translation of Scholarly Works" by the Sports, Youth and Cultural Activities Department, Government of Gujarat, promotes the translation of significant literary, cultural, and scholarly works to and from the Gujarati language to foster national integration and cross-cultural dialogue. The scheme is implemented by the Gujarat Sahitya Academy and offers financial support to individuals and institutions for translating original works from other Indian languages into Gujarati or vice versa. The scheme covers a wide range of genres, including novels, dramas, stories, essays, one-act plays, poetry, criticism, and research-based works.

## Benefits
> **Financial Assistance:**


- **For books up to 112 pages:** Up to ₹10,000/-.- **For books exceeding 112 pages:** Up to ₹15,000/-.
> **Printing Size Guidelines:**


- **For “Demy” size:** ₹2,300/- (paperback).- **For “Double Crown” size:** ₹2,500/- (paperback), ₹2,700/- (hardcover).
> **Note:** Reimbursement is capped at the lower of actual cost or ceiling.

## Eligibility Criteria
- An individual translator or a translation-handling institution is eligible under this scheme.
  - The translation must be from one Indian language into Gujarati, or from Gujarati into another Indian language.
  - The original author’s or publisher’s written permission for translation must be obtained and attached.
  - The manuscript must be unpublished and originally translated by the applicant.
  - Only one application per financial year is allowed.
  - Applicants who have received financial assistance five times or more under Sahitya Academy schemes are ineligible.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Online
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should visit the online [application form](https://gujaratsahityaacademy.com/user/yojana/add/MzM3NjIwNzU=) page.
**Step 2:** In the application form, provide all the mandatory details, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents.
**Step 3:** Click on the checkbox and verify the captcha.
**Step 4:** Click on the "Submit" button to complete the application process.

metadata.schemeName: Inter-state Border Areas Development Programme
metadata.briefDescription: The aims and objectives of the Inter-State Border Areas Development Programme ISBADP are to provide facilities for the socioeconomic development of the people living along the Inter-State boundary with Assam.

page_content:
# Inter-state Border Areas Development Programme

**Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Meghalaya | **Categories:** Social welfare & Empowerment | **Tags:** Meghalaya, Rural Development, Roads & Building, Inter-State Boundary, Social Welfare, Public Distribution, Civil Supplies

## Description
The aims and objectives of the Inter-State Border Areas Development Programme ISBADP are to provide facilities for the socioeconomic development of the people living along the Inter-State boundary with Assam. Projects taken up under this program are to ensure sustainability and provide value addition to any given product. As far as possible, a cluster approach is encouraged.
ISBADP covers the villages within 0-10 km crow fly distance from the Inter-State boundary with Assam. Those villages located 0-5 km to the Inter-State boundary get first priority.
ISBADP funds are ordinarily used to bridge critical gaps and meet the immediate needs of the people residing near the Inter-State boundary. Planning and implementation of ISBADP schemes is done on a participatory and decentralized basis through the Deputy Commissioners/ Line Departments/ Village Councils.
The implementation of the ISBADP is taken up through the concerned Deputy Commissioners who hold regular meetings with line departments of their respective districts such as Power, Rural Development, Roads & Buildings, Water Supply, Social Welfare, Public Distribution, Civil Supplies, etc. in order to ensure the implementation of the ISBADP schemes in the identified Inter-State border villages.

## Benefits
1. Infrastructure Development: The ISBADP may focus on improving infrastructure such as roads, bridges, railways, and connectivity in the border areas. This can enhance accessibility, trade, and transportation in these regions.
1. Socio-economic Development: The scheme may aim to uplift the socio-economic conditions of the border areas by implementing various development projects. It can include initiatives related to education, healthcare, skill development, employment generation, and poverty alleviation.
1. Border Security Enhancement: Development programs in border areas can contribute to strengthening border security. By improving infrastructure, communication networks, and surveillance systems, the scheme can enhance the overall security apparatus in these regions.
1. Tourism Promotion: The ISBADP might support the development of tourism infrastructure and attractions in the border areas to promote tourism. This can lead to increased tourist inflow, job creation, and economic growth in these regions.
1. Cultural Exchange and Integration: Development programs can foster cultural exchange and integration between border communities. The scheme may include initiatives to preserve and promote local culture, heritage, and traditional practices, fostering harmony and mutual understanding.
1. Environmental Conservation: The ISBADP may incorporate initiatives to protect and conserve the natural resources and environment of the border areas. This can include measures for forest conservation, wildlife protection, and sustainable development practices.

## Eligibility Criteria
1. The scheme is applicable to the residents of the state of Meghalaya living in remote and inaccessible areas situated near the international border.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Offline
1. The Directorate of Border Areas Development submits proposals to Border Areas Development Department, the Department then forwards the same to Planning and Finance Departments for approval and sanction.

page_content:
# Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme - Magel Tyala Shettale (Individual Farm Pond) **Level:** State | **States/UTs:** Maharashtra | **Categories:** Agriculture,Rural & Environment | **Tags:** MahaDBT, Individual Farm Pond, Magel Tyala Shettale, Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Krishi Yojana ## Description Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme-Magel Tyala Shettale (Individual Farm Pond) has been launched by Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, Dairy Development & Fishries Department, Maharashtra State in the year 2022-23 (vide G.R. Dated 29 th June, 2022) Under this scheme subsidy payable to individual farmer is minimum Rs.14433/- and maximum Rs.75000/- depending on the size of the farm pond.
Out of total area, 82 percent area of agriculture land in the state is rainfed and is dependent on rainfall. Water stress due to uneven distribution of rains and periodic interruptions in rains leads to large reduction in crop production. Sometimes crops are also destroyed. Farm ponds, in such situation plays an important role in providing protective irrigation and reduces crop losses substantially. Considering this matter, Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme-Individual Farm Pond has been sanctioned by the Maharashtra State Govt. vide G.R. Dated 29th June,2022. The scheme is implemented in all districts of the state. Under this scheme the subsidy payable to individual farmer is minimum Rs 14433/- and maximum Rs 75000/- depending on the size of the farm pond. Farmers should hold at least 0.20 ha land in Kokan region, while it is 0.40 ha limit for rest of the Maharashtra. Online applications are invited from farmers under Maha-DBT portal. The scheme is implemented by selecting the beneficiaries online through Maha-DBT portal. After completion of the farm pond, the subsidy payable under the scheme is credited through the PFMS system to theAadhaar number linked bank account of the farmer. The farm ponds are of two types one being with inlet outlet and the other without inlet and outlet type. The implementation of the component "Magel TyalaShettale" under Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme was approved videGovernment Circular dated April 25,2023. The name “Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Krishi Yojana" was given vide GR. dated 18th October 2023. ## Benefits 1) Financial Assistance is given to farmers. 2)The subsidy payable to an individual farmer minimum Rs.14433/- and maximum Rs.75000/- depending on the size of the farm pond. ## Eligibility Criteria 1) Farmer should hold at least (Minimum) 0.20 ha. land and Kokan region, while it is 0.40 ha. limit for rest of Maharashtra. 2) The applicant farmers land will have to be technically suitable for digging farm pond. So that the runoff rainwater can be stored in the farm pond through natural flow and recharge will be possible. In case of farm ponds without inlet and outlet there should be a natural source from where extra runoff during rainy season can be lifted and stored in farm pond. 3) Before applying for farm pond, the applicant farmers should not have availed the subsidy for farm pond, community tank or bodi in paddy bunding or any Government Scheme. ## Exclusions Farmers who have availed the subsidy for farm pond, community tank or bodi in paddy bunding under any Government Scheme previously is not eligible for subsidy again. ## How to Apply **Mode:** Online **Step 01:** Farmer Registration
**Step 02:** Select user type and complete Aadhar authentication.
**Step 03:** Profile completion (Mobile number, Address details, Land & land holding information)
**Step 04:** Apply for Individual Farm Pond (a) select scheme Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme (b) Select farm pond type (with inlet outlet or without inlet outlet) (c) Select farm pond size.

metadata.schemeName: Kisan Vikas Patra Scheme
metadata.briefDescription: ‘Kisan Vikas Patra Scheme’ was relaunched in the year 2014 by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry Of Finance, Government of India in view of the popular demand and to revitalize Small Savings. The amount invested in Kisan Vikas Patra (KYP) doubles in 115 months at the present rate.

page_content:
# Kisan Vikas Patra Scheme

**Ministry:** Ministry Of Finance | **Level:** Central | **States/UTs:** All | **Categories:** Banking,Financial Services and Insurance | **Tags:** Kisan, Investment, Savings, Certificate

## Description
The ‘Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP)’ is a certificate savings scheme that was launched by the Government of India on 1st April 1988. The scheme provided a facility of unlimited investment by way of purchase of certificates from post offices in various denominations. The maturity period of the scheme when launched was 5 ½ years and the money invested doubled on maturity.
       However, the scheme ‘Kisan Vikas Patra Scheme’ was relaunched in the year 2014 by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry Of Finance, Government of India in view of the popular demand and to revitalize Small Savings. The amountt invested in Kisan Vikas Patra (KYP) doubles in 115 months at the present rate. The certificates can be purchased by an adult for himself/herself or on behalf of a minor or to a minor. It can also be purchased jointly by two adults.
        A certificate may be transferred from one person to another with consent in writing to an officer of the Post Office or Bank. Under the scheme, the transferee has to be eligible to purchase the certificate. The certificate may be prematurely encashed any time after two years and a half from the date of purchase, in the event of the death of the holder or any holder in case of the joint holder, on the order of a court of Law and forfeiture by a pledge.
**Type of Certificates and issue thereof:** The Certificates shall be of the following types, namely:

  - **Single Holder Type Account:** This type of account may be opened by an adult for himself, or on behalf of a minor or a person of unsound mind of whom he is the guardian, or by a minor who has attained the age of ten years;   - **J****oint A- Type Account:** This type of account may be opened jointly in the names of upto three adults payable to all the account holders jointly or to the survivors;   - **Joint B-Type Account:** This type of account may be opened jointly in the name of upto three adults payable to any of the account holders or to the survivor or survivors

## Benefits
1. The scheme offers an interest rate of 7.5 % compounded annually on investment.
   1. Amount Invested doubles in 115 months (9 years & 7 months).
   1. No maximum deposit limit.
   1. Accounts can be opened in Post offices and in authorized banks.
   1. KVP can be transferred from one person to another and from one post office to another.
   1. KVP can be encashed after 2 and half years from the date of investment at the specified rates.

## Eligibility Criteria
1. Any individual who is a resident of India can avail of the benefits under the scheme.
   1. A parent/guardian may invest on behalf of a minor or person of unsound mind.
   1. The minimum age of minors should be 10 years.

> **Deposits:**


  - A minimum of ₹1000/- and any sum in multiples of ₹100/-, may be deposited in an account.
  - There shall be no maximum limit for deposits in an account or in accounts held by an account holder.
  - An individual may open any number of accounts.

> **Payment on maturity:**


  - The maturity period of an account opened between 12th December 2019 to 31st March 2020 (both days inclusive) shall be 9 years and five months. Deposit made in the account shall double on maturity and the amount of maturity may be repaid to the account holder.
  - The maturity period of an account opened on or after the first day of April 2020 shall be 10 years and four months. Deposit made in the account shall double on maturity.
  - The maturity period of the deposit under this Scheme shall be determined by the rate of interest applicable at the time of opening the account.

## How to Apply
**Mode:** Offline
> **Application process:**

**Step 01:** Any person or persons, desiring to purchase a Certificate, shall present an application either in person or through an authorized agent of the small savings schemes at a Post Office or Bank. The person may visit the nearest Post Office Branch or a designated bank.
**Step 02:** Collect the applicant form or [download](https://www.indiapost.gov.in/VAS/DOP_PDFFiles/Savings%20Bank/Kisan%20Vikas%20Patra%20Scheme%20%202019%20English.pdf) it from the [official website](https://www.indiapost.gov.in/VAS/Pages/Form.aspx#SavingCertificates).
**Step 03:** Fill out the application form and attach all the required documents.
**Step 04:** Fill out the declaration and nomination details.
**Step 05**: Submit the application form with an initial amount of investment/deposit.
**Step 06:** Upon processing your application, a KVP certificate is issued immediately. Keep the documents safe which will need at the time of maturity.
> **Procedure for payment:**

Payment for the purchase of a Certificate may be made to a Post Office or Bank in any of the following modes, namely:

  - by cash; or
  - by locally executed cheque, pay order, or demand draft drawn in favour of the Post Master; or
  - by presenting a duly signed withdrawal form or cheque together with the passbook for withdrawal from a Savings Account standing in a credit of the purchaser at the same Post Office or Bank.

> **Issue of Certificates:**


  - On payment being made, except where payment is made by a cheque, pay order, or demand draft, a Certificate shall be issued immediately and the date of such Certificate shall be the date of payment.
  - Where payment for the purchase of a Certificate is made by cheque, pay order, or demand draft, the Certificate shall not be issued before the proceeds of the cheque, pay order, or demand draft, as the case may be, are realized and the date of such Certificate shall be the date of encashment of the cheque, pay order or demand draft, as the case may be.
  - If, for any reason a Certificate cannot be issued immediately, a provisional receipt shall be given to the purchaser which may later be exchanged for a Certificate, and in such a case the date of the Certificate shall be the date of provisional receipt.

> **Premature closure of account:**

1. The account may be prematurely closed by the account holder by filling a specified application form to the accounts office, at any time before maturity under the following circumstances, namely:-
(a) on the death of the account holder in a single account, or any or all the account holders in a joint account;
(b) on forfeiture by a pledgee, being a Gazetted Officer;
(c) when ordered by a court.
2. On the closure of the account under sub-paragraph (1) of the scheme guideline, principal amount along with simple interest calculated at the rate applicable from time to time to Post Office Savings Account for the complete months for which the account has been held, shall be payable.
3. Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-paragraph (2) of the scheme guideline, if an account is closed any time after the expiry of two years and six months from the date of opening of the account, the amount, inclusive of interest shall be payable as per specified rate. 
> **Transfer of account:**

An account may be transferred from one individual to another, subject to the condition that the transferee is eligible to open an account under this Scheme, in the following cases, namely:-

   1. on the death of the account holder in case of a single account or on the death of all the account holders in a joint account, the amount shall be transferred to the legal heirs or the nominees, as the case may be;
   1. on the order of the court, the account shall be transferred from the account holder to the court or to any other individual as per the orders of the court;


  - on pledging, the account shall be transferred in accordance with paragraph 7 of the scheme guideline;
  - in the event of the death of any of the account holders in a joint account, the account shall be transferred in the name of the surviving account holder or account holder, as the case may be.

> **Payment on the death of the account holder:**


  - In the event of the death of the depositor of a single account or of all the depositors in a joint account, the deposit shall be payable to the nominee if a nomination exists or to the legal heir(s).
  - Where there are not more than three surviving nominees or legal heirs, they may, at their option continue the account and receive the amount of deposit along with interest on maturity in the manner provided for in this scheme, as if they had opened the account themselves.
  - Where the account is not continued under sub-paragraph (2) of the scheme guideline, it shall be closed and the amount of deposit along with interest as provided in paragraph 6 shall be repaid.
  - On the death of one or two of the account holders in a joint account, the surviving account holder or holders, if any, shall be treated as the owner or owners of the account and such account holder or holders may continue the account under sub-paragraph (2) of the scheme guideline or close the account under sub-paragraph (3) of the scheme guideline.
